china/china-space.4493c51167ac: Don’t mix up: Chang’e three landed on the near side, which faces Earth. The far side came next, with Chang’e four.
china/china-space.29b6664ebf46: The Tiangong space station was completed in twenty twenty-two. Its modules are…
china/china-space.6214bbf54933: Don’t mix up: Chang’e five did not carry astronauts. Robots collected the samples.
china/china-space.8b13120823c5: The far side never faces Earth. Queqiao, near the Earth-Moon L two point, sees both.
china/china-space.0b5b15c92e40: First landing ever on the far side; Yutu two rover. Needed the Queqiao relay.
china/china-space.53914f91f44b: Twenty twenty-two. The Tiangong space station is complete. Three modules — Tianhe in twenty twenty-one, Wentian in July twenty twenty-two, and Mengtian in October twenty twenty-two — joined in a T shape about four hundred kilometers up, or two hundred fifty miles up. In November twenty twenty-two two crews, six astronauts, met in orbit for the first time.
china/china-space.34d1fff9458e: Their longitudes are beyond ninety degrees east or west — outside the Earth-facing box.
china/china-space.a398fcffb0be: After Shenzhou five, China became the blank country to master crewed spaceflight on its own.
china/china-space.48a98526f50f: Don’t mix up: Dongfanghong one carried no people. China’s first astronaut flew thirty-three years later, in two thousand three.
china/china-space.fe1fb117e8be: Material beyond the textbook, extension: Queqiao’s halo orbit and line-of-sight geometry; the simplified physics of landing and docking, the docking game uses simplified Hill or Clohessy-Wiltshire equations with time times four; the landing game uses lunar gravity one point six two meters per second squared and a one thousand five hundred to seven thousand five hundred newton throttleable engine; Long March figures, approximate; launches per year, approximate; landing-site coordinates;
china/china-space.dd0ea39b77cf: Both ships race around Earth at seven point seven kilometers per second, seventeen thousand miles per hour — yet they must meet at a crawl, about zero point two meters per second, slower than a toddler walks. Tap the thrusters: each tap changes your speed a little. There are no brakes in space; to stop you fire the opposite way.
china/china-space.2edca5b1a8eb: The first four countries: the USSR, nineteen fifty-seven; the USA, nineteen fifty-eight; France, nineteen sixty-five; and Japan, February nineteen seventy.
china/china-space.d6d937a0c5f3: Tiangong, Chang’e four, Shenzhou five, Dongfanghong one
china/china-space.bc43a0682757: Famous jobs: Chang’e five and six, Tianwen one. Five B version — the Tiangong modules
china/china-space.d6691997ab1c: Mission one: build the “Magpie Bridge” — why a relay?
china/china-space.d4bb3a4629aa: Memory hook: Orbit, land, return — 绕, 落, 回.
china/china-space.fc6aaca8f87c: Your mission: fly from China’s first satellite in nineteen seventy to today. Build the “Magpie Bridge” relay, soft-land on the far side, dock a Shenzhou with the Tiangong space station, and pick the right Long March rocket for each job. Collect all twelve stars to rise from Cadet to Chief Designer!
china/china-space.715698dc281c: China’s first rocket, the Long March one, was about thirty meters tall — a ten-storey building.
china/china-space.21cc7009615c: Keys: throttle, side jets. Safe landing: is less than or equal to three meters per second on flat ground.
china/china-space.81d1c2b50109: lesson numbers differ slightly between printings, and links to the new-era lesson in Unit three. The English is written for US middle-schoolers new to the topic, with pinyin and meanings for key names.
china/china-space.eb332f206bb2: Two thousand three. Shenzhou five: Yang Liwei, China’s first astronaut. Yang Liwei, 杨利伟, circled Earth fourteen times in about twenty-one hours. China became the third country — after the USSR and the USA — to send a person into space on its own rocket.
china/china-space.75379810a67e: Bars: orbital launch attempts from China per year, approximate, including a few failures. Source: compiled public launch logs, for example Gunter’s Space Page, J. McDowell’s launch log; twenty twenty-two to twenty twenty-five cross-checked with news reports. The few launches of nineteen seventy to nineteen ninety-nine are not drawn.
china/china-space.8198af0d5622: Twenty thirteen. Chang’e three lands; the Yutu rover rolls off. Chang’e three made the first soft landing on the Moon by any country since nineteen seventy-six, in the Bay of Rainbows region on the near side. It released Yutu, 玉兔, the “Jade Rabbit” who lives with Chang’e in the legend.
china/china-space.43b5485c465d: The Moon always shows Earth the same face. So how do you talk to a robot parked on the far side — where Earth is never in the sky? In twenty nineteen China became the first country to pull it off.
china/china-space.3d213d293d16: Twenty twenty-five. Tianwen two heads for an asteroid. On the twenty-ninth of May, twenty twenty-five, a Long March three B launched Tianwen two to collect samples from a small near-Earth asteroid, Kamoʻoalewa. That year China launched about ninety-two rockets — a record. Next goal: Chinese astronauts on the Moon before twenty thirty.
china/china-space.f425f2b535ab: Two thousand seven. Chang’e one orbits the Moon. The lunar programme is named after Chang’e, 嫦娥, the Moon goddess of Chinese legend. Its plan has three steps: orbit, 绕, land, 落, return, 回. Chang’e one did step one and mapped the whole Moon.
china/china-space.af4ee6cdf682: Shenzhou five, Dongfanghong one, Tiangong, Chang’e four
china/china-space.d932f0b5989f: Nineteen ninety-nine. Shenzhou one: a test flight with no crew. China’s crewed spaceflight programme, started in nineteen ninety-two, flew its first spacecraft. Shenzhou, 神舟, means “divine vessel”. Four uncrewed test flights came before anyone climbed aboard.
china/china-space.03de04b7c586: In two thousand three Yang Liwei became China’s first astronaut. Which spacecraft did he fly?
china/china-space.8e94309bdbfd: Shenzhou one to four were uncrewed tests; Shenzhou seven made the first spacewalk.
china/china-space.205afcebe0df: Mission timeline: nineteen seventy to today
china/china-space.0408752007b4: Twenty twenty. Chang’e five brings the Moon home. The giant Long March five sent Chang’e five from Wenchang on Hainan Island. It landed in the Ocean of Storms, drilled and scooped one thousand seven hundred thirty-one grams of rock and soil, or three point eight pounds, launched back into lunar orbit, and returned to Earth on the seventeenth of December — completing “orbit, land, return”.
china/china-space.fea499163320: Twenty twenty-one. Tianwen one lands the Zhurong rover on Mars. Tianwen one, 天问, “Questions to Heaven”, after an ancient poem, did three jobs on its first try: orbit Mars, land, and drive a rover. Zhurong, 祝融, is named after the god of fire. China became the second country to drive a rover on Mars, after the USA.
china/china-space.f21233f383d0: Memory hook: two F carries people. Three B goes high — BeiDou, early Chang’e. Five is the heavy “Fat Five.” Seven feeds the station.
china/china-space.275bdd6b5f43: China’s heavy-lifter: its core is five meters wide, sixteen feet, as wide as a two-lane road. Launched from Hainan, near the sea, because it is too big to move by train.
china/china-space.99a424c71a94: Don’t mix up: Chang’e is a robot programme. No Chinese astronaut has walked on the Moon yet; that goal is set for before twenty thirty.
china/china-space.8330be9dbfb8: Nineteen seventy. Dongfanghong one: China’s first satellite. A Long March one rocket lifted the one hundred seventy-three kilogram satellite — about three hundred eighty pounds — from Jiuquan in the Gobi Desert. From orbit it played the song “The East Is Red”, 东方红, back to Earth. China became the fifth country to launch its own satellite.
china/china-space.83467910a458: Memory hook: Five went and came back: one thousand seven hundred thirty-one grams.
china/china-space.69c619254628: Read the map: All six Apollo landings are inside the near-side box: astronauts needed to radio Earth directly. Two of China’s four landings are on the far side.
china/china-space.3f96bf635ffa: In twenty twenty Chang’e five brought back one thousand seven hundred thirty-one grams of samples. This completed which step?
china/china-space.190327abf1bc: Twenty twelve. Shenzhou nine: the first hand-flown docking. In twenty eleven China launched a small space lab, Tiangong one, 天宫, “Heavenly Palace”, and the uncrewed Shenzhou eight docked with it automatically. In June twenty twelve astronaut Liu Wang flew Shenzhou nine in by hand. On board was Liu Yang, China’s first woman in space.
china/china-space.2d0003863ffb: Mission three: dock Shenzhou with Tiangong
china/china-space.42e3810b7855: In twenty twenty-one, which spacecraft landed the Zhurong rover on Mars?
china/china-space.3547a4e0d288: Two thousand eight. Shenzhou seven: China’s first spacewalk. Zhai Zhigang, 翟志刚, opened the hatch and stepped out into space, waving a Chinese flag. He wore a spacesuit made in China called Feitian, 飞天, “flying to the heavens”.
china/china-space.7ae1243ce6ae: Mission four: pick the right rocket
china/china-space.f7b31441add3: Chang’e six and Tianwen two, twenty twenty-four to twenty twenty-five, newer than some printings.
china/china-space.bcb62aa640ee: About sixty-five thousand kilometers beyond the Moon, about forty thousand miles, lies the Earth-Moon L two point, a Lagrange point. There the pulls of Earth and Moon work together so a satellite can circle Earth in step with the Moon, using very little fuel. Queqiao doesn’t sit right on L two. Launched May twenty eighteen, it flies a big loop around it — a “halo orbit” — so the Moon never blocks its view of Earth.
china/china-space.b19524f36522: Keys: speed up, slow down, up and down. To dock: closing speed zero point zero five to zero point three meters per second. Up-or-down miss is less than or equal to zero point five meters.
china/china-space.c7b9f8833f8b: Chang’e four, Shenzhou five, Dongfanghong one, Tiangong
china/china-space.8f61a3f30cde: Twenty twenty-four. Chang’e six: samples from the far side. Relaying through the new Queqiao two satellite, Chang’e six landed in Apollo crater on the far side, collected one thousand nine hundred thirty-five point three grams of samples, and came home on the twenty-fifth of June — the first far-side samples in history.
china/china-space.03d9176a2850: Don’t mix up: Tiangong one was a small test lab, not the big Tiangong space station of twenty twenty-two.
china/china-space.9aa410c3569f: You’re flying a Chang’e lander one thousand eight hundred meters above the surface, five thousand nine hundred feet, falling at forty-five meters per second, one hundred miles per hour. The Moon has no air, so parachutes are useless — only your braking engine can slow you. Throttle up, hover near one hundred meters, dodge the boulders and set down gently on flat ground.
china/china-space.b63fe82444b7: Don’t mix up: Chang’e five samples are from the near side; Chang’e six samples are from the far side.
china/china-space.8ac98d63dbce: It was part of “Two Bombs, One Satellite”, 两弹一星: the atomic bomb, nineteen sixty-four; the hydrogen bomb, nineteen sixty-seven; and this satellite.
china/china-space.b6c6e48e3c40: Suggested use: one, run the timeline and have students order Dongfanghong one, Shenzhou five, Chang’e one to six, Tianwen one, Tiangong, and tell the four programmes apart, Shenzhou, Tiangong, Chang’e, Tianwen; two, in Mission one, ask students to explain why the far side needs a relay — then why Queqiao doesn’t sit exactly on L two; three, read the Moon map: why are all Apollo sites on the near side?
china/china-space.f6954d522111: Chang’e four needed the Queqiao satellite mainly because…
china/china-space.a4f6d1a11650: In orbit, higher means slower to go round. Fire upward, away from Earth, and you climb to a slightly higher orbit — so you slowly fall behind the station. Fire downward and you creep ahead. This game uses simplified Hill equations, also called Clohessy-Wiltshire, for that effect and runs time four times faster. The real Shenzhou plans each burn with computers and a ground team.
china/china-space.70073c35c1b9: Radio travels in straight lines, like light — it can’t go through the Moon. Slide the lander round to the far side and watch the signal. Then drag the Queqiao relay satellite, 鹊桥, “Magpie Bridge”, to a spot that can “see” both Earth and the lander.
china/china-space.208726a6745d: Dongfanghong one played “The East Is Red” from orbit.
china/china-space.06248eb0c510: Don’t mix up: Shenzhou seven was the spacewalk mission; docking came later, with Shenzhou eight and nine.
china/china-space.de9f24e7584d: In nineteen seventy China launched its first man-made satellite. It was called…
china/china-space.eb101750a407: “Two Bombs, One Satellite” or 两弹一星 refers to…
china/china-space.0a38d903464c: China’s rockets are named Long March after the Red Army’s famous march of the nineteen thirties; in Chinese, 长征. These are drawn to the same scale, simplified shapes, approximate numbers. Click a rocket for its card; switch on the comparisons to stand them next to America’s Saturn Five and the Statue of Liberty.
china/china-space.bec35e66d2e2: A Long March one rocket lifted the one hundred seventy-three kilogram satellite, three hundred eighty pounds, from Jiuquan in the Gobi Desert. From orbit it played the song “The East Is Red” back to Earth; in Chinese, 东方红. China became the fifth country to launch its own satellite.
china/china-space.2696e6ede982: Twenty nineteen. Chang’e four: first-ever landing on the far side. Nobody had ever landed on the far side, because you can’t radio Earth from there. First China parked the Queqiao relay satellite beyond the Moon, May twenty eighteen. Then Chang’e four landed in Von Kármán crater and sent out the Yutu two rover.
china/china-space.8b538725ab3e: Memory hook: Nineteen seventy: the East is Red — and so is the sky.
china/china-space.35e6b8609980: This lesson follows China’s national History Curriculum Standard for Compulsory Education, twenty twenty-two edition, strand “Contemporary Chinese History — achievements in science and culture”, matching the unified-edition textbook Chinese History, Grade eight, Volume two, Unit six lesson on science and culture achievements, “Two Bombs, One Satellite”, crewed spaceflight, lunar exploration;
china/china-space.6ded7a72c441: Latitude forty-five point four degrees south, longitude one hundred seventy-seven point six degrees east

china/china-space.88d193c46b0e: Don’t mix up: Third country to fly people into space — not the first. And Shenzhou five did not go to the Moon.

china/chinese-spirit.918658fb65f3: Tu led a team that discovered artemisinin, a compound used to treat malaria. She received half of the twenty fifteen Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

china/chinese-spirit.9998d7049190: In nineteen fifty-eight he took on classified work. He could no longer tell even his family where he was going for work.
china/chinese-spirit.04cda3fb6982: Chien-Shiung Wu. Wu grew up in China and worked as a physicist in the U.S. She and her collaborators showed that one kind of radioactive decay behaves differently from its mirror image. They cooled cobalt sixty and used a magnetic field to line up its nuclear spins. More electrons came out in the direction opposite to the spins.
china/chinese-spirit.817ebe2bac80: Zhan led construction of the railway from Beijing to Zhangjiakou. It opened in nineteen oh nine.
china/chinese-spirit.e591b81686af: Yuan Longping in a frame from a China News Service video
china/chinese-spirit.5bc875302d28: Tu Youyou. Tu led a team that discovered artemisinin, a compound used to treat malaria. She received half of the twenty fifteen Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. A fourth-century medical text by Ge Hong described soaking sweet wormwood. That gave Tu’s team an idea: try extracting substances from the plant at a lower temperature.
china/chinese-spirit.ee8dd4c61dfe: Nineteen fifty-seven. Chien-Shiung Wu. Wu and her collaborators publish their experimental results.
china/chinese-spirit.8ad0a6d139cf: Nineteen sixty. Red Flag Canal workers. Work begins on the Red Flag Canal in Lin County.
china/chinese-spirit.45f99497cce2: The Red Flag Canal story connects to the theme of responsibility in the twenty twenty-two Compulsory Education Morality and Rule of Law Curriculum Standards. Consider how public works can meet a community need. Ministry of Education guide
china/chinese-spirit.47a11bab4e6c: Yuan Longping. Yuan and other researchers bred high-yield hybrid rice by crossing different lines of rice. In nineteen sixty-four, he examined clusters of rice flowers with a magnifying glass. He found a male-sterile plant. It made no pollen that could fertilize an egg, but pollen from another line could help it set seed.
china/chinese-spirit.42a15f79dc54: Twenty fifteen. Tu Youyou. Tu shares the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
china/chinese-spirit.a48beb7b40bd: In the nineteen fifties, she sent staff to the Soviet Union to learn how to examine cells for signs of disease. After they returned, her team began screening for cervical cancer.
china/chinese-spirit.329ac58a2924: They cooled cobalt sixty and used a magnetic field to line up its nuclear spins. More electrons came out in the direction opposite to the spins.
china/chinese-spirit.0a29c18aec27: Qian returned in nineteen fifty-five. Construction started in nineteen sixty, Yuan’s find was in nineteen sixty-four, and the prize was in twenty fifteen.
china/chinese-spirit.50db994129eb: Jiaxian Road in Shenzhen, named for Deng Jiaxian
china/chinese-spirit.e5e7ac5e05f5: Nineteen sixty-nine. Red Flag Canal workers. The full Red Flag Canal network, including its branch channels, is completed.
china/chinese-spirit.b86324c0b3e0: What made the rice plant Yuan found in nineteen sixty-four useful for crossbreeding?
china/chinese-spirit.e2781c3bcfc1: Qian Xuesen. Qian worked with Caltech’s early rocketry team and later helped build China’s rocket and space programs. U.S. authorities barred him from leaving for several years. Once the ban was lifted in nineteen fifty-five, he and his family left Los Angeles by ship for China.
china/chinese-spirit.c023bfa65609: Nineteen sixty-five. Red Flag Canal workers. Water begins flowing through the Red Flag Canal’s main channel.
china/chinese-spirit.24348324c1f5: Zhan Tianyou. Zhan led construction of the railway from Beijing to Zhangjiakou. It opened in nineteen oh nine. At Qinglongqiao, he laid out a switchback. Trains could take a longer route up the mountain by reversing direction on the tracks.
china/chinese-spirit.2c49142c65cc: Tu shared the twenty fifteen Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discoveries concerning malaria therapy.
china/chinese-spirit.ca51d520fca2: Nineteen fifty-eight. Deng Jiaxian. Deng takes on classified research.
china/chinese-spirit.1440f9ef8e5d: Deng Jiaxian. Deng led teams in China’s early nuclear weapons program. Yang Zhenning later wrote about him in the essay “Deng Jiaxian.” In nineteen fifty-eight he took on classified work. He could no longer tell even his family where he was going for work.
china/chinese-spirit.456036058abb: Nineteen fifty-five. Qian Xuesen. After the U.S. travel ban is lifted, Qian returns to China.
china/chinese-spirit.acf377ba63a7: Nineteen thirty. Wen Yiduo. Wen takes a teaching post in Qingdao, where he studies Tang poetry.

china/climate-rivers.06a294c8b574: The Qinling-Huaihe Line is China’s most important natural boundary, 秦岭—淮河: a mountain range plus a river. The zero degrees Celsius January line and the eight hundred millimeters yearly rainfall line both run roughly along it, thirty-two degrees Fahrenheit and thirty-one inches, respectively. Read each card, then click the side of the map where it belongs.
china/climate-rivers.99ace8fc69f0: The eight hundred millimeter rainfall line separates which two regions?
china/climate-rivers.d252b419fce6: Supports the twenty twenty-two Compulsory-Education Geography Curriculum Standard, “Understanding China”: use maps and data to describe the main features of China’s climate and how they affect life and work; describe the main features of the Yangtze and the Yellow River and their influence on society and the economy. Textbook: Grade eight, Volume one, Chapter two, The Natural Environment of China, Section two, Climate, and Section three, Rivers.
china/climate-rivers.2818ea1e64a4: China is about the size of the USA and spans nearly fifty degrees of latitude, about twice as many as Maine to Florida. Switch layers, drag the month slider, and click the map to investigate.
china/climate-rivers.933bb6744aac: Which mountain range is NOT on the monsoon and non-monsoon boundary?
china/climate-rivers.7d257ce97dfa: Eight hundred millimeters: humid and semi-humid. Four hundred millimeters: semi-humid and semi-arid. Two hundred millimeters: semi-arid and arid.

china/division-integration.2378f3178588: The Western Jin briefly reunited China; it lasted from two sixty-six to three sixteen. After it fell, the Eastern Jin held only the south; it lasted from three seventeen to four twenty.

china/division-integration.f353e0e234d2: Northern Wei later split into Eastern and Western Wei, replaced by Northern Qi and Northern Zhou. china/division-integration.832e43409f32: Five thirty-four: Northern Wei breaks into an eastern and a western half, later called Northern Qi and Northern Zhou. china/division-integration.cd7aedd56235: Four twenty to five eighty-nine: one line of dynasties ruled the north and another ruled the south, facing each other across the Huai and Yangtze rivers. For one hundred seventy years there were, in effect, two Chinas side by side.

After the Han dynasty collapsed, China split into rival kingdoms from about two hundred to five eighty-nine C E. The Roman Empire was breaking up in the very same centuries. Rome never came back together; China did.
china/division-integration.04cf07081065: Each kingdom developed: Wei built irrigation and military farms, and the northern economy recovered; Zhuge Liang governed Shu and developed the southwest; in two hundred thirty Wu sent Wei Wen with a fleet to Yizhou, today’s Taiwan, strengthening links between the mainland and Taiwan.

china/dynasties.01420de8d495: six hundred forty-one: Princess Wencheng, 文成公主, travelled to Tibet to marry the Tubo king Songtsen Gampo, 松赞干布.

china/dynasties.eec027915aa4: Republic of China, nineteen twelve to nineteen forty-nine. Nineteen twelve to nineteen forty-nine. Nineteen twelve: no more emperors. On the first of January, nineteen twelve, the Republic of China was founded in Nanjing, with Sun Yat-sen as provisional president. The nineteen eleven Revolution, 辛亥革命, overthrew Qing and ended over two thousand years of rule by emperors. The period was full of struggle: warlords, the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression from nineteen thirty-one to nineteen forty-five, and civil war.
china/dynasties.05cfd883c9ff: Qing took its name in sixteen thirty-six and entered Beijing in sixteen forty-four; the slider counts from sixteen forty-four. Maps are schematic, traced roughly from textbook maps.
china/dynasties.c8bd1a0de1d0: Xia. Circa twenty seventy to sixteen hundred B C E. Father to son: the first hereditary throne. When Yu’s son Qi inherited the throne, “all under heaven” became one family’s business. That rule — the throne stays in the family — lasted four thousand years. Around twenty seventy B C E Yu founded Xia — the textbook’s first dynasty. Before Xia, leaders were chosen by merit, “abdication”, 禅让. After Yu, his son Qi took the throne, and power stayed in the family.
china/dynasties.3f95bbecf0a0: In Sichuan, merchants began using jiaozi, 交子, the world’s earliest paper money.

china/dynasties.603f22089ffc: General Yue Fei, 岳飞, won big victories against Jin. Meanwhile the south grew richer than the north — by Southern Song, China’s economic centre had moved south for good.

After a war, Song and Liao made peace: Song paid silver and silk each year, and the two sides traded peacefully for over one hundred years. Bi Sheng, 毕昇, invented movable-type printing. In Sichuan, merchants began using jiaozi, 交子, the world’s earliest paper money.

china/dynasties.d2f92d4f8fd5: Yuan. Twelve seventy-one to thirteen sixty-eight. The province system, 行省制度. Yuan divided its huge empire into provinces, 行省. Yuan took Lin’an in twelve seventy-six and finished off the last Song resistance in twelve seventy-nine. The Xuanzheng Yuan, 宣政院, governed Tibet; a Penghu inspectorate, 澎湖巡检司, managed Penghu and Liuqiu, today’s Taiwan.
china/dynasties.7d8038dc9dbc: Cai Lun, 蔡伦, made paper from bark, hemp, rags and old fishing nets — cheap and light. Paper became one of China’s Four Great Inventions.

china/dynasties.2ce88da7b823: Western Zhou. Ten forty-six to seven hundred seventy-one B C E. The enfeoffment system, 分封制. The Zhou king gave land and people to relatives and heroes, making them lords, 诸侯, who guarded the realm and sent tribute — a bit like medieval Europe’s lords and vassals. In ten forty-six B C E King Wu beat the Shang army at the Battle of Muye, 牧野之战. In seven hundred seventy-one B C E the Quanrong, 犬戎, captured Haojing and Western Zhou ended.

china/dynasties.8cf3c199abec: Western Han. Two hundred two B C E to eight C E. Zhang Qian opens the Silk Road. In one hundred thirty-eight B C E Zhang Qian, 张骞, set off west — and was captured for over ten years before getting home. His trips opened the Silk Road, linking Chang’an to Central Asia and on towards Rome. Emperor Wu, 汉武帝, made Han strongest and made Confucianism the official teaching, 罢黜百家, 尊崇儒术. In sixty B C E Han set up the Protector-General of the Western Regions, 西域都护 — today’s Xinjiang came under the central government from then on.
china/dynasties.4cdc9f02a3e7: Tang. Six hundred eighteen to nine hundred seven. A golden age: Chang’an, world city. Under Emperor Taizong, the “Zhenguan reign”, and Emperor Xuanzong, the “Kaiyuan golden age”, Chang’an held about a million people — merchants, monks and students from across Asia. Six hundred forty-one: Princess Wencheng, 文成公主, travelled to Tibet to marry the Tubo king Songtsen Gampo, 松赞干布. Seven hundred fifty-five: the An-Shi Rebellion, 安史之乱, began — the turning point from glory to decline.

china/dynasties.d10b031caa58: People’s Republic of China, nineteen forty-nine onward. Nineteen forty-nine to today. Nineteen forty-nine: New China. Emperor Yongle moved the capital to Beijing in fourteen twenty-one and built the Forbidden City. Ming rebuilt the Great Wall in brick and stone, from the Yalu River to Jiayu Pass.
china/dynasties.a5f1d6e7b260: Eastern Zhou. Seven hundred seventy to two hundred fifty-six B C E, Spring and Autumn seven hundred seventy to four hundred seventy-six, Warring States four hundred seventy-five to two hundred twenty-one. Seven states, a hundred schools of thought. War pushed change: iron tools, new laws, and thinkers like Confucius, Mozi, Laozi and Han Fei arguing about how to run a country — the “Hundred Schools of Thought”. Spring and Autumn, seven hundred seventy to four hundred seventy-six B C E: strong lords competed to be “hegemon”. Confucius, 孔子, taught. Warring States, four hundred seventy-five to two hundred twenty-one B C E: seven big states. Shang Yang’s reforms, 商鞅变法, made Qin the strongest; Li Bing, 李冰, built the Dujiangyan irrigation system.

china/dynasties.71f1bd5b64e0: Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms. Nine hundred seven to nine hundred sixty, Five Dynasties. Five dynasties in fifty-three years. The north changed hands five times while about ten smaller kingdoms ruled the south. The south saw less war, so its farms and towns kept growing. In the north, Later Liang, Later Tang, Later Jin, Later Han and Later Zhou followed one another in just fifty-three years. Jin conquered Wu in two hundred eighty and ended sixty years of division. It lasted about thirty-five years before the north broke apart again. In two hundred sixty-six Sima Yan took the throne from Wei and founded Jin. The unity was short: princes fought each other, rebellions broke out, and Western Jin fell in three hundred sixteen.

Eleven forty-two: Song and Jin made peace, with a border along the Huai River and Dasan Pass, 大散关. “When Suzhou and Huzhou have a good harvest, the whole country has enough”, 苏湖熟, 天下足.

china/dynasties.7fd25a9e66af: Sui. Five hundred eighty-one to six hundred eighteen. The Grand Canal and the imperial exams. Five hundred eighty-nine: Sui conquered Chen and reunited China after almost three hundred years of division. The Grand Canal ran two thousand plus kilometers from Zhuojun, today’s Beijing, to Yuhang, today’s Hangzhou, centred on Luoyang — one thousand two hundred forty plus miles, about New York to Miami.

china/dynasties.da3cf036bfa7: Northern and Southern Dynasties. Four hundred twenty to five hundred eighty-nine. Emperor Xiaowen’s reforms. In four hundred ninety-four Emperor Xiaowen of Northern Wei, a Xianbei 鲜卑 ruler, moved his capital to Luoyang and had his court adopt Han clothes, language and surnames — a big step in the blending of peoples. The south had four dynasties in a row — Song, Qi, Liang, Chen — all ruling from Jiankang. Zu Chongzhi, 祖冲之, calculated pi to between three point one four one five nine two six and three point one four one five nine two seven — the world’s best for about one thousand years.

china/dynasties.b181cb92da14: Eastern Han. Twenty-five to two hundred twenty. Cai Lun improves paper, one hundred five C E. Cai Lun, 蔡伦, made paper from bark, hemp, rags and old fishing nets — cheap and light. Paper became one of China’s Four Great Inventions. Zhang Heng, 张衡, built a seismoscope, 地动仪, that showed the direction of distant earthquakes. Ban Chao, 班超, restored Han control in the Western Regions; Buddhism arrived from India.

china/dynasties.6713ef2d2a6f: Qin. Two hundred twenty-one to two hundred seven B C E. Two hundred twenty-one B C E: China is unified. Qin conquered the other six states in ten years and created China’s first unified, centralised state ruled by an emperor. Qin itself lasted only fifteen years — but its systems lasted two thousand. He called himself the “First Emperor”, 始皇帝, and ran the country through commanderies and counties, 郡县制, led by officials he appointed. One script, small seal 小篆, one round coin with a square hole, one set of weights and measures — and the Great Wall joined up.

china/early-civilization.4fea711629dd: In Yuanmou, Yunnan, scientists found early humans from about one point seven million years ago: Yuanmou Man, the earliest early humans so far confirmed in China.
china/early-civilization.6e5542f673eb: About one point seven million years ago people live at Yuanmou in Yunnan. All we have are two front teeth and some stone tools — but that is enough to prove they were here.
china/early-civilization.5cbc0c4cce06: Memory rhyme: Yuanmou’s first at one point seven million; Peking Man had fire and chipped stone; Upper Cave sewed with bone needles; Hemudu, today in Yuyao, Zhejiang: rice and stilt house; Banpo, today in Xi’an: millet and half-sunk house.
china/early-civilization.8779ab32f0d8: Meanwhile, elsewhere: There is not one human being in North or South America — and there will not be for more than one point six million years.

china/early-civilization.3ed13b3215e5: About four thousand to five thousand years ago, the Yan and Yellow Emperor tribes of the Yellow River valley allied, defeated Chiyou at Zhuolu, and gradually formed the Huaxia people. The two are honoured as the first ancestors of Chinese civilization.
china/early-civilization.5e4a1a185d4a: The earliest humans confirmed in China, about one point seven million years ago. Named after Yuanmou county in Yunnan, in the far southwest.
china/early-civilization.6a8850dadfad: About ten thousand years ago people in China begin to plant seeds instead of only gathering them: rice in the warm, wet south and millet in the dry north. China is one of the first places on Earth to grow both.
china/early-civilization.ae08a11f0834: At Zhoukoudian near Beijing lived Peking Man, about seven hundred thousand to two hundred thousand years ago. They made chipped stone tools, used natural fire and lived in groups.
china/early-civilization.1307075f5bc3: Common mix-up: Hemudu is OLDER than Banpo, about seven thousand years ago versus about six thousand years ago.
china/early-civilization.dd189ab5eeb4: About five thousand three hundred to four thousand three hundred years ago Liangzhu has a walled city, huge earth dams and finely carved jade. A few people are now much richer and more powerful than the rest: an early state is forming. Legend places the Yellow Emperor and the Yan Emperor in about this age.
china/early-civilization.5ad7729b007b: From about seven hundred thousand to two hundred thousand years ago, people live in caves at Zhoukoudian near today’s Beijing. They chip stone tools, hunt and gather in groups, and — the big step — use fire and keep it alive.
china/early-civilization.69a08943cec2: About seven thousand years ago villagers at Hemudu, near the east coast, grow rice, dig with spades made of bone, and build wooden houses on posts with joints that fit together without nails.
china/early-civilization.39dbb016706d: Zoom in on the last few thousand years: Hemudu, Banpo, the legendary age of the Yan and Yellow Emperors, then Yao, Shun and Yu, about twenty seventy B C E, Yu founds the Xia dynasty.
china/early-civilization.65cce40d8b20: Nobody could write yet — so how do we know who lived in China one point seven million years ago? From teeth, bones, burnt seeds and broken pots. Walk into two rebuilt Stone Age villages, then drag a time slider from the first known humans in China to the first farmers and the first walled towns — most of it long before the pyramids were finished.
china/early-civilization.8b7dbe8f9b38: Meanwhile, elsewhere: Egypt’s Great Pyramid has been standing for about two hundred fifty years. Cities with brick houses and drains line the Indus River in today’s Pakistan.
china/early-civilization.1fafebb5c688: Yuanmou Man, Yunnan, about one point seven million years ago.
china/early-civilization.9b86dc8d89a2: In a cave at the top of the same hill lived Upper Cave Man, about thirty thousand years ago. They looked like modern people and sewed clothes with bone needles.

They reached Europe through Arab traders, centuries before there was a United States.
china/inventions.bb98d5c42e90: Making a sheet of paper. Pulp, screen, dry, peel. one, Soak and cut the raw materials. two, Pound them into pulp. three, Dip a bamboo screen into the pulp vat and lift out a thin wet layer. four, Press and dry the sheets. five, Peel off the finished paper. Paper replaced heavy bamboo slips and expensive silk as the main writing material. Papermaking later spread to Korea, Japan and the Arab world, and then to Europe through the Arabs. Drag the Papermaking slider through steps one to five!

china/megaprojects.95f9fa8b772a: Much of China’s natural gas is in the west — for example under the Tarim Basin in Xinjiang. But most gas is used in the crowded, factory-filled east. The first West-East Gas Pipeline runs about four thousand kilometers from Lunnan in the Tarim Basin to Shanghai, about two thousand five hundred miles — almost coast to coast across the USA. In Chinese it is 西气东输, “send western gas east”. It went into full operation in two thousand four.

china/megaprojects.6b21703c036d: A thermosyphon is a sealed steel pipe. Its Chinese name is 热棒, “heat rod.” The bottom is buried in the permafrost, the finned top sticks up into the air, and inside is liquid ammonia. In winter the ground is warmer than the air, so the ammonia boils at the bottom, the vapour rises, gives off its heat at the fins, condenses and trickles back down. In summer the air is warmer, so the cycle simply stops.
china/megaprojects.93dc61326462: In the middle of the sea, the road has to switch from bridge to tunnel, from above the water to below the seabed. Each island — about one hundred thousand square meters, like fourteen football fields — is the switching station. To build them, workers drove one hundred twenty giant steel cylinders, each twenty-two meters across, seventy-two feet, into the seabed to form the walls, then filled them with sand.

The main line ends at Guangzhou; branch lines reach Shanghai, Hong Kong and other cities. Designed to carry about thirty billion cubic meters of gas a year. Later third and fourth lines were added; the Turpan-Zhongwei section of the fourth line, about one thousand seven hundred forty-five kilometers, went into service in June twenty twenty-five.
china/megaprojects.36f525b68231: About five hundred fifty kilometers of the line sits on permafrost — ground that stays frozen all year and is full of ice. Only the top layer thaws in summer. This top layer is the “active layer”. If the embankment lets heat into the ground, the ice melts, the soil turns to mush and sinks, and the rails bend. Drag the years, switch the engineering tricks on and off, and compare.

china/megaprojects.57fba82d1907: Zhuhai Link Road. Part of this road runs in a tunnel under the busy Gongbei district of Zhuhai. Zhuhai is a Special Economic Zone in Guangdong Province, next door to Macao. The fifty-five-kilometer total counts this link road and the Hong Kong one too.
china/megaprojects.57039ed1603a: West artificial island. About one hundred thousand square meters — roughly fourteen football fields. Its walls are giant steel cylinders driven into the seabed and filled with sand. The road slopes down here into the tunnel.
china/megaprojects.6e7de79c6e22: Zhuhai-Macao Port island. An island built in the sea for the border-check halls of Zhuhai and Macao. china/megaprojects.66cab4cb05b5: Main bridge, twenty-two point nine kilometers. Most of the bridge is long, low steel-box spans on concrete piers — cheap to build where only small boats pass. Three taller cable-stayed bridges leave gaps for ships. Their towers are shaped like a sail, Jiuzhou, dolphins, Jianghai, and a Chinese knot, Qingzhou. The bridge used about four hundred twenty thousand tonnes of steel — often compared to sixty Eiffel Towers. It is designed to last one hundred twenty years and to stand up to strong typhoons and earthquakes.
china/megaprojects.8fc034f44a92: The Qinghai-Tibet Railway runs one thousand nine hundred fifty-six kilometers from Xining in Qinghai to Lhasa in Tibet, Xizang — a distance of one thousand two hundred fifteen miles. In Chinese, the railway is 青藏铁路. Its Golmud-Lhasa section opened on July first, two thousand six. It is the world’s highest plateau railway; its top, the Tanggula Pass, is five thousand seventy-two meters high, sixteen thousand six hundred forty feet — higher than any mountain in the lower forty-eight US states. In Chinese, the pass is 唐古拉山口. Ride it first!
china/megaprojects.b77df58e5a39: The tunnel is about six point seven kilometers long; its immersed-tube part, about five point seven kilometers, was the longest immersed road tunnel in the world when built.
china/megaprojects.bef87b199701: Undersea tunnel, six point seven kilometers. The tunnel is about six point seven kilometers long; its immersed-tube part, about five point seven kilometers, was the longest immersed road tunnel in the world when built. Thirty-three concrete sections, each one hundred eighty meters long and about eighty thousand tonnes, were sunk into a trench and joined underwater. The deepest point is more than forty meters below the sea surface. Above you, the biggest ships in the world can sail by — and no tower gets in the airport’s way.

The Treaty of Nerchinsk of sixteen eighty-nine confirmed in law that the Heilongjiang and Ussuri basins, including Sakhalin, were Chinese territory.
china/ming-qing.349a9e538da1: fourteen thirty-three, The seventh and last voyage ends
china/ming-qing.db71b465b96f: A dynasty is a line of rulers from one family. The Ming emperors, the Zhu family, ruled China for two hundred seventy-six years. Ming means “bright”. When it began, Europe was still in the Middle Ages.

china/ming-qing.2e74f71f2c14: two, Unit three, lessons such as “Ming rule”, “Ming foreign relations”, “Ming science, architecture and literature”, “Consolidating the unified multi-ethnic state”, “Stronger Qing autocracy”.
china/ming-qing.9815d48448b7: Kangxi had defeated Galdan, leader of the Dzungars, 准噶尔, a Mongol group; Qianlong put down later Dzungar and Khoja rebellions. He now creates the General of Ili to govern all of Xinjiang as far as Lake Balkhash. The title is 伊犁将军. The Qing now rules more than thirteen million square kilometers, five million square miles, a bigger area than today’s United States.
china/ming-qing.1e0a9173b6d3: Common mix-up: Zheng He’s first voyage in fourteen oh five was eighty-seven years before Columbus in fourteen ninety-two: “more than half a century earlier than the European navigators”.
china/ming-qing.799cd22a42f1: For decades wokou raided China’s southeast coast. The wokou, 倭寇, were pirates based in Japan. General Qi Jiguang and his well-drilled “Qi family army” beat them nine times out of nine at Taizhou. The general’s Chinese name is 戚继光. By fifteen sixty-five the threat is basically over.
china/ming-qing.700c7b0b1967: British warships arrive off the coast and the Opium War begins. China’s modern history starts here: see the next lesson, Modern China eighteen forty to nineteen nineteen.
china/ming-qing.a322e3388a77: Dutch colonists had occupied Taiwan since sixteen twenty-four. Zheng Chenggong crosses the strait with his fleet in sixteen sixty-one. His Chinese name is 郑成功, and he is known in the West as Koxinga. In sixteen sixty-two the Dutch surrender and Taiwan returns to China.
china/ming-qing.8ec2aa319395: In seventeen sixty-two the Qianlong Emperor set up an official to govern Xinjiang. It was…
china/ming-qing.f8b7be1ca826: Sent by the Yongle Emperor, Zheng He leaves Liujiagang with more than twenty thousand men and dozens of big ships. Liujiagang is near today’s Shanghai. By fourteen oh seven the fleet has sailed to Calicut in India and come home.
china/ming-qing.2cd5c8d16911: Qing forces enter Taiwan in sixteen eighty-three. The next year the government sets up Taiwan Prefecture under Fujian Province, tightening its administration of the island. The prefecture’s Chinese name is 台湾府.
china/ming-qing.cd7e22b3ee23: In fourteen oh five a fleet with more than twenty thousand sailors left China — eighty-seven years before Columbus crossed the Atlantic, and on far bigger ships. Where did they go? And what happened to China over the next four hundred years? Sail the route yourself, build the emperors’ palace in three D, then drag the year slider from thirteen sixty-eight to eighteen forty and watch two dynasties, the Ming and the Qing, shape the China on today’s map.
china/ming-qing.93152a9dfbc4: fourteen seventeen, Fifth voyage: the east coast of Africa

china/ming-qing.c45a252b1ee4: Ming and Qing, to eighteen forty: a unified multi-ethnic state grows stronger
china/ming-qing.9a61afc16df2: The emperors’ palace in the middle of Beijing; “forbidden” because ordinary people could not enter. It covers about seventy-two hectares, one hundred seventy-eight acres, roughly one hundred thirty-five American football fields.
china/ming-qing.e2ba0fd2a97b: Gifts and trade goods. Porcelain and silk went out; spices came back. The fleet brought porcelain, fine “china” dishes, silk, tea and copper coins as gifts and for trade. It brought back spices, jewels, medicines and rare animals. It visited more than thirty countries and regions in Asia and Africa and strengthened China’s friendly ties with them. Peaceful voyages: gifts and trade, not conquest.
china/ming-qing.8c705be1af5b: For US classrooms: the English is written for students with no background in Chinese history. Chinese terms carry pinyin and a meaning on first use, with “meanwhile in the world” anchors and miles or feet next to metric units. The anchors are Columbus in fourteen ninety-two, the Mayflower in sixteen twenty, and the Declaration of Independence in seventeen seventy-six.
china/ming-qing.f7996323467f: On the fifth voyage ships reach Aden in Arabia, then Mogadishu and Malindi on the east coast of Africa. The voyage lasted from fourteen seventeen to fourteen nineteen.
china/ming-qing.48adfe70dc6d: The Qing had already granted titles to the Dalai Lama and the Panchen Lama, Tibet’s two leading Buddhist figures, in sixteen fifty-three and seventeen thirteen respectively. Now the Yongzheng Emperor posts a Grand Minister Resident in Tibet to manage Tibetan affairs with them on behalf of the central government. The title is 驻藏大臣.
china/ming-qing.60e0d6ba4d2f: Curriculum: twenty twenty-two Compulsory Education History Standards, ancient China, “Ming and Qing, before the Opium War”, in outline: stronger autocracy; Ming foreign relations, Zheng He, Qi Jiguang; consolidation of the unified multi-ethnic state, Taiwan, Yaksa, the Dzungars, Tibet; the closed-door policy; architecture such as the Forbidden City. Textbook: unified-edition Chinese History, Grade seven Volume.
china/ming-qing.0e2c20bd9c51: On the last voyage some of the crew reach Mecca near the Red Sea. The voyage lasted from fourteen thirty-one to fourteen thirty-three. The Chinese name for Mecca is 天方. In twenty-eight years: seven voyages to more than thirty countries and regions in Asia and Africa. After this, the great fleets stop.

china/ming-qing.df540dfa0444: Zhu Yuanzhang, 朱元璋, born a poor farmer’s son, becomes emperor at Yingtian, today: Nanjing, today’s Nanjing. The same year his army takes Dadu, today: Beijing, today’s Beijing, ending the rule of the Mongol-led Yuan dynasty.
china/ming-qing.5f82c016eba3: The ports on the map have no names. Tap the port named as the “next stop” to sail from Liujiagang all the way to the east coast of Africa and the Red Sea coast: roughly six thousand to seven thousand miles one way, about ten thousand kilometers, about twice the distance from New York to London. china/ming-qing.0d15cf5e4355: Between fourteen oh five and fourteen thirty-three, how many times did Zheng He sail to the Western Oceans?
china/ming-qing.23a8fcb50153: Chinese emperors are usually called by the name of their reign. Yongle of the Ming sent Zheng He to sea and built the Forbidden City. Yongle, 永乐, ruled from fourteen oh two to fourteen twenty-four. Kangxi, Yongzheng and Qianlong of the Qing secured the borders. Kangxi, 康熙, ruled from sixteen sixty-one to seventeen twenty-two. Yongzheng, 雍正, ruled from seventeen twenty-two to seventeen thirty-five, and Qianlong, 乾隆, from seventeen thirty-five to seventeen ninety-six. George Washington was US president during Qianlong’s last years.
china/ming-qing.f6cb78777c5e: Southwest: the Qing granted titles to the Dalai Lama, sixteen fifty-three, and the Panchen Lama, seventeen thirteen; in seventeen twenty-seven Yongzheng set up the Grand Minister Resident in Tibet; Qianlong created the golden urn lottery for choosing reincarnations. By the mid-eighteenth century the Qing held a vast, unified territory.
china/ming-qing.cef058eadcc8: Compass and star-sighting. Advanced navigation technology. The navigators followed compass bearings recorded as “needle routes”. At night they measured the height of stars with sighting boards, 牵星板, to work out how far north or south they were. Advanced shipbuilding and navigation were key conditions for the voyages. Compass by day and night, stars to find the place.
china/ming-qing.6ecbcdddb2cf: To strengthen ties with overseas countries, the Yongle Emperor sent Zheng He to the “Western Oceans”. In fourteen oh five the great fleet left Liujiagang. From fourteen oh five to fourteen thirty-three he made seven voyages.
china/ming-qing.1894d7420585: Built under the Yongle Emperor of the Ming: planned from fourteen oh six and basically finished in fourteen twenty; the capital moved to Beijing in fourteen twenty-one. That is seventy-two years before Columbus sailed.
china/ming-qing.6b38edd02bd7: fourteen twenty-one, The capital moves to Beijing
china/ming-qing.d56ebcc0415c: The Forbidden City. Built under the Yongle Emperor of the Ming: planned from fourteen oh six and basically finished in fourteen twenty; the capital moved to Beijing in fourteen twenty-one. That is seventy-two years before Columbus sailed. The palace of twenty-four Ming and Qing emperors; today the Palace Museum. The largest and best-preserved ancient palace complex in the world, World Heritage, nineteen eighty-seven: about seventy-two hectares, one hundred seventy-eight acres, roughly one hundred thirty-five football fields.
china/ming-qing.6ca480fd22dd: seventeen seventy-one, The Torghuts come home
china/ming-qing.615f6445d367: The Yongle Emperor moves the capital north from Nanjing to Beijing. The Forbidden City, planned from fourteen oh six and finished in fourteen twenty, becomes the palace of twenty-four Ming and Qing emperors.
china/ming-qing.9cbe0eae7de4: seventeen fifty-seven, Only one port stays open
china/ming-qing.235b6e53d7c5: Zhu Yuanzhang, 朱元璋, born a poor farmer’s son, becomes emperor at Yingtian, today’s Nanjing. The same year his army takes Dadu, today’s Beijing, ending the rule of the Mongol-led Yuan dynasty.
china/ming-qing.f782d2c2c396: sixteen forty-four, The Ming falls; the Qing takes Beijing
china/ming-qing.00e85aba1be3: The Torghut Mongols had moved to the Volga River in Russia more than a century earlier. Led by Ubashi, 渥巴锡, they trek thousands of miles back to China.
china/ming-qing.a87170b6215b: Northwest: Kangxi defeated Galdan of the Dzungars; Qianlong put down the Dzungar rebellion and the revolt of the Greater and Lesser Khojas, and in seventeen sixty-two set up the General of Ili to govern Xinjiang. In seventeen seventy-one the Torghut Mongols returned from the Volga.
china/ming-qing.195055950b4b: The Protectorate of the Western Regions was a Western Han office, sixty B C.
china/ming-qing.cd5178122ac9: three, after the map, have students sort Qing measures by region: southeast, northeast, northwest, southwest.
china/ming-qing.529eadf4cb2d: The palace of twenty-four Ming and Qing emperors; today the Palace Museum.
china/ming-qing.7b04a5240d96: Treasure ship. Flagship of the Ming fleet. From fourteen oh five to fourteen thirty-three Zheng He, 郑和, led a fleet to the “Western Oceans”, the seas west of the South China Sea, seven times. The History of Ming records that the largest treasure ships were forty-four zhang long and eighteen zhang wide — a zhang 丈 is an old unit of about ten feet — which would make them longer than a football field. Historians still debate the exact size, but they were among the largest wooden ships of the age. Columbus’s flagship in fourteen ninety-two was only about sixty feet long, or nineteen meters. The fleet carried more than twenty thousand people, as many as a small town, and set out from Liujiagang, in Taicang, Jiangsu Province, near today’s Shanghai. Zheng He: fourteen oh five to fourteen thirty-three, seven voyages, thirty plus countries, farthest to East Africa and the Red Sea.
china/ming-qing.3dd0faf23eff: Common mix-up: “nine thousand nine hundred ninety-nine and a half rooms” is only a folk legend; the Palace Museum counts over nine thousand rooms.
china/ming-qing.442b9b54b006: The largest and best-preserved ancient palace complex in the world, World Heritage, nineteen eighty-seven: about seventy-two hectares, one hundred seventy-eight acres, roughly one hundred thirty-five football fields.

china/ming-qing.69bb915af326: The Qianlong Emperor allows foreign trade only at Guangzhou, Canton, and only through licensed merchant houses called the Thirteen Hongs, 十三行. This is the closed-door policy. It gave some protection against Western colonisers, but it cut China off just as Europe’s Industrial Revolution was starting.

china/ming-qing.39ad288f74c3: Russian forces had pushed into the Heilongjiang region. The Heilongjiang is the Amur River. After Qing troops beat them twice at Yaksa, sixteen eighty-five to sixteen eighty-six, China and Russia negotiate as equals. china/ming-qing.325ae163db00: In sixteen sixty-two, who drove out the Dutch colonists and recovered Taiwan?
china/ming-qing.be0ff3e2f44c: Zheng He visited more than thirty countries and regions in Asia and Africa. The voyages strengthened China’s friendly exchange with them. They were a feat in world navigation, more than half a century earlier than the European voyages.
china/ming-qing.56891c6197d5: Year slider: drag from thirteen sixty-eight to eighteen forty
china/ming-qing.ac081ca103a4: A peasant army led by Li Zicheng captures Beijing and the Ming dynasty ends. Li Zicheng’s Chinese name is 李自成. Soon the Qing army, Manchus from the northeast, comes through the Great Wall at Shanhai Pass and makes Beijing its capital.
china/ming-qing.60bc2a91bb11: China’s last dynasty, founded by the Manchu people from the northeast. “Qing” sounds like “ching”. This lesson stops in eighteen forty, just before the Opium War.
china/ming-qing.22a56c7cff73: fourteen thirteen, Fourth voyage: on to the Persian Gulf
china/ming-qing.4fe4e80d196c: Now to the Qing, map of China. In sixteen sixty-two Zheng Chenggong drove out the Dutch colonists and recovered Taiwan. In sixteen eighty-four the Qing set up Taiwan Prefecture under Fujian Province. Earlier, in the Ming, Qi Jiguang had defeated the pirates on the southeast coast.
china/ming-qing.de2290ce2f3a: The emperor abolishes the chancellor, 丞相, a kind of prime minister. The six ministries now report straight to him, and a secret police, the Jinyiwei, watches officials. The Jinyiwei’s Chinese name is 锦衣卫. All power sits with one man.

china/modern-china.5c943cea6514: Opium War and Treaty of Nanjing. Eighteen forty to eighteen forty-two. The beginning of China’s modern history. June eighteen thirty-nine: the official Lin Zexu, 林则徐, destroyed confiscated opium on the beach at Humen, 虎门, near Guangzhou — a heavy blow to opium smuggling. June eighteen forty: using the Humen opium destruction as an excuse, Britain launched the Opium War. August eighteen forty-two: the Qing government was forced to sign the Treaty of Nanjing: cede Hong Kong Island to Britain; pay twenty-one million silver dollars; open Guangzhou, Xiamen, Fuzhou, Ningbo and Shanghai as treaty ports; tariffs on British goods had to be agreed with Britain. Impact: China began to sink into a semi-colonial, semi-feudal society. The Opium War marks the start of China’s modern history.
china/modern-china.d9538b325c02: three D staircase: the search for a way to save China
china/modern-china.7c3c5654ce2b: The Boxers rose against foreign powers under the slogan "Support the Qing, wipe out the foreigners"; the Boxers were called 义和团 in Chinese.
china/modern-china.ea132a01bd10: Which magazine marked the start of the New Culture Movement in nineteen fifteen?
china/modern-china.1272f2e5fad5: Overthrew more than two thousand years of autocratic monarchy
china/modern-china.7c69c0b7853e: Memory rhyme: Petition, eighteen ninety-five, Hundred Days, eighteen ninety-eight, coup. The Imperial University survived, forerunner of Peking University.
china/modern-china.fe6963c5a81b: Memory rhyme: Land, Liaodong, Taiwan, Penghu, money, two hundred million taels, ports, Shashi, Chongqing, Suzhou, Hangzhou, factories.
china/modern-china.f3b09606795b: The Taiping army fought its way north to the Yangtze River, captured Nanjing and made it the capital, renamed Tianjing — today, Nanjing — with Tianjing meaning “Heavenly Capital”. It announced a plan to share farmland equally. The kingdom lasted until eighteen sixty-four.
china/modern-china.3bb11a02289a: Lin Zexu, 林则徐: the official who destroyed the opium. Hong Xiuquan, 洪秀全: leader of the Taiping uprising. Li Hongzhang, 李鸿章: official who built factories and a navy. Empress Dowager Cixi, 慈禧: the real ruler of the late Qing. Kang Youwei, 康有为: leader of the eighteen ninety-eight reform. Sun Yat-sen, 孙中山: leader of the nineteen eleven Revolution. Chen Duxiu, 陈独秀: founder of New Youth magazine.
china/modern-china.8dcdd86b0ed3: Summary. Step by step, progressive Chinese learned from the West ever more deeply: technology, institutions, ideas. Each attempt failed to save China on its own — the search continued into nineteen nineteen. Try the three D staircase next!
china/modern-china.914a3400f55f: Nineteen hundred: Britain, the USA, Russia, Japan, France, Germany, Italy and Austria formed an allied army, took Tianjin and Beijing.
china/modern-china.5a08b65e2ba9: Drag the year slider, eighteen thirty-nine to nineteen nineteen. Each unequal treaty adds new treaty ports to the map; the diamonds are moments when Chinese people fought back or tried something new. Click a port or a marker for details. The card on the right tells you what happened that year, and what was going on in the United States at the same time. The map is schematic.
china/modern-china.c0d4a12ee322: Watch out: The New Culture Movement began in nineteen fifteen; the May Fourth Movement happened in nineteen nineteen. The first prepared the minds for the second — they are not the same event.
china/modern-china.a2835be1ef39: Memory rhyme: Wuchang rises in nineteen eleven; the Republic is born on January first, nineteen twelve.
china/modern-china.7c7346b13137: Eight-Nation Alliance and Boxer Protocol. Nineteen hundred to nineteen oh one. China became a fully semi-colonial, semi-feudal society. The Boxers, 义和团, rose against foreign powers under the slogan “Support the Qing, wipe out the foreigners”. Nineteen hundred: Britain, the USA, Russia, Japan, France, Germany, Italy and Austria formed an allied army, took Tianjin and Beijing. Nineteen oh one Boxer Protocol: pay four hundred fifty million taels of silver, guaranteed by customs and other taxes; the Legation Quarter at Dongjiaominxiang with foreign guards and no Chinese residents; destroy the Dagu forts and let foreign troops be stationed along the Beijing-Shanhaiguan railway; strictly forbid anti-imperialist activities. Impact: the Qing became a “court of the foreigners”; China completely sank into a semi-colonial, semi-feudal society.
china/modern-china.d3c600918ac1: Eighteen ninety-eight, The Hundred Days’ Reform. Kang Youwei and Liang Qichao persuaded Emperor Guangxu to reform. After one hundred three days, Empress Dowager Cixi staged a coup — but the reform enlightened people’s minds. This was learning institutions.
china/modern-china.b025ad939fe4: An indemnity is money the loser of a war is forced to pay the winner. China paid in silver, weighed in taels: one tael is about thirty-seven grams, or one point three ounces. In Chinese, a tael is 两.
china/modern-china.051f2f20e77f: Textbook: national unified edition, Chinese History, Grade eight Volume one, Units one to four, Lessons one to twelve.
china/modern-china.f9d0fbdc5ef5: Eighteen sixties to eighteen nineties, The Self-Strengthening Movement. To “self-strengthen”, officials built arsenals, Anqing, Jiangnan, Fuzhou; to “seek wealth”, they built civilian companies, and created the Beiyang Fleet.
china/modern-china.db600e9e0260: Watch out: The Republic of China was founded on January first, nineteen twelve, in Nanjing, not in nineteen eleven. The revolution did not change China’s semi-colonial, semi-feudal nature.
china/modern-china.a7336c38ac20: Nineteen hundred to nineteen oh one, The Eight-Nation Alliance. Allied armies took Tianjin and Beijing. The Boxer Protocol demanded four hundred fifty million taels, a legation quarter and foreign troops — China completely became a semi-colonial, semi-feudal society.
china/modern-china.ed85dc4d909c: Meanwhile in the US and the world: The US wanted the same deal: in eighteen forty-four it got China to sign the Treaty of Wangxia, 望厦条约, which gave Americans the same trading privileges.
china/modern-china.1dd5e7df3521: From eighteen forty China began to become a semi-colonial, semi-feudal society.
china/modern-china.ee76d89d1e8c: “Semi-colonial”: China still had its own government, but foreign powers controlled much of its trade, taxes and territory. “Semi-feudal”: the old system of emperor and landlords was still in place. This is how China’s textbooks describe the country between eighteen forty and nineteen forty-nine.
china/modern-china.a1eeb96fc3ed: Suggestion: play the animated map first and ask students to notice how treaty ports spread from the coast up the Yangtze and from south to north. Then use the three D staircase to build the “technology, institutions, ideas” logic, and discuss why each attempt failed and what it left behind. The treaty game works well as a class competition.
china/modern-china.285f7590b6f2: Eighteen ninety-four to eighteen ninety-five, The Sino-Japanese War. The Beiyang Fleet was destroyed. The Treaty of Shimonoseki ceded the Liaodong Peninsula, Taiwan and Penghu, cost two hundred million taels and opened four more ports — greatly deepening China’s semi-colonial status.
china/modern-china.b2e4edef262b: The Boxer Protocol, nineteen oh one
china/modern-china.562973ab6f82: Watch out: The Eight-Nation Alliance invaded in nineteen hundred; the Boxer Protocol was signed in nineteen oh one.
china/modern-china.e05bdcb5dbc3: Watch out: The Old Summer Palace was burned by the Anglo-French army in eighteen sixty, not by the Eight-Nation Alliance in nineteen hundred.
china/modern-china.b4a02fef11e0: Meanwhile in the US and the world: The California Gold Rush was on. Thousands of Chinese sailed to California, which they called “Gold Mountain”, 金山.
china/modern-china.bfce236fc29b: New Culture Movement. From nineteen fifteen. A movement that liberated people’s thinking. Nineteen fifteen: Chen Duxiu, 陈独秀, founded Youth Magazine in Shanghai, renamed New Youth, 新青年, from Volume two, launching the movement. Leaders: Chen Duxiu, Li Dazhao, Lu Xun, Hu Shi and others; Peking University became one of its centres. Content: promote democracy, oppose autocracy; promote science, oppose ignorance; promote new morality, oppose old morality; promote new literature, oppose old literature. Hu Shi wrote “Suggestions for the Reform of Literature”; Lu Xun published the first vernacular short story, “A Madman’s Diary”. Later, Li Dazhao and others spread Marxism; the movement freed people’s minds and prepared the ground for Marxism in China.
china/modern-china.a4e100c11f03: Which achievement of the Hundred Days’ Reform survived the eighteen ninety-eight coup?
china/modern-china.7e6e14cad1dd: Supports the “Modern and Contemporary Chinese History” strand of the twenty twenty-two national compulsory-education history curriculum standard, modern period: foreign aggression and the unequal treaties; China gradually becoming a semi-colonial, semi-feudal society; the Taiping movement, the Self-Strengthening Movement, the Hundred Days’ Reform, the nineteen eleven Revolution and the New Culture Movement.
china/modern-china.ec8e7fa7acd6: Meanwhile in the US and the world: The United States had only twenty-six states. Texas and California were not yet part of it.
china/modern-china.4b8a50af2c38: Nineteen eleven to nineteen twelve, The nineteen eleven Revolution. On October tenth, nineteen eleven, the Wuchang Uprising broke out. On January first, nineteen twelve, Sun Yat-sen became Provisional President in Nanjing — the Republic of China was born and the monarchy ended.
china/modern-china.add32873f67c: In eighteen fifty-three the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom made which city its capital, renaming it Tianjing?
china/modern-china.7526cdbff94d: Animated lesson: China, eighteen forty to nineteen nineteen
china/modern-china.0d7975467c54: Nineteen fifteen, The New Culture Movement. Chen Duxiu founded Youth Magazine, later New Youth, in Shanghai; the movement centred on Peking University. Its banners: democracy and science. Learning now reached the level of ideas.
china/modern-china.6ad7f5aa2212: Nineteen eleven Revolution. Nineteen eleven to nineteen twelve. Overthrew the autocratic monarchy. Sun Yat-sen, 孙中山, founded the Revive China Society in eighteen ninety-four and the Tongmenghui, 同盟会, the “Revolutionary Alliance”, in Tokyo in nineteen oh five, whose programme — expel the Manchu rulers, restore China, found a republic, equalise land rights — became the Three Principles of the People, nationalism, democracy, people’s livelihood. October tenth, nineteen eleven: the Wuchang Uprising broke out and province after province responded. January first, nineteen twelve: Sun Yat-sen took office in Nanjing as Provisional President — the Republic of China was founded. The Qing emperor abdicated in February. March nineteen twelve: the Provisional Constitution of the Republic of China — the first law in Chinese history with the nature of a bourgeois-republican constitution. Significance: it ended more than two thousand years of autocratic monarchy and spread the idea of a democratic republic — but Yuan Shikai seized the fruits of the revolution.
china/modern-china.5ac03ef1a96e: June eighteen forty: using the Humen opium destruction as an excuse, Britain launched the Opium War.
china/modern-china.bd4ae94d423a: A port city that a treaty forced China to open, where foreigners could live and trade. Before eighteen forty-two foreign ships were allowed to trade at only one port, Guangzhou, once spelled “Canton”.
china/modern-china.8867da4dc5c7: Pay two hundred million taels of silver
china/modern-china.3e16fd1b2660: Taiping Heavenly Kingdom. Eighteen fifty-one to eighteen sixty-four. The peak of China’s old-style peasant wars. Eighteen fifty-one: Hong Xiuquan, 洪秀全, launched the Jintian Uprising in Guiping, Guangxi, and founded the “Taiping Heavenly Kingdom”, 太平天国, “Heavenly Kingdom of Great Peace”. Eighteen fifty-three: the Taiping army took Nanjing, renamed it Tianjing, 天京, “Heavenly Capital”, and made it the capital; it issued the Heavenly Land System, a plan to share out farmland equally. Eighteen fifty-nine: Hong Rengan put forward A New Work for Aid in Administration, the first fairly systematic plan in modern China for developing capitalism. After the Tianjing Incident in eighteen fifty-six, it declined; Tianjing fell in eighteen sixty-four and the movement failed. Significance: it dealt heavy blows to Qing rule and to foreign aggressors.
china/modern-china.1e4d90894769: Big idea: Two threads run through eighteen forty to nineteen nineteen: foreign aggression made China semi-colonial, and the Chinese people kept fighting back and searching for a way out.
china/modern-china.76ba00836a83: Eighteen fifty-one to eighteen sixty-four, The Taiping Heavenly Kingdom. Hong Xiuquan rose at Jintian, Guangxi, eighteen fifty-one. The Taipings fought north and in eighteen fifty-three made Nanjing their capital, Tianjing. Crushed by Chinese and foreign forces, it fell in eighteen sixty-four.
china/modern-china.11ec222dadaf: Britain and France wanted even more of China’s market. Backed by Russia and the United States, they attacked again in eighteen fifty-six.
china/modern-china.3359eb273ebf: The greatest achievement of the nineteen eleven Revolution was that it…
china/modern-china.5e624b5138ae: Eighteen fifty-six to eighteen sixty, The Second Opium War. The Treaty of Tianjin opened ten more ports, deep up the Yangtze; the Convention of Peking added Tianjin and ceded Kowloon. Anglo-French troops burned the Old Summer Palace.
china/modern-china.46d04893220f: Meanwhile in the US and the world: In the eighteen forties American families were heading west in covered wagons along the Oregon Trail.
china/modern-china.f5bb0caacb93: June eighteen thirty-nine: the official Lin Zexu destroyed confiscated opium on the beach at Humen, 虎门, near Guangzhou — a heavy blow to opium smuggling. Lin Zexu’s Chinese name is 林则徐.
china/modern-china.a7f2e2584443: British traders were smuggling opium, an addictive drug, into China and draining away its silver. The emperor sent the official Lin Zexu to stop it. Lin Zexu’s Chinese name is 林则徐. In June eighteen thirty-nine he had the confiscated opium — more than one point one million kilograms, about two point four million pounds — destroyed in public on the beach at Humen.
china/modern-china.12b989025cc3: Common mix-up: The Treaty of Nanjing ceded Hong Kong Island; the Kowloon area was ceded to Britain by the Convention of Peking. Nanjing’s indemnity was twenty-one million silver dollars, while Shimonoseki and the Boxer Protocol counted in taels of silver.
china/modern-china.6b20de9cf051: Second Opium War. Eighteen fifty-six to eighteen sixty. Anglo-French forces burned the Old Summer Palace. Supported by Russia and the USA, Britain and France launched the Second Opium War to open China’s market further. Eighteen fifty-eight Treaty of Tianjin: foreign envoys to live in Beijing; ten more ports including Hankou and Nanjing; foreign merchant ships and warships free to sail the Yangtze ports. Eighteen sixty: the Anglo-French army took Beijing, looted and burned the Old Summer Palace, 圆明园, the emperors’ garden palace. Convention of Peking: Tianjin opened as a port; the Kowloon area ceded to Britain. Taking advantage of the war, Tsarist Russia seized more than one point five million square kilometers of Chinese territory in the northeast and northwest. Impact: China’s semi-colonial status deepened further.
china/modern-china.5a1f2eec207e: Eighteen forty-two, Treaty of Nanjing, China’s first unequal treaty: cede Hong Kong Island, pay twenty-one million silver dollars, open five treaty ports — Guangzhou, Xiamen, Fuzhou, Ningbo, Shanghai — and accept “agreed tariffs”.
china/modern-china.df18ef4925f5: Using the destruction of the opium as its excuse, Britain sent a fleet to attack China. Its real aim was to open China’s market to British factory goods. China’s textbooks count eighteen forty as the start of the country’s modern history.
china/modern-china.65031c01417b: The Treaty of Nanjing, eighteen forty-two
china/modern-china.3f5300b629c6: The Old Summer Palace, also called Yuanmingyuan, was looted and burned in eighteen sixty by…
china/modern-china.7fce918bec3e: Self-Strengthening Movement. Eighteen sixties to eighteen nineties. Learning Western technology: “self-strengthening”, 自强, and “seeking wealth”, 求富. Leaders: Prince Gong, Yixin, at court; Zeng Guofan, Li Hongzhang, Zuo Zongtang and Zhang Zhidong in the provinces. Guiding idea: “Chinese learning as the foundation, Western learning for practical use.” Early stage, slogan “self-strengthening”: military industries such as the Anqing Arsenal, the Jiangnan Arsenal and the Fuzhou Navy Yard. Later stage, slogan “seeking wealth”: civilian industries such as the China Merchants Steam Navigation Company and the Hanyang Iron Works; also new navies such as the Beiyang Fleet, new-style schools and students sent abroad. The Beiyang Fleet’s total defeat in the Sino-Japanese War marked its failure, but it brought in Western technology and China’s first modern enterprises — it is seen as the start of China’s modernisation.
china/modern-china.d5036bd8af6c: Nineteen oh one Boxer Protocol: pay four hundred fifty million taels of silver, guaranteed by customs and other taxes; the Legation Quarter at Dongjiaominxiang with foreign guards and no Chinese residents; destroy the Dagu forts and let foreign troops be stationed along the Beijing to Shanhaiguan railway; strictly forbid anti-imperialist activities.
china/modern-china.de9493f626df: Hundred Days’ Reform. Eighteen ninety-eight. Reformists tried to build a constitutional monarchy. Eighteen ninety-five: Kang Youwei and the provincial graduates in Beijing for the exam petitioned the emperor — the “Gongche Petition”, 公车上书. June eleventh, eighteen ninety-eight: Emperor Guangxu issued the edict “Defining the State Policy” and launched the reform. Measures: reform government offices and appoint reformers; encourage private mines and factories; open new schools, drop the “eight-legged essay”, a rigid essay form used in the old exams, found the Imperial University of Peking; train a new army and navy. September twenty-first: Empress Dowager Cixi staged a coup and the reform failed; Tan Sitong and the other “Six Gentlemen” were killed. It lasted one hundred three days. Significance: a patriotic political movement and an ideological enlightenment.
china/modern-china.97f3b416f9da: Eighteen forty, The Opium War. In June eighteen thirty-nine Lin Zexu destroyed confiscated opium at Humen. In eighteen forty Britain used this as an excuse to launch the Opium War — the beginning of China’s modern history.
china/modern-china.1db0f6e30e9e: August eighteen forty-two: the Qing government was forced to sign the Treaty of Nanjing: cede Hong Kong Island to Britain; pay twenty-one million silver dollars; open Guangzhou, Xiamen, Fuzhou, Ningbo and Shanghai as treaty ports; tariffs on British goods had to be agreed with Britain.
china/modern-china.ecc057c9cd1b: War costs and silver payments were pushed onto poor farmers. In eighteen fifty-one Hong Xiuquan led them in an uprising at Jintian village in Guangxi and announced a new state, the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom, 太平天国. Hong Xiuquan’s Chinese name is 洪秀全.
china/modern-china.4fe02e41a76a: Meanwhile in the US and the world: In eighteen fifty-three US Navy warships under Commodore Perry sailed into Tokyo Bay to force Japan to open its ports too.
china/modern-china.75a50b505bbc: Watch out: Modern history begins with the outbreak of the war in eighteen forty, not with the eighteen forty-two treaty. The Treaty of Nanjing was the first unequal treaty in modern Chinese history.
china/modern-china.b3ded45bec3b: Sino-Japanese War and Treaty of Shimonoseki. Eighteen ninety-four to eighteen ninety-five. Greatly deepened China’s semi-colonial status. Eighteen ninety-four: Japan provoked the war. In the Battle of the Yellow Sea, Deng Shichang, 邓世昌, captain of the warship Zhiyuan, died a hero. Early eighteen ninety-five: the Beiyang Fleet was completely destroyed at Weihaiwei. April eighteen ninety-five Treaty of Shimonoseki: cede the Liaodong Peninsula, Taiwan with all its affiliated islands, and the Penghu Islands to Japan; pay two hundred million taels of silver; open Shashi, Chongqing, Suzhou and Hangzhou; allow Japan to open factories in treaty ports. Under pressure from Russia, Germany and France, Japan returned the Liaodong Peninsula, but China paid thirty million taels to “redeem” it. After the war the powers began a scramble to carve up China.
china/modern-china.cacdd95bfde7: China lost the war. The first unequal treaty made it give Hong Kong Island to Britain, pay twenty-one million silver dollars, open five ports — watch them appear on the map — and let Britain have a say in China’s import taxes. China began to turn into a semi-colonial, semi-feudal society.
china/modern-china.bc80650756e1: Memory rhyme: Jintian, eighteen fifty-one, capital at Tianjing, eighteen fifty-three, Tianjing falls, eighteen sixty-four.
china/modern-china.ed44d94fd1b6: What would you do if warships sailed halfway around the world to force your country to keep buying an illegal drug? In eighteen forty that happened to China. Britain started the Opium War, and China — then ruled by the emperors of the Qing dynasty, 清朝, sixteen forty-four to nineteen twelve — lost. For the next eighty years foreign powers forced one unfair treaty after another on China.

china/natural-wonders.1c431256a2f1: Water dissolves or deposits limestone, karst
china/natural-wonders.7b6334f464c5: At each stop you see a real photo. Step one: name the landform type. Step two: explain how it formed. Ten points per correct step, bonus points for streaks. How high can you rank?
china/natural-wonders.0ba1d3f54ae5: Karst is land made of rock that water can dissolve, mostly limestone. In Chinese, it’s 喀斯特, also 岩溶, which means “rock-dissolving”. The name comes from the Kras region of Slovenia. Southwest China has one of the biggest karst areas on Earth.
china/natural-wonders.25f6059168aa: In a cave, stalactites and stalagmites, 石钟乳 and 石笋, are made by
china/natural-wonders.aafb5b045c66: Simplified model: in real caves growth rates vary a lot — roughly zero point one to three millimeters a year, one to thirty centimeters per one hundred years, depending on how much water drips, temperature and carbon dioxide. Here stalactite and stalagmite grow at the same rate.
china/natural-wonders.e2796143f5a8: Grade seven Volume one, The Movement of Plates, formation of the Himalayas; Grade eight Volume two, regional landscapes of the Southwest and Northwest.
china/natural-wonders.ea2dbd301fec: In caves like Reed Flute Cave in Guilin — the cave is called 芦笛岩 — water full of dissolved limestone drips from the ceiling. As each drop loses its carbon dioxide, a tiny ring of calcite is left behind: stalactites grow down — in Chinese, 石钟乳. Stalagmites grow up — in Chinese, 石笋. And when they meet they make a column, 石柱. Set the growth rate and press to fast-forward time.
china/natural-wonders.2328665a44bf: At this rate, a stalagmite as tall as you needs about fourteen thousand nine hundred sixty years, for a height of one hundred fifty centimeters, about five feet.
china/natural-wonders.1ff71c52a594: Travertine dams and pools grow fast — the bar starts only about fifty thousand years ago.
china/natural-wonders.121e3fcce33f: Supports the twenty twenty-two Compulsory-Education Geography Standard, “Understanding China”: describe China’s main landform features from maps and data; use examples to show how natural elements are linked; and how internal forces and external forces shape the surface — crustal movement for the first, and running water, wind and glaciers for the second. Textbook: P E P Grade eight Volume one, Chapter two, The Natural Environment of China, Section one, Landforms;
china/natural-wonders.042adf511983: Your mission: visit eight wonders on the map, use the geology clock to crack each one’s “recipe”, then pass the Geologist’s Field Trip.
china/natural-wonders.2e76eb5e017f: Water containing C O two dissolves limestone
china/natural-wonders.de85813904b0: Guilin, since about ten million years ago
china/natural-wonders.805c677f05a9: Qomolangma, since about fifty million years ago
china/natural-wonders.4dd23011c4c3: Lots of limestone and a hot, rainy climate
china/natural-wonders.d6cc17329a8d: When a drop loses C O two, calcium carbonate comes out of the water — karst can build as well as dissolve.
china/natural-wonders.eb72652078be: Beyond the junior-high textbook: how karst, Danxia, yardang, granite and glacial landforms form is covered systematically only in senior-high geography, Compulsory Volume one, “Landforms”; this page gives an intuitive introduction. Rock ages and carving periods are rounded approximations compiled by the author from UNESCO summaries and popular geology sources; studies differ.

The time axis is logarithmic: each step is ten times older. Values are rounded approximations and studies differ.
