china/new-era.b9e6c09d9aa4: Data notes: poverty figures are the official count of rural poor under China’s current standard, National Bureau of Statistics; high-speed-rail lengths are rounded year-end figures. Events from twenty twenty-three to twenty twenty-four are newer than some printings of the textbook and are included as extension material. Examples are “C nine one nine enters service” and “Chang’e six”.
china/new-era.62eff9742183: Don’t mix up: The basic station has three modules, one core and two labs — not counting visiting spacecraft.
china/new-era.1407a0e4e590: The Two Centenary Goals, “centenary” equals one hundredth birthday: a moderately prosperous society by the CPC’s one hundredth birthday, twenty twenty-one, and a great modern socialist country by the People’s Republic’s one hundredth, twenty forty-nine.
china/new-era.894ab2f8c868: Time machine: from twenty twelve toward twenty forty-nine
china/new-era.f0c888bdbf95: Which list is the “Five-sphere Integrated Plan”, 五位一体?
china/new-era.a5a4dca58fe3: In twenty fourteen the leadership put forward a four-part strategy called the “Four Comprehensives”, 四个全面. “Comprehensive” means “in every respect”.
china/new-era.1c044d109aef: Twenty twenty-three. A home-built airliner carries passengers. On May twenty-eighth, twenty twenty-three, the C nine one nine — a passenger jet designed and built in China, about the size of a Boeing seven three seven — flew its first commercial flight, from Shanghai to Beijing.
china/new-era.c1532158f17b: Declared in February twenty twenty-one: all rural poor under the current standard were out of poverty.
china/new-era.8f1cb2a09553: December seventeenth: Chang’e five came home with one thousand seven hundred thirty-one grams of Moon rock and soil — the first samples brought back by anyone since nineteen seventy-six.
china/new-era.2a1d4eb2471d: Memory hook: Core first, Tianhe, twenty twenty-one, then ask, Wentian, then dream, Mengtian — a T by the end of twenty twenty-two.
china/new-era.da4657b1783a: Robotic arm. A ten-metre helping hand outside the station. About ten meters long, with seven joints — like a human arm with a shoulder, elbow and wrist. It can “crawl” along the outside of the station, end over end. It moves astronauts during spacewalks and can shift heavy equipment.
china/new-era.d2cec7337b92: Twenty forty-nine. Second centenary goal. By the middle of the century — the hundredth birthday of the People’s Republic in twenty forty-nine — build China into a great modern socialist country that is prosperous, strong, democratic, culturally advanced, harmonious and beautiful.
china/new-era.07d5b8ff4b2d: August twenty sixteen: “Micius”, 墨子号, the world’s first quantum science satellite, was launched.
china/new-era.d5283d556554: In October twenty fifteen the CPC put forward a new development philosophy in five words: innovation, coordination, green, openness and sharing. The philosophy is called 新发展理念. Growth should be smarter, more balanced, cleaner, more connected to the world, and fairer.
china/new-era.1072021cbad1: Twenty seventeen. The nineteenth National Congress: a “new era”. September nineteen forty-nine: a big conference of many parties and groups, the CPPCC, met in Beiping. It passed the Common Programme, 共同纲领, which worked as a temporary constitution, and elected Mao Zedong, 毛泽东, Chairman. It chose the five-star red flag, the song “March of the Volunteers” as the anthem, and renamed Beiping “Beijing” — the capital. October first, nineteen forty-nine: at Tian’anmen, 天安门, “Gate of Heavenly Peace”, Mao announced the new government to a crowd of three hundred thousand. china/prc-founding.5e66a16c0edc: Land reform. Nineteen fifty to nineteen fifty-two. Before: a small class of landlords owned much of the farmland; most peasants rented fields and paid heavy rents. By the end of nineteen fifty-two it was basically complete: about three hundred million peasants — twice the whole US population then — received land. Why it matters: a feudal land system more than two thousand years old was destroyed; farm output rose and the ground was prepared for industrialisation.

Goal: put most effort into heavy industry, steel, machines, vehicles, to lay the first foundations of an industrial country with a modern defence. Nineteen fifty-six: the first Chinese-built truck rolled out in Changchun, the first jet plane was built, and the Shenyang machine-tool plant opened. Scientists such as Deng Jiaxian and Qian Xuesen made outstanding contributions; their spirit is the “two bombs, one satellite” spirit.
china/prc.ba19b275043a: The Wuhan Yangtze River Bridge opened in nineteen fifty-seven: a road on top and a railway underneath, joining north and south China across the country’s longest river, the Yangtze, 长江.
china/prc.7d02b00e7770: After land reform was basically completed, at the end of nineteen fifty-two…
china/prc.42be82ed8008: The Third Plenary Session of the eleventh CPC Central Committee, December nineteen seventy-eight
china/prc.56d761e9da18: Meanwhile in the US: Americans were getting ready for the year two thousand — and worrying about the “Y two K” computer bug.
china/prc.fb6735a59481: Meanwhile in the US: In nineteen fifty-six President Eisenhower signed the law that created the Interstate Highway System.
china/prc.81548af86f1c: Meanwhile in the US: At those Games the American swimmer Michael Phelps won eight gold medals. In November two thousand eight Barack Obama was elected president.
china/prc.bac3923e646a: Suggestion: use lesson steps six to eight to build the opening-up pattern, special economic zones, coastal open cities, coastal open economic regions, inland. The year slider in the three D hall lets students name achievements in time order; pair it with the year game.
china/prc.62e4b0395a05: Meanwhile in the US: Bill Clinton was president. Three days later, on July fourth, nineteen ninety-seven, NASA’s Pathfinder landed on Mars.
china/prc.9f0fad25d083: Nineteen eighty, Special economic zones. Four special economic zones were set up: Shenzhen, Zhuhai, Shantou and Xiamen — “windows” for technology, management and knowledge. In nineteen eighty-eight Hainan became a province and the largest special economic zone.
china/prc.49a15eea6559: Launched piece by piece from Wenchang on Hainan Island, the three modules of Tiangong were joined into a T shape by the end of twenty twenty-two. Tiangong, 天宫, means “heavenly palace”. Crews of three live there for about six months at a time.
china/prc.2dfc9b347169: Meanwhile in the US: George H. W. Bush was elected president in nineteen eighty-eight.
china/prc.f35f8a7e72de: The policy begun in December nineteen seventy-eight: reform the economy at home and open to trade and investment from abroad. At home, let farmers and companies make more of their own decisions.
china/prc.3b815cf75cd2: On October sixteenth, nineteen sixty-four, China’s first atomic bomb was tested in the desert at Lop Nur. A hydrogen bomb followed in nineteen sixty-seven. With missiles and a satellite, these are known as “two bombs, one satellite”, 两弹一星.
china/prc.4c1d22d4e3c7: The everyday name for the People’s Republic of China, PRC, the country founded on October first, nineteen forty-nine.
china/prc.56067cc1a98c: The Fuxing trains, designed in China, began running between Beijing and Shanghai: one thousand three hundred eighteen kilometers in about four and a half hours, a distance of eight hundred nineteen miles. Fuxing, 复兴号, means “rejuvenation”. China’s high-speed network is the longest in the world.
china/prc.66373c624739: Nineteen eighty-four to two thousand one, All-round opening up. In nineteen eighty-four fourteen coastal port cities were opened; in nineteen ninety Shanghai Pudong was developed and opened; in two thousand one China joined the WTO. A pattern formed: special economic zones, coastal open cities, coastal open economic regions, inland.
china/prc.0c0240a2cecf: Hybrid rice. Nineteen seventy-three. Yuan Longping, “father of hybrid rice”. Nineteen seventy-three: Yuan Longping and his team bred indica hybrid rice for the first time in the world. Hybrid rice greatly raised rice yields and helped solve the problem of feeding China’s people. It has been grown in many countries, contributing to world food security.
china/prc.1a503a9525f5: On October fifteenth, two thousand three, Yang Liwei circled the Earth in Shenzhou five, 神舟, “divine vessel”. His name in Chinese is 杨利伟. China became the third country to send a person into space with its own rocket.
china/prc.36bbef08b822: Meanwhile in the US: In nineteen fifty-one Americans watched the first coast-to-coast live TV broadcast.
china/prc.8083f82a8e94: Meanwhile in the US: The American system is GPS, the one in most US phones, complete since nineteen ninety-five. In twenty twenty a SpaceX capsule carried NASA astronauts to orbit for the first time.
china/prc.4c34388c4d99: Memory rhyme: Orbit, two thousand seven, far side, twenty nineteen, samples home, twenty twenty.
china/prc.7ff7c323e8a0: Common mix-up: The first special economic zones were Shenzhen, Zhuhai, Shantou and Xiamen, in nineteen eighty; Hainan became one in nineteen eighty-eight. Hong Kong returned on July first, nineteen ninety-seven, Macao on December twentieth, nineteen ninety-nine.
china/prc.adc47ccfeaee: China’s first astronaut to travel into space, aboard Shenzhou five in two thousand three, was…
china/prc.38118b4b2a8c: June nineteen sixty-seven: China’s first hydrogen bomb was successfully tested.
china/prc.0c07b4316114: Meanwhile in the US: That same month the damaged Apollo thirteen made it safely back to Earth. The first US satellite, Explorer one, had flown in nineteen fifty-eight.
china/prc.5c1908f5deba: Hainan became a special economic zone in nineteen eighty-eight.
china/prc.3248efe1c9c4: October first, nineteen forty-nine, The founding ceremony. In September the CPPCC adopted the Common Programme and chose Beijing as the capital, the five-star red flag and the “March of the Volunteers”. On October first Mao Zedong proclaimed the founding of the People’s Republic of China at Tian’anmen.
china/prc.7dcbe0f20563: This page is the overview of nineteen forty-nine to today for US middle-schoolers new to Chinese history: key terms carry pinyin and a meaning, and each event on the year slider has a “meanwhile in the US” anchor. The anchors only help students place the date; they are not textbook content. Four deeper lessons cover each period. They are linked at the top.
china/prc.a1dcdab5173f: Memory rhyme: Tianhe, Wentian and Mengtian — equals a “T” in the sky, twenty twenty-two.
china/prc.aab8e685a9f1: Nineteen seventy-eight, A great turning point. The Third Plenary Session of the eleventh Central Committee in December nineteen seventy-eight restored “emancipating the mind and seeking truth from facts”, shifted the focus to economic construction and launched reform and opening up. Farmers in Xiaogang Village, Anhui, began the household contract responsibility system.
china/prc.31ab266f1263: Meanwhile in the US: Jimmy Carter was president. In December nineteen seventy-eight the US and China announced that they would open full diplomatic relations on January first, nineteen seventy-nine.
china/prc.bf94c16a88bb: The founding of the PRC on October first, nineteen forty-nine, marked…
china/prc.b184231b6251: Memory rhyme: two thousand three, Yang Liwei: China’s first step into space.
china/prc.fe7b7714a6af: Memory rhyme: two thousand eight Beijing-Tianjin; twenty seventeen Fuxing.
china/prc.6e1233b84d0e: April nineteen seventy: China launched its first man-made Earth satellite, Dongfanghong one, “The East Is Red one”.
china/prc.0ae1d5fc3b2e: October first, nineteen ninety-seven; December twentieth, nineteen ninety-nine
china/prc.e0f82462c558: Meanwhile in the US: In nineteen ninety NASA launched the Hubble Space Telescope, and the World Wide Web was being invented.
china/prc.b1057054ed16: Supports the PRC part of the “Modern and Contemporary Chinese History” strand of the twenty twenty-two national history curriculum standard: the founding of the PRC, the War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea, land reform, the First Five-Year Plan and socialist transformation; the Third Plenary Session of the eleventh Central Committee as a great turning point; reform and opening up;
china/prc.e68bdcbb721b: Drag the years: seventy-three years on one map
china/prc.4cc9c4b790aa: In nineteen fifty-one Tibet was peacefully liberated. With that, the textbook says, the mainland of China was unified. Lhasa sits about three thousand six hundred fifty meters above sea level, or twelve thousand feet — more than twice as high as Denver.
china/prc.25af0afec7db: Chang’e lunar programme. Two thousand seven, twenty nineteen. From orbiting the Moon to landing on its far side. Two thousand seven: Chang’e one, China’s first lunar probe, was launched. January twenty nineteen: Chang’e four made the first-ever soft landing on the far side of the Moon; the Yutu two rover explored it. Twenty twenty: Chang’e five brought lunar samples back to Earth.
china/prc.acd7d2cb9e6d: High-speed rail and Fuxing trains. Two thousand eight, twenty seventeen. The world’s largest high-speed rail network. Two thousand six: the Qinghai-Tibet Railway opened along its whole length. Two thousand eight: the Beijing-Tianjin intercity railway opened — China’s first high-speed line designed for three hundred fifty kilometers per hour. Twenty seventeen: the Fuxing, “Rejuvenation”, bullet trains, with independent intellectual property, entered service. China’s high-speed rail network is the longest in the world.
china/prc.fbd758b48cbc: In nineteen sixty “Iron Man” Wang Jinxi and his drilling team worked through the bitter northeastern winter to open the Daqing oil field. His name in Chinese is 王进喜. Within a few years China could supply its own oil.
china/prc.73013e02d966: In December two thousand one China joined the World Trade Organization, WTO, the group of countries that agrees the rules of world trade. Ports such as Shanghai grew into the busiest on Earth, and “Made in China” appeared in stores everywhere.

china/qin-han.73d498f92d2d: In two twenty-one B C E King Ying Zheng of Qin conquered the six states and founded China’s first unified, multi-ethnic, centralized state, with its capital at Xianyang. He took the title “First Emperor”, Shi Huangdi.
china/qin-han.b408327116aa: Meanwhile, elsewhere: Rome is now an empire under Augustus, from twenty-seven B C E to fourteen C E. Jesus is growing up in Galilee, a land under Roman control.
china/qin-han.ae3f522b0d57: In sixty B C E the Western Han set up the Protectorate of the Western Regions. From then on, the region of today’s Xinjiang came under the central government and became an inseparable part of China.
china/qin-han.8e2d1c2c8256: A new title invented in two twenty-one B C E by Qin Shi Huang, 秦始皇, “First Emperor of Qin”. China had emperors for the next two thousand one hundred thirty-two years, until nineteen twelve.
china/qin-han.cae70ba1ea39: In the late Warring States period Qin grew strong. From two hundred thirty to two hundred twenty-one B C E King Ying Zheng conquered Han, Zhao, Wei, Chu, Yan and Qi, founding the Qin dynasty — China’s first unified, multi-ethnic, centralized state — with its capital at Xianyang.
china/qin-han.96b3e228ffa5: Qin’s harsh rule provoked revolt. In two hundred nine B C E Chen Sheng and Wu Guang rose up at Dazexiang — the first large-scale peasant uprising in Chinese history. Qin fell in two hundred seven B C E; after the Chu-Han war, Liu Bang founded the Western Han in two hundred two B C E with its capital at Chang’an.
china/qin-han.42408304cd79: Time map: drag through four hundred forty years
china/qin-han.3ebe756daca6: Meanwhile, elsewhere: Mount Vesuvius buries Pompeii, seventy-nine C E; the Colosseum opens, eighty C E; Rome reaches its greatest size in one seventeen C E.
china/qin-han.5510db1f2787: Meanwhile, elsewhere: In two oh two B C E Rome finally defeats Hannibal at Zama — the very year the Han dynasty begins.
china/qin-han.cb0aaa72c0fa: The dynasty founded by Liu Bang in two oh two B C E. Most Chinese people today call themselves “Han people” and call their writing “Han characters”.
china/qin-han.4b231484a7ac: Sixty B C E: the Han sets up a governor for the Western Regions. Caravans now carry silk west and bring back horses, grapes, walnuts, glass and new music. Around this time Han China and the Roman Empire each rule about sixty million people — together close to half of all humans alive.
china/qin-han.a3f4e87a0917: Meanwhile, elsewhere: Rome destroys its rival Carthage in one forty-six B C E and becomes master of the Mediterranean.
china/qin-han.addbb819f58c: The Protectorate of the Western Regions, sixty B C E
china/qin-han.e03ad9a9201a: Meanwhile, elsewhere: In Rome the Gracchus brothers are killed for trying to give land to the poor, one thirty-three and one twenty-one B C E.
china/qin-han.b79f45cce6e9: Suggestions: one, use the slider to let students name the problems before unification, including different coins, scripts and measures, and separate walls, before summarizing why Qin’s measures mattered; two, use the Qin or Ming toggle to correct the idea that today’s brick wall is the Qin wall; three, map steps five to seven build the chain Zhang Qian, Silk Road, Protectorate of the Western Regions;
china/qin-han.9f990d5646d8: Two twenty-one B C E: Qin has beaten the last rival state. The First Emperor orders one coin, one script, one set of weights and measures, and one axle width for carts. He replaces the old lords with appointed officials, builds roads, a canal in the south and a long wall in the north.
china/qin-han.e4c8df6e836f: It broke out in two oh nine B C E against Qin’s harsh rule.
china/qin-han.b5a19291d4c9: Seventy-three C E: Ban Chao, 班超, reopens the Western Regions; in ninety-seven his envoy Gan Ying reaches the Persian Gulf, trying to find Rome. One oh five: Cai Lun, 蔡伦, improves paper-making. One thirty-two: Zhang Heng, 张衡, builds a device that detects distant earthquakes. One sixty-six: envoys from Daqin arrive, that is, from Rome.
china/qin-han.03983e02da40: Meanwhile, elsewhere: In Central Asia he reached lands that Alexander the Great had conquered two hundred years earlier. His journey of about four thousand kilometers each way, about two thousand five hundred miles, was like walking from New York to Los Angeles — through deserts and enemy land.
china/qin-han.bfb11c830b1b: The First Emperor ran the regions through commanderies and counties — thirty-six commanderies at first, later more than forty. Meng Tian drove back the Xiongnu and a wall was built from Lintao in the west to Liaodong in the east; in the south the Lingqu Canal joined the Xiang and Li rivers.
china/qin-han.39cb087f46c8: Harsh laws, heavy taxes and forced labour make people desperate. In two oh nine B C E two farmers, Chen Sheng and Wu Guang, start China’s first great peasant uprising. By two oh seven B C E the Qin is gone — after only fifteen years. Two rebel leaders, Xiang Yu and Liu Bang, then fight over the empire.
china/qin-han.9f486bb0c094: Four, after the game, ask which road students chose, north or south, and what goods travelled each way.
china/qin-han.77f52f5b3080: In nine C E an official named Wang Mang seizes the throne and the Western Han ends. In twenty-five C E a member of the Han family, Liu Xiu, 刘秀, restores the dynasty with a new capital further east, at Luoyang: the Eastern Han.
china/qin-han.a71e1cea4a12: Two oh two B C E: Liu Bang, 刘邦, born a commoner, becomes emperor and rules from Chang’an. After years of war the land is so poor that even the emperor cannot find four horses of the same colour for his carriage. The early Han emperors cut taxes and let farmers recover.
china/qin-han.e67a311c1b08: What was the original purpose of Zhang Qian’s first mission, in one thirty-eight B C E?
china/qin-han.ebfd95da0089: Aligned with the twenty twenty-two national History Curriculum Standard, compulsory education, ancient China: the founding and consolidation of a unified multi-ethnic state under Qin and Han; textbook: national unified edition, Grade seven Volume
china/qin-han.e2276dd3fc51: Emperor Wu weakens the remaining princes, makes Confucian teaching the official learning, opens an imperial academy, puts salt, iron and coin-making under state control — and sends armies north against the Xiongnu. 汉武帝 ruled from one forty-one to eighty-seven B C E.
china/qin-han.984351515005: Meanwhile, elsewhere: Julius Caesar conquers Gaul, present-day France, and is murdered in forty-four B C E. Rich Romans pay huge prices for Chinese silk without knowing where it comes from.
china/qin-han.0fa50fc9fcce: Under Emperor Wu the Western Han reached its height. He reigned from one hundred forty-one to eighty-seven B C E. His generals Wei Qing and Huo Qubing drove back the Xiongnu and took the Hetao region and the Hexi Corridor, where four commanderies were set up: Wuwei, Zhangye, Jiuquan and Dunhuang.
china/qin-han.f23d61e8b3fb: One thirty-eight B C E: Emperor Wu sends Zhang Qian west, 张骞 in Chinese, to find allies against the Xiongnu. He is captured, held for more than ten years, escapes, keeps going, and gets home after thirteen years — with no alliance, but with the first real knowledge of the lands to the west. A second trip in one nineteen B C E opens regular contact.
china/qin-han.b1db693f3ee4: Drag the slider from two twenty-one B C E to two twenty C E. Watch the Great Wall being built, follow Zhang Qian step by step into the far west, and see the Silk Road appear. Click any dot or coloured area. For scale: the map is about five thousand kilometers wide, or three thousand one hundred miles — wider than the United States from coast to coast.
china/qin-han.246a8d6c205e: To win the Yuezhi as allies against the Xiongnu, Emperor Wu sent Zhang Qian to the Western Regions in one hundred thirty-eight B C E; he went again in one hundred nineteen B C E. His journeys strengthened ties between the Central Plains and the Western Regions.
china/qin-han.fed861cdd4bc: Child emperors, scheming relatives and palace eunuchs wreck the government. In one eighty-four C E the Yellow Turban uprising, led by Zhang Jiao, shakes the empire. Generals grab power, and in two twenty the Han ends. Next lesson: three kingdoms.
china/qin-han.e7b14b79e2c2: In twenty-five C E Liu Xiu founded the Eastern Han with its capital at Luoyang. Ban Chao restored Han control of the Western Regions and sent Gan Ying toward Daqin; Gan Ying reached the Persian Gulf. Cai Lun improved papermaking. Under Qin and Han the unified multi-ethnic state was built and consolidated.
china/qin-han.bf33b3a82b07: One, Unit three, Lessons nine to fifteen: Qin unification, the late-Qin uprisings, the Western Han and the Wen Jing era, Emperor Wu, the Eastern Han, the Silk Road, Han science and culture.
china/qin-han.ad606a4c4d9b: Meanwhile, elsewhere: Rome controls only Italy and a few nearby islands, Sicily, Sardinia, Corsica. In two eighteen B C E its enemy Hannibal marches war elephants over the Alps.
china/qin-han.23a2c176f3e2: In two twenty-one B C E Qin unified China. Where was its capital?
china/qin-han.9fd3eb4f22c3: Seven kingdoms with seven kinds of money, different writing and even different widths of cart axle: how do you turn them into one country? In two twenty-one B C E the king of Qin did it in about ten years and called himself First Emperor. Qin is 秦 Qín, said “chin”. The Han dynasty that followed lasted over four hundred years and was about as big and as populous as the Roman Empire on the other side of the world. Han in Chinese is 汉.

china/reform-opening.58c6ee5c766f: Two thousand two, sixteenth Party Congress: the “Three Represents”, 三个代表, put forward by Jiang Zemin, became a guiding thought — the Party must stand for advanced production, advanced culture and the interests of the great majority of the people.
china/reform-opening.49584aa36f15: Suggestion: let students drag the slider and work out the pattern for themselves — points, a line along the coast, whole regions, inland. Then check it with the ordering game. GDP figures are rounded official statistics and Shenzhen’s population figures are rounded census or yearbook data, shown for the trend only; ordinary three D blocks are schematic. Maps are schematic.
china/reform-opening.f2eb11f394f4: About four hundred forty-two meters — the same height as Chicago’s Willis Tower, also called the Sears Tower.
china/reform-opening.122e8b1f6d81: Nineteen eighty: farms and fishing villages
china/reform-opening.5e58f32178b8: Three D model: grow the Shenzhen skyline, nineteen eighty to twenty twenty
china/reform-opening.b3464e823b3e: Ping An Finance Centre, twenty seventeen. About five hundred ninety-nine meters, one hundred eighteen floors — taller than One World Trade Center in New York, five hundred forty-one meters. From fishing villages to one of the world’s tallest towers in under forty years.
china/reform-opening.c9624ca40a76: Nineteen eighty: farms and fishing villages. August nineteen eighty: the Shenzhen Special Economic Zone was set up, just across a small river from Hong Kong. Why here? Hong Kong was already a rich trading city: money, factories and know-how could simply walk across the bridge. Slide back to nineteen eighty: almost nothing is taller than a tree.
china/reform-opening.ba8a88ff7344: Memory hook: Two thousand one: member number one hundred forty-three.
china/reform-opening.82fcd5a9310c: The fifteenth Party Congress, nineteen ninety-seven
china/reform-opening.9122b027a666: By twenty eleven Shenzhen was home to technology companies known around the world.
china/reform-opening.fd1bf3d29a49: Watch out: Match each idea to its congress: nineteen ninety-seven, fifteenth, two thousand two, sixteenth, two thousand seven over twenty twelve, seventeenth and eighteenth.
china/reform-opening.f5a1f215018d: Deng Xiaoping Theory. Nineteen eighty-two, nineteen eighty-seven, nineteen ninety-two, nineteen ninety-seven. Deng Xiaoping is called the chief architect of reform and opening up. Nineteen eighty-two: he called for building “socialism with Chinese characteristics” — China should follow its own road, not copy others. Nineteen eighty-seven, thirteenth Party Congress: China is at the primary stage of socialism. Basic line: economic development as the central task, plus two basic points — keep the socialist road and Party leadership, and keep reforming and opening up. Nineteen ninety-two: on a tour of the south, including Shenzhen, Deng, aged eighty-seven, said: “Development is the absolute principle.” Plans and markets are both just tools. Nineteen ninety-seven, fifteenth Party Congress: Deng Xiaoping Theory was made the Party’s guiding thought.
china/reform-opening.585e9ad28bb7: Memory hook: Fifteenth — Deng’s theory; sixteenth — Three Represents; seventeenth and eighteenth — Scientific Outlook.
china/reform-opening.6da7cf98dfce: In nineteen ninety-two Deng Xiaoping looked out over the city from its revolving restaurant during his southern tour.
china/reform-opening.2fcfd0954710: Nineteen nineties: cities along the Yangtze, towns on the land borders and inland provincial capitals were opened too.
china/reform-opening.136ad7b9fd0c: 经济特区 — test labs for opening up
china/reform-opening.30e86df68aee: After the “Cultural Revolution” ended in nineteen seventy-six, some leaders said: just keep doing whatever Mao decided, the “two whatevers”.
china/reform-opening.c8b01bc6a814: From fishing villages to one of the world’s tallest towers in under forty years.
china/reform-opening.5919a9f11f8e: Nineteen seventy-eight: farmers in Xiaogang Village, 小岗村, Anhui, secretly divided the fields among families: each family would farm its own plot.
china/reform-opening.2ab53ffe1666: 家庭联产承包责任制 — each family farms its own contracted fields
china/reform-opening.b1bed8b34559: Urban reform and the socialist market economy. from nineteen eighty-four, nineteen ninety-two. Before: state-owned factories simply followed the state plan — what to make, how many, what price. From nineteen eighty-four to eighty-five reform moved into the cities. The key step: bring state-owned enterprises to life by letting managers make decisions and rewarding good work. Other kinds of business were allowed to grow beside public ownership — private shops, joint ventures, foreign companies. Nineteen ninety-two: the fourteenth Party Congress set the goal — a socialist market economy, 社会主义市场经济. By the early two thousands it was basically in place.
china/reform-opening.c14fa520a31c: Diwang Building, nineteen ninety-six. About three hundred eighty-four meters — as tall as the Empire State Building’s roof, three hundred eighty-one meters. Finished in nineteen ninety-six, it was then the tallest building in China. By now Shenzhen made toys, clothes and electronics sold all over the world.
china/reform-opening.87d5164d16ac: Watch out: Pudong is a development area in Shanghai, dating from nineteen ninety — not one of the special economic zones.
china/reform-opening.f5a99c8176b5: The open-door pattern: coast first, then inland. Nineteen eighty-five to the nineteen nineties. From nineteen eighty-five: whole regions — the Yangtze River Delta, the Pearl River Delta, southeast Fujian and later the Bohai Rim — became coastal open economic regions. Nineteen ninety: Pudong in Shanghai was developed and opened. Its name, 浦东, means “east of the river.” Its farmland became a forest of skyscrapers. Nineteen nineties: cities along the Yangtze, towns on the land borders and inland provincial capitals were opened too. Result: an all-round, multi-level, wide-ranging pattern of opening — from the coast to the interior.
china/reform-opening.fe8d9a08083a: A famous roadside slogan of the nineteen eighties: “Time is money, efficiency is life.”
china/reform-opening.f34e3466b82e: Special economic zones. Nineteen eighty, nineteen eighty-eight. Nineteen eighty: four special economic zones, SEZs, were set up in Shenzhen, Zhuhai, Shantou and Xiamen — all on the coast of Guangdong and Fujian, near Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan. Inside a zone, special rules welcomed foreign companies, money and technology: a “window” to the world. Shenzhen grew fastest of all — people spoke of “Shenzhen speed”. Nineteen eighty-eight: Hainan, 海南, a tropical island about the size of Maryland, became a province and the largest SEZ.
china/reform-opening.61bd5d628580: Two thousand seven, seventeenth Party Congress: the Scientific Outlook on Development, 科学发展观, put forward by Hu Jintao, was written into the Party constitution: put people first; development should be balanced and sustainable.
china/reform-opening.a9ac4e3c0ddb: Deng Xiaoping is called the chief architect of reform and opening up. Nineteen eighty-two: he called for building “socialism with Chinese characteristics” — China should follow its own road, not copy others.
china/reform-opening.535f990631dc: The Third Plenary Session of the eleventh Central Committee. December nineteen seventy-eight. Who met: the Communist Party’s Central Committee — a few hundred top leaders — in Beijing. Thinking: “free your mind, seek truth from facts”. Politics: stop putting “class struggle” first; shift the country’s main work to building the economy and start reform and opening up. Leadership: a new leading group formed with Deng Xiaoping, 邓小平, at its core. Why it matters: it opened the new period of reform, opening up and socialist modernisation.
china/reform-opening.fe6cfce237b8: Opening up entered a new stage: China joined the world economy on a much larger scale — look at how the economy chart climbs after two thousand one.
china/reform-opening.c723e61ad8b9: Twenty ten: China’s economy became the second largest in the world, after the United States.
china/reform-opening.1372cf121c0f: In nineteen eighty Shenzhen, 深圳, next door to Hong Kong, was a county of farms and fishing villages with about three hundred thirty thousand people. Forty years later it had seventeen million — twice New York City. The change began in December nineteen seventy-eight, when China’s leaders chose “reform and opening up”, 改革开放: reform the economy at home, open the door to the world.
china/reform-opening.bbeee63d1aae: May nineteen seventy-eight: a newspaper essay argued that an idea is true only if it works in real life — practice is the test.
china/reform-opening.f4709f63ff36: Try it: Drag the year back to nineteen eighty, then press “Grow”. Which decade adds the most towers?
china/reform-opening.93fc9df4a39f: Nineteen ninety: Pudong in Shanghai was developed and opened; its farmland became a forest of skyscrapers. Pudong, 浦东, means “east of the river”.
china/reform-opening.dd295a2f93ca: Tianjin. Tianjin is Beijing’s gateway to the sea, on the Bohai. Since two thousand eight high-speed trains link the two cities in about thirty minutes.
china/reform-opening.5de68678dd9b: China joins the World Trade Organization. The eleventh of December, two thousand one. The WTO is the organisation of countries that agree on common rules for trade; the US is a member too. After fifteen years of talks, China became its one hundred forty-third member on the eleventh of December, two thousand one. Opening up entered a new stage: China joined the world economy on a much larger scale — look at how the economy chart climbs after two thousand one. Twenty ten: China’s economy became the second largest in the world, after the United States.

china/reform-opening.6a4f5035a4ee: Rural reform: the household contract responsibility system. from nineteen seventy-eight. Before: villagers farmed together in communes and shared the harvest about equally — work hard or not, you got the same. Nineteen seventy-eight: farmers in Xiaogang Village, 小岗村, Anhui, secretly divided the fields among families: each family would farm its own plot. The deal: “Hand in the state’s share, keep enough for the collective, and all the rest is ours.” The land still belongs to the collective; families contract it. Harvests jumped. The system spread nationwide, and village factories, township enterprises, sprang up.

Twenty twelve, eighteenth Party Congress: it too became a guiding thought of the Party. Together with Deng Xiaoping Theory these form one system of ideas: socialism with Chinese characteristics.

china/revolution.b9313af8b761: Watch out: Reaching Wuqi did not yet end the Long March as a whole — that came in October nineteen thirty-six.
china/revolution.d0c779f5a6b8: Eleven short steps, under a minute each — press Start, then to move on at your own speed. Watch the revolution move from the cities to the countryside, the Long March turn danger into safety, and two wars end in victory: the War of Resistance against Japan and the War of Liberation, the civil war of nineteen forty-six to nineteen forty-nine. Maps are schematic.
china/revolution.56e4c97d6793: Nineteen thirty-seven to nineteen forty-five, The War of Resistance. Japan committed the Nanjing Massacre. Chinese forces fought back: Pingxingguan, nineteen thirty-seven, Taierzhuang, nineteen thirty-eight, the Hundred Regiments Offensive, nineteen forty. On August fifteenth, nineteen forty-five, Japan surrendered unconditionally; Taiwan returned to China. It was the first complete victory against foreign invasion in modern times.
china/revolution.9297e24d45f4: Nineteen twenty-seven, Armed struggle and Jinggangshan. On August first the Nanchang Uprising fired the first shot against the KMT reactionaries. The August seventh Meeting chose agrarian revolution and armed resistance. Mao Zedong led the Autumn Harvest Uprising troops to Jinggangshan — the first rural revolutionary base.
china/revolution.e9312e6a8d20: Huining reunion. October nineteen thirty-six. The three main Red Armies meet: the Long March ends. October nineteen thirty-six: the Red First, Second and Fourth Front Armies met at Huining, Gansu, and Jiangtaibao, Ningxia. The Long March ended in victory. Significance: it preserved and tempered the core forces of the revolution and moved the revolution’s headquarters to the northwest. The Long March spirit: fearing no hardship, never giving up, putting the people’s interests first.
china/revolution.aca4ea8579fb: The founding of the CPC, nineteen twenty-one
china/revolution.9599d7e6071b: Wuqi Town, northern Shaanxi. October nineteen thirty-five. The Central Red Army reaches northern Shaanxi. October nineteen thirty-five: the Central Red Army reached Wuqi Town in northern Shaanxi and joined the Shaanxi Red Army. Northern Shaanxi became the base of the Chinese revolution.
china/revolution.9950379ddf58: Meanwhile in the US: The stock market crashes in nineteen twenty-nine and the Great Depression begins. The Empire State Building opens in nineteen thirty-one.

china/seas-islands.86a7a9037f43: Don’t mix up: China’s inland seas are the Bohai Sea and the Qiongzhou Strait — not the Yellow Sea. The term is 内海. And the southernmost point of China’s territory is Zengmu Ansha in the Nansha Islands, about four degrees north, not Sanya on Hainan Island.

china/silk-road-explorers.9bbd76e5a0d5: Zhang Qian. Western Han, one hundred thirty-eight to one hundred twenty-six B C. Emperor Wu of Han sent him to find the Yuezhi people and team up against the Xiongnu. Captured by the Xiongnu and held for more than ten years. Deserts and the high Pamir mountains. Captured again on the way home. First-hand knowledge of the Western Regions, 西域. News of Dayuan’s fine “heavenly horses”. Later: grapes, alfalfa, pomegranates, walnuts reach China. His journeys strengthened ties between the Central Plains and the Western Regions; the Silk Road took shape. In sixty B C the Western Han set up the Protectorate of the Western Regions — today’s Xinjiang formally came under the central government.

china/song-yuan.0a901e17e5b7: Founded by the Mongol ruler Kublai Khan, grandson of Genghis Khan. In twelve seventy-nine it reunited the whole country — a territory far bigger than today’s lower forty-eight US states.
china/song-yuan.b2b7c7d372e0: Zhao Kuangyin, 赵匡胤, an army general, is made emperor by his own troops and founds the Song. His capital is Kaifeng. To the north lies the Liao, founded by the Khitan people in nine sixteen.
china/song-yuan.fe7cd1294b37: The English is written for US middle-schoolers with no background in Chinese history: names carry characters, pinyin or a say-it hint, with familiar anchors, Miami’s latitude, the size of the lower forty-eight states, what was happening in Europe and North America. On the year slider, borders and capitals are schematic.
china/song-yuan.9fc28dc9ba35: The watertight-bulkhead technology of Chinese junks was inscribed by UNESCO in twenty ten as intangible cultural heritage in need of urgent safeguarding.
china/song-yuan.b0f5724c55b9: Three D model: Quanzhou harbour and a Song ocean ship
china/song-yuan.f004b46dd389: Taiwan Prefecture was set up later, by the Qing in sixteen eighty-four.
china/song-yuan.0b5dee59e918: Stern rudder. Steers the ship. A large rudder hung at the stern steers the ship. A pottery boat model of the Eastern Han found in Guangzhou already has a stern rudder, one of the earliest in the world. Rudder at the back, compass on deck: steering and direction.
china/song-yuan.89d011ea468d: Huining, Jin capital. Today: Acheng, Harbin, Heilongjiang. Wanyan Aguda of the Jurchen founded the Jin here; within twelve years the Jin destroyed both the Liao and the Northern Song.
china/song-yuan.339741f00135: Quanzhou harbour, Quanzhou equals chwen-joe. A world-famous port of the Song and Yuan. Quanzhou is on China’s southeast coast, about as far south as Miami. In the Song, overseas trade exceeded earlier dynasties; Guangzhou and Quanzhou were great ports known around the world. Quanzhou was a starting point of the Maritime Silk Road; merchants from Arabia, Persia and Southeast Asia came to trade. In twenty twenty-one “Quanzhou: Emporium of the World in Song-Yuan China” joined the UNESCO World Heritage List. Song-Yuan sea trade: remember “Guang-Quan”, Guangzhou and Quanzhou.
china/song-yuan.c74c2bbcfc83: How do you run a country bigger than the lower forty-eight US states with no phones and no trains? The Yuan split it into provinces, 行省. Tap a name, then tap its rough location on the schematic map. Correct answers are pinned to the map; you score a “first try” point only if your first tap is right.
china/song-yuan.e90fa124c568: In ten oh five the Northern Song and the Liao made a peace agreement. It is known as…
china/song-yuan.6772d41e8162: A thousand years ago — about five hundred years before Columbus — who was already paying with paper money, and whose ships could hit a rock and still not sink? The answer to both is Song-dynasty China, 宋, nine sixty to twelve seventy-six.
china/song-yuan.23a7490cd45e: The Jurchen Jin, dating to eleven fifteen, destroyed the Liao in eleven twenty-five and then the Northern Song in eleven twenty-seven, the Jingkang Incident. Zhao Gou founded the Southern Song, later based in Lin’an. After peace talks the border ran along the Huai River — Dasan Pass.
china/song-yuan.ecbfc998939f: In twelve oh six Temüjin united the Mongol tribes and was honoured as Genghis Khan. In twelve seventy-one Kublai named his state Yuan and the next year made Dadu, today’s Beijing, the capital. In twelve seventy-six Yuan troops took Lin’an, and in twelve seventy-nine the Yuan unified the whole country.
china/song-yuan.ae08ae243dc0: Curriculum: twenty twenty-two Compulsory Education History Standards, ancient China, “Liao, Song, Xia, Jin and Yuan”, in outline: coexisting regimes and ethnic integration, the southward shift of the economic centre, overseas trade, Yuan unification and the province system, and Song-Yuan science. Textbook: unified-edition Chinese History, Grade seven Volume.
china/song-yuan.0aa9c9f6aa4a: Guangzhou and Quanzhou were great Song ports; Quanzhou became a World Heritage site in twenty twenty-one.
china/song-yuan.ea27e5661e1d: The Yuan created the province system: the Central Secretariat ran the “heartland” around Dadu, and provinces, 行省, ran the rest. The Xuanzheng Yuan governed Tibet, and the Penghu Inspectorate governed Penghu and Liuqiu, Taiwan. Today’s provinces grew out of this system.
china/song-yuan.5c77dd6f1b31: Time slider: who rules where, nine sixty to thirteen sixty-eight?
china/song-yuan.132a36990776: Song ocean-going ship. Big, strong and built for the open sea. Song shipbuilding led the world: ships were large, carried heavy loads and resisted storms. A Song ship found in Quanzhou Bay in nineteen seventy-four had a hull divided into thirteen compartments. What survives is about twenty-four meters long, or seventy-nine feet, the length of a tennis court. Big ships could carry hundreds of people and sailed to Southeast Asia, South Asia, Arabia and East Africa, a sea voyage of more than six thousand miles, ten thousand kilometers. Three “big” things about Song ships: big hull, big load, big voyages.
china/song-yuan.c216e8d30436: Big idea: Technology, ships and compass, and policy, Shibosi, and economy, south, equals a golden age of sea trade.
china/song-yuan.31ff1210aeb4: Ten oh five, Song and Liao make peace
china/song-yuan.6d0a76bc90a0: Merchants in Sichuan had been swapping heavy iron coins for paper notes called jiaozi, 交子 — the world’s first paper money. In the ten twenties the government takes over printing them.
china/song-yuan.f2ab3d4dd439: Song times: the Northern Song, dating to nine sixty, stood beside the Liao of the Khitan and the Western Xia of the Tangut. In ten oh five the Song and Liao made the Chanyuan Treaty: the Song paid silver and silk each year, and a long peace followed.
china/song-yuan.71f6e3aec67c: Suggestions: one, play the map and have students name the three stages, began, sped up, completed, and the reasons; two, use the three D flooding test to explain watertight compartments and link it with the compass at sea as technical conditions of Song sea trade; three, after the province game ask: where does today’s “province” come from? The Yuan province system.
china/song-yuan.29afc4732ec5: Two halves: the Northern Song from nine sixty to eleven twenty-seven, with its capital at Kaifeng, and, after the north was lost, the Southern Song from eleven twenty-seven to twelve seventy-nine, with its capital at Lin’an, Hangzhou today. That is, Lin’an was in today’s Hangzhou.
china/song-yuan.fe55244a60d2: Ten twenty-three, Paper money goes official
china/song-yuan.9d3e83b1f99a: In twenty twenty-one “Quanzhou: Emporium of the World in Song-Yuan China” joined the UNESCO World Heritage List.
china/song-yuan.a23c15dcfa1d: The world’s first paper money, used in Sichuan about one thousand years ago — more than six hundred years before the first banknotes in Europe, in Sweden in sixteen sixty-one, or in colonial America, in Massachusetts in sixteen ninety.
china/song-yuan.ca9d6c6e4a67: A Liao army invades and is stopped at Chanzhou, today’s Puyang, Henan. The two sides agree to the Chanyuan Treaty, 澶渊之盟: the Song sends silver and silk every year. A long peace and busy border trade follow.
china/song-yuan.b1756567cb05: Maritime Trade Office, Shibosi, shir-bwo-suh. The government office that managed sea trade. The Song government set up Maritime Trade Offices in Guangzhou, Quanzhou, Mingzhou and other ports to manage overseas trade. They inspected ships, collected taxes and bought goods for the state. In the Southern Song, income from sea trade became an important source of government revenue. Shi-bo equals “market and ships”: like an ancient customs house.
china/song-yuan.4902905d3217: Two, Unit two, lessons such as “Liao, Western Xia and the Northern Song”, “The Jin and the Southern Song”, “The Song economy”, “Yuan rule”, “Song-Yuan science and foreign contact”.
china/song-yuan.faa4acff424e: Watertight compartments. If one compartment leaks, the ship stays afloat. Thick wooden bulkheads split the hull into separate, sealed compartments. If one compartment is holed and floods, water cannot spread to the others, so the ship can keep sailing. The bulkheads also brace the hull and make it stronger. The watertight-bulkhead technology of Chinese junks was inscribed by UNESCO in twenty ten as intangible cultural heritage in need of urgent safeguarding. Try the Flooding test!

china/spring-warring.cad894791fc9: Meanwhile, elsewhere: In Babylon, King Nebuchadnezzar the Second builds the Ishtar Gate, about five seventy-five B C E.
china/spring-warring.b49477ed263b: Meanwhile, elsewhere: Athens is in its golden age: the Parthenon is built from four forty-seven to four thirty-two B C E and Socrates is asking awkward questions.
china/spring-warring.5bb9b17f8d41: Meanwhile, elsewhere: The Buddha is teaching in India. Athens tries a new idea called democracy, five oh eight B C E. Persia rules from Egypt to India.
china/spring-warring.f166f5e87afd: The two halves of this age: seven hundred seventy to four hundred seventy-six B C E and four hundred seventy-five to two hundred twenty-one B C E. “Spring and Autumn” is the title of a history book; “Warring States” says exactly what it was.
china/spring-warring.6cfd71da63b8: Ideas: one, three D Dujiangyan: let students predict which river carries more water in each season, then test the “sixty over forty split” with the slider; switch on Sand and discuss why the Feisha Weir flushes sand by itself, showing how ancient builders worked with nature. Two, Step five of the animation links Shang Yang’s reforms to Qin’s unification, cause and effect.
china/spring-warring.267d84accd00: Meanwhile, elsewhere: Greece has just held its first Olympic Games, seven seventy-six B C E. Rome, the legend says, will be founded in seven fifty-three B C E.
china/spring-warring.8b19e9b60128: Meanwhile, elsewhere: Hannibal of Carthage is about to march his elephants over the Alps to attack Rome, two eighteen B C E.
china/spring-warring.d590039c7fda: Start with a two thousand two hundred-year-old water system that still works today, then drag the year slider and watch more than a hundred states shrink to seven, then to one.
china/spring-warring.cbdc3bb02279: Spring and Autumn seven seventy to four seventy-six B C E; Warring States four seventy-five to two twenty-one B C E.
china/spring-warring.3c879b084562: Three, Extension: the unit also covers iron farm tools and ox-ploughing; connect these to “private ownership of land” in the reforms.
china/spring-warring.ecfd85c40cae: Shang Yang’s reforms began in three fifty-six B C E under…
china/spring-warring.127887229e92: Meanwhile, elsewhere: Alexander the Great is born in three fifty-six B C E — the very same year. By three twenty-three B C E he has conquered an empire from Greece to India.
china/spring-warring.ecfa480257c6: Duke Huan of Qi hires a brilliant minister, Guan Zhong, 管仲, who reforms the state and builds a strong army; Duke Huan of Qi is 齐桓公 in Chinese. Under the slogan “honour the king, drive off the invaders”, Duke Huan becomes the first hegemon.
china/spring-warring.90364b5722ae: Literally “changing the laws”. States rewrote their rules to get stronger; the reforms of Shang Yang, 商鞅, in Qin went furthest.
china/spring-warring.c0df203e7ab5: In six thirty-two B C E Duke Wen of Jin beats the southern power Chu at Chengpu and becomes hegemon; Duke Wen of Jin is 晋文公 in Chinese. Later King Zhuang of Chu takes the title in turn; King Zhuang of Chu is 楚庄王 in Chinese. Small states get swallowed; big ones get bigger.
china/spring-warring.933b1d38aa15: From two hundred thirty to two hundred twenty-one B C E King Ying Zheng of Qin conquered the six states one by one — Han, Zhao, Wei, Chu, Yan, Qi — and in two hundred twenty-one B C E unified China. You will meet the Qin dynasty in the next unit.
china/spring-warring.672b3dc40487: In seven hundred seventy B C E King Ping moved east to Luoyi and the Eastern Zhou began. It has two parts: the Spring and Autumn period, seven hundred seventy to four hundred seventy-six B C E, and the Warring States period, four hundred seventy-five to two hundred twenty-one B C E.
china/spring-warring.2291d01f099f: In seven seventy B C E the Zhou king moves east to Luoyi. He is still called king, but more than a hundred lords now do as they please. This first half of the age is called the Spring and Autumn period.
china/spring-warring.a8696205e52b: From three fifty-six B C E Shang Yang rewrites Qin’s rules: land can be bought and sold; farmers who grow more grain are rewarded; soldiers earn rank and land by winning battles; the state is divided into counties run by the ruler’s officials. Shang Yang is 商鞅 in Chinese. Qin becomes the strongest state.
china/spring-warring.df6a5c6ebc53: In three hundred fifty-six B C E Duke Xiao of Qin backed Shang Yang’s reforms: private land could be bought and sold; farming and fighting were rewarded; ranks were given for military merit; counties were set up and run by officials sent by the ruler. Qin became the richest and strongest state of the late Warring States.
china/spring-warring.4b4d3ba11d01: What happens when a king is too weak to control his own lords? In China it meant five hundred fifty years of rivalry and war, seven hundred seventy to two hundred twenty-one B C E — and the greatest burst of new ideas in Chinese history. Confucius lived in this age, at about the same time as the Buddha in India and just before Socrates in Greece.
china/spring-warring.1013c7a3df5b: Confucius is born in Lu; Confucius, 孔子, lived from five fifty-one to four seventy-nine B C E. He teaches ren and opens his school to rich and poor alike; 仁 means caring about other people. Meanwhile the kings of Wu and Yue fight a famous feud; Yue finally destroys Wu.
china/spring-warring.b8cdf10d70a6: Meanwhile, elsewhere: Rome and Carthage are fighting their first great war, two sixty-four to two forty-one B C E. In India, Emperor Ashoka spreads Buddhism.
china/spring-warring.bde5d05738ab: Textbook: Unified edition, Chinese History, Grade seven Volume one, Unit two, lessons on the Spring and Autumn period, changes in the Warring States, and the Hundred Schools.
china/spring-warring.dc94314ffa31: An irrigation system built about two hundred fifty-six B C E that tames a river without a dam. It still waters farmland in Sichuan today.
china/spring-warring.b7ada54a3cc8: Time map: drag through five hundred fifty years
china/spring-warring.5ebbf8fca39b: In just ten years Qin conquers Han, Zhao, Wei, Chu, Yan and Qi, in that order, from two thirty to two twenty-one B C E. Drag slowly and watch each one turn grey.
china/spring-warring.dfcbe800c2bc: “the Land of Abundance”, 天府之国
china/spring-warring.678ea05eea9a: Timeline and schematic map: Duke Huan of Qi as hegemon, where the seven states were, Shang Yang’s reforms, Dujiangyan, and how Qin finally conquered the other six one by one.
china/spring-warring.62552b43ee71: About two hundred fifty-six B C E Li Bing, governor of Shu for the state of Qin, led the building of Dujiangyan on the Min River. The Chengdu Plain became “the Land of Abundance” — a rich rear base for Qin.
china/spring-warring.e681081690e2: In two sixty B C E Qin crushes Zhao’s army at Changping; no state can now stop Qin alone. About two fifty-six B C E, Qin’s governor Li Bing builds Dujiangyan, turning the Chengdu Plain into rich farmland — more grain for Qin; Li Bing is 李冰 in Chinese.
china/spring-warring.f78d0167685e: Drag the slider from seven hundred seventy B C E to two hundred twenty-one B C E. First meet the lords who became hegemon; then watch the seven Warring States, coloured areas, get swallowed by Qin one by one. Click any dot or coloured area. The seven states together covered very roughly as much land as the United States east of the Mississippi.
china/spring-warring.26789e13fdd1: In seven hundred seventy B C E the Zhou king moves east to Luoyi, today: Luoyang. He is still called king, but more than a hundred lords now do as they please. This first half of the age is called the Spring and Autumn period.
china/spring-warring.2425635343e9: Aligned with the twenty twenty-two Compulsory Education History Curriculum Standard, Ancient China, “Spring and Autumn and Warring States”, in summary: understand the social changes of the period, rivalry among the lords, Shang Yang’s reforms, et cetera. Know water projects such as Dujiangyan; learn about Laozi, Confucius and the Hundred Schools, and the flowering of thought.

china/strategy-battles.ea7adf026ff1: An L-shaped pit with four mixed units; roughly one thousand three hundred figures and eighty or more chariots, approximate.
china/strategy-battles.bb137e0ba4d0: Pins, 键. Bronze pins the parts turn on. Two pins go right through the housing and the stock.
china/strategy-battles.c5014d062819: Crossbow square, kneeling and standing. The front corner of Pit two. Kneeling crossbowmen in the middle, standing archers around them. One idea: one group shoots while the other reloads, so the arrows never stop. An L-shaped pit with four mixed units; roughly one thousand three hundred figures and eighty-plus chariots, approximate.
china/strategy-battles.f9124c109431: Armoured infantry. Filling the long corridors of Pit one. The main body of the army: thousands of soldiers in armour, in columns four wide. They carried long bronze weapons such as spears and halberds, 戈, 矛, 戟. About two hundred thirty meters times sixty-two meters, seven hundred fifty-five times two hundred three feet — longer than two US football fields. Estimated about six thousand clay soldiers and horses.
china/strategy-battles.6802e689e05d: Teeth, 牙. Two bronze hooks that catch and hold the string. When you cock the crossbow, the string is pulled back and locks behind the teeth. The teeth and the sight are one piece that turns on a bronze pin.
china/strategy-battles.58756f731d7c: Fei River, eighty-seven times ten thousand versus eight times ten thousand
china/strategy-battles.4bec9f1ea3d9: Don't mix up: A crossbow, 弩, is not just a bow, 弓: the trigger lets you hold the string drawn and aim calmly, so less strength and training are needed.
china/strategy-battles.1601a5afe1c5: Mission one: crack the Art of War
china/strategy-battles.774c5dd9f9d0: Battle of Guiling three hundred fifty-three B C
china/strategy-battles.d646a1f41d66: About two hundred figures in three rows face the enemy first.
china/strategy-battles.46613ccbd5d6: Mission four: inspect the Terracotta Army

china/strategy-battles.0398b1b55bbf: Zhou and allied tribes, King Wu, versus Shang, King Zhou 纣王

china/strategy-battles.eb435242e836: Mission two: you are the commander
china/strategy-battles.4fb0ee9e3cf9: 军无辎重则亡, 无粮食则亡. An army without supply wagons is lost; an army without food is lost.
china/strategy-battles.2800cdbc1ea5: 知彼知己, 百战不殆. Know the enemy and know yourself, and you will not be in danger in a hundred battles.
china/strategy-battles.30a03f5a818a: It is thought to be the headquarters that commanded the army in Pits one and two.
china/strategy-battles.de6695a237a3: The idioms “every tree and blade of grass looks like a soldier” and “the wind and the cranes” — in Chinese, 草木皆兵 and 风声鹤唳 — come from…
china/strategy-battles.2d32bef1308e: A small U-shaped pit with sixty-eight figures and one chariot: the command post.
china/strategy-battles.6785b47802e8: Vanguard: archers and crossbowmen. The three front rows at the east end of Pit one. About two hundred figures in three rows face the enemy first. Most wear battle robes but no armour — light and quick. Their job: shoot first, from long range. About two hundred thirty meters times sixty-two meters, seven hundred fifty-five times two hundred three feet — longer than two US football fields. Estimated about six thousand clay soldiers and horses.
china/strategy-battles.65a17b6742be: Muye, seventy times ten thousand versus four point eight times ten thousand
china/strategy-battles.8f8d00645c90: Zhou: three hundred chariots, three thousand elite guards, forty-five thousand armoured soldiers. Shang: “seven hundred thousand”, traditional figures, Records of the Grand Historian; the Shang number is surely exaggerated
china/strategy-battles.480d6407c73f: Former Qin: claimed “a million”; records list six hundred thousand or more foot and two hundred seventy thousand cavalry, but only part reached the battle. Eastern Jin: about eighty thousand, traditional figures
china/strategy-battles.266db87eca99: Which battle laid the foundation for the Three Kingdoms, 三国鼎立?
china/strategy-battles.7610f202bf4c: String, 弦. Pushes the bolt forward when released. A complete Qin crossbow found in the pits still had traces of a string thought to be made of animal tendon.
china/strategy-battles.cf38b87e9093: Eighty-seven minus eight equals seventy-nine, times ten thousand, the biggest gap. But remember: these are traditional, probably exaggerated numbers.
china/strategy-battles.c015f61262d8: Sun Quan and Liu Bei, 刘备, versus Cao Cao
china/strategy-battles.6f557e9068f3: In Pit one of the Terracotta Army, who stands in the three front rows?
china/strategy-battles.c1f350b9b781: The Art of War, “孙子兵法”, was written by Sun Wu, 孙武, a general at the end of the Spring and Autumn period — about two thousand five hundred years ago, older than the Roman Republic’s big wars. People around the world, sports coaches and business leaders too, still read it. Tap a card to see what it means and which battle used it.
china/strategy-battles.6338bdc2d922: Target one of three: a straw target one hundred fifty meters away, or one hundred sixty-four yards. Cock, load, set the sliders and fire!
china/strategy-battles.4ba7fd813d91: Stock, 臂. The wooden body with a groove for the bolt. The wood has rotted away in the pits; the bronze parts survived.
china/strategy-battles.a755c87a1510: Sources: traditional records, Records of the Grand Historian, Records of the Three Kingdoms, Book of Jin, and the unified-edition textbook Chinese History, Grade seven; numbers are traditional or approximate. No reliable figures survive for Guiling.
china/strategy-battles.6a87bec72a08: Don't mix up: “Borrowing arrows with straw boats” and Zhuge Liang “borrowing the east wind” come from the novel Romance of the Three Kingdoms, written over one thousand years later, not from the history book Records of the Three Kingdoms. The real fire attack at Chibi was carried out by Huang Gai, an officer under Zhou Yu.
china/strategy-battles.6fc6de6e596c: Don't mix up: The Terracotta Army pits are not the First Emperor’s tomb. They lie about one point five kilometers east of the tomb mound, which has never been opened. That distance is about one mile.
china/strategy-battles.a4cb4dc910ae: Trigger, 悬刀. The hanging “knife” you pull to shoot. A small pull on a long lever releases a huge force: that is leverage.
china/strategy-battles.d5fcf2af7862: the layout of Pit two and the “how it fights” drill, an interpretation. The commander’s choices are teaching scenarios. All maps are schematic and drawn on China’s standard map, shared slash chinamap dot J S; today’s province lines are only for orientation.
china/strategy-battles.6b88286dabb6: The Terracotta Army pits held hundreds of bronze crossbow triggers, 弩机. A crossbow can be drawn, held and aimed before you shoot — so an ordinary farmer-soldier could learn to hit hard and far quickly. Work the trigger step by step, then set the draw weight and angle to hit the straw target.
china/strategy-battles.731b13ee56ed: The front corner of Pit two
china/strategy-battles.05bb184204f2: Linzi. Today: Zibo, Shandong. One of the biggest cities in the world two thousand three hundred years ago — so crowded that “raising your sleeves makes shade”.
china/strategy-battles.1c486487abd5: Eastern Jin, Xie Shi, Xie Xuan, versus Former Qin, Fu Jian 苻坚
china/strategy-battles.2ce6f620f087: Only sixty-eight figures: guards lining the walls, facing each other, and one chariot.
china/strategy-battles.3f90ccfa7e78: At Guandu, two hundred A D, Cao Cao’s key move was…
china/strategy-battles.5a9fc498aebb: The idiom “besiege Wei to rescue Zhao” — in Chinese, 围魏救赵 — comes from the Battle of…
china/strategy-battles.9b2a9c5d56f7: Who wrote the Art of War, 孙子兵法?
china/strategy-battles.aace1eceede6: No. Sun Wu lived at the end of the Spring and Autumn period and wrote the Art of War. Sun Bin, 孙膑, lived in the Warring States period, about one hundred fifty years later — said to be his descendant — and came up with “besiege Wei to rescue Zhao”. In nineteen seventy-two bamboo books of both men’s military writings were dug up together in a Han tomb at Yinqueshan, Shandong Province.
china/strategy-battles.8b7ac12c9cc4: Bolt, 矢. A short arrow with a bronze three-sided head. Tens of thousands of bronze arrowheads have been found with the Terracotta Army.
china/strategy-battles.91d457dc4547: 避实而击虚. Avoid the enemy’s strong points; strike the weak ones.
china/strategy-battles.96af2de94d09: Yuan Shao: about one hundred thousand foot soldiers and ten thousand cavalry. Cao Cao: about twenty thousand or fewer, traditional figures, Records of the Three Kingdoms; Cao’s number is disputed
china/strategy-battles.b637a3ed17d9: It is from the chapter “Attack by Strategy”, 谋攻篇.
china/strategy-battles.eedfe7ebae14: Guandu, eleven times ten thousand versus two times ten thousand
china/strategy-battles.fd1033c6f075: You are King Wu of Zhou, 周武王.
china/strategy-battles.bc0a446eb6b8: About two hundred thirty meters times sixty-two meters, seven hundred fifty-five times two hundred three feet — longer than two US football fields. Estimated about six thousand clay soldiers and horses.
china/strategy-battles.f41c639caf3a: Sun Bin of Qi attacked Wei’s capital to make Wei leave Zhao, then beat the tired Wei army at Guiling, three fifty-three B C.
china/strategy-battles.2874328b452c: Command post. Pit three, the smallest pit. Only sixty-eight figures: guards lining the walls, facing each other, and one chariot. It is thought to be the headquarters that commanded the army in Pits one and two. A small U-shaped pit with sixty-eight figures and one chariot: the command post.
china/strategy-battles.df7a09f6cefc: Sight, 望山. The aiming blade — like the sight on a rifle. It sticks up when the crossbow is cocked. Line it up with the target. Some Han-dynasty sights even had a scale of marks for different distances.
china/strategy-battles.7346fb3fa9cb: Sunzi says: 不战而屈人之兵, 善之善者也. — The very best victory makes the enemy give up without a fight.
china/strategy-battles.70b115afa506: Earn stars in this lesson to climb. In ancient Chinese armies a 伍 was a squad of five and a 什 a squad of ten.
china/strategy-battles.e4d9bee8d30c: Bow, 弓. Stores energy when it bends. The harder the bow is to bend, the more energy it stores — and the faster the bolt flies.
china/strategy-battles.0e3865f717da: Housing, 郭. The bronze box that holds all the parts together. Archaeologists found Qin trigger parts made to very similar sizes — almost like standard spare parts.
china/strategy-battles.ccc8c5946492: Cao Cao: claimed “eight hundred thousand”; Zhou Yu estimated about two hundred thousand or more. Sun-Liu allies: about fifty thousand, traditional figures
china/strategy-battles.b64e5c333d67: Traditional army sizes, in units of ten thousand soldiers
china/strategy-battles.01527a204f04: Cao Cao versus Yuan Shao, 袁绍
china/strategy-battles.15031e770551: Both describe the panic of the defeated Former Qin army in three eighty-three.
china/strategy-battles.342fdcfb0769: Rear guard. The last rows at the west end, facing backwards. They guard the army’s back. About two hundred thirty meters times sixty-two meters, seven hundred fifty-five times two hundred three feet — longer than two US football fields. Estimated about six thousand clay soldiers and horses.
china/strategy-battles.95099d3f4e54: This is a cross-unit deep dive based on China’s History Curriculum Standard for Compulsory Education from twenty twenty-two and the unified-edition textbook Chinese History, Grade seven Volume one. Unit two covers the change from Xia to Shang to Zhou, the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods, and the Hundred Schools. Unit three covers the topic “Qin unifies China”. And Unit four covers the Three Kingdoms and the Eastern Jin and Southern Dynasties.
china/strategy-battles.b5ce61ecc66c: Battle of Chibi, Red Cliffs, two oh eight A D
china/strategy-battles.9156134c7970: Mission three: cock the Qin crossbow
china/strategy-battles.f9946ca9a014: Next to the First Emperor’s tomb, thousands of life-size clay soldiers stand in real battle order. Pit one is mostly infantry and chariots, with three rows of archers and crossbowmen in front. Click a block to see who stands there, and drag the time bar to see how such a formation could fight, one interpretation.
china/strategy-battles.e4a4ceb40f63: Battle of Muye circa ten forty-six B C
china/strategy-battles.f4586bf9d29d: Chibi, eighty times ten thousand versus five times ten thousand
china/strategy-battles.ccd9f03e6ec9: In about ten forty-six B C King Wu of Zhou defeated King Zhou of Shang at the Battle of…
china/strategy-battles.31add7b99dc2: Flank guards. The outer rows along the north and south sides. The outermost soldiers face outwards, so the army can’t be attacked from the side. About two hundred thirty meters times sixty-two meters, seven hundred fifty-five times two hundred three feet — longer than two US football fields. Estimated about six thousand clay soldiers and horses.
china/strategy-battles.e738582464ed: Memory hint: Pit one equals the main army, Pit two equals the mixed strike force, Pit three equals the headquarters.
china/strategy-battles.084eddb368cb: Battle of Muye. Circa ten forty-six B C. Muye, near today’s Xinxiang, Henan Province. Zhou and allied tribes, King Wu, versus Shang, King Zhou 纣王. Zhou wins. The Shang dynasty falls and the Western Zhou begins, with its capital at Haojing. 不战而屈人之兵, 善之善者也. The very best victory makes the enemy give up without a fight.

china/sui-tang.602f50c97013: Deck and stone railings. The road across, with carved railings. The bridge is about fifty metres long and about nine metres wide. Its stone railings are carved with dragons and other beasts — the bridge is a work of art as well as engineering. After about one thousand four hundred years of floods and earthquakes it still stands.
china/sui-tang.b3558234c29c: Its single main arch spans more than thirty-seven metres. The arch is a low, flat segment of a circle, so the deck slopes gently and carts can cross easily.
china/sui-tang.49b0f0308465: A man-made waterway over two thousand kilometers long linking north and south China, or one thousand two hundred fifty miles — the longest canal of the ancient world, more than three times as long as New York’s Erie Canal and one thousand two hundred years older.
china/sui-tang.9283ae88ea48: The Grand Canal reached Zhuojun in the north and blank in the south.
china/sui-tang.afbe67c90e0a: In six forty-one Princess Wencheng married Songtsen Gampo, ruler of Tubo, bringing Central Plains techniques and books with her and strengthening Han-Tibetan friendship. This was a link between peoples within China.
china/sui-tang.413261a0f221: Memory hook: twenty-eight rings side by side — easy to repair.
china/sui-tang.229202c7af57: Chang’an became an international metropolis and Tang poetry reached its peak: Li Bai is called the “Poet Immortal” and Du Fu the “Poet Sage”. The An-Shi Rebellion of seven fifty-five turned the Tang from prosperity to decline; the dynasty ended in nine oh seven.
china/sui-tang.88f7240f0285: Five eighty-one: Yang Jian, 杨坚, Emperor Wen of Sui, takes power in the north. Five eighty-nine: his armies conquer the south. After nearly four hundred years, China is one country again. To find able officials, the Sui begins choosing them by written examination.
china/sui-tang.b8a832f39be4: Twenty-eight parallel arch rings. How the main arch is built. Look under the arch: the main arch is made of twenty-eight separate arch rings laid side by side. If one ring is damaged it can be repaired on its own, without rebuilding the whole bridge.
china/sui-tang.da17f9c4faf9: Under Emperor Xuanzong the Tang is at its height; Emperor Xuanzong is 唐玄宗 in Chinese. New ploughs and water wheels raise harvests; Chang’an has about a million people and merchants from Persia, Arabia, Korea and Japan; Li Bai and Du Fu write poems still learned by heart today. At the end of seven fifty-three the blind monk Jianzhen reaches Japan on his sixth try, and enters Nara in seven fifty-four.
china/sui-tang.248b865bdfa5: Memory hook: Grand Canal “one, two, three, four, five”: one canal, two aims, north-south transport, firmer rule, three points, Zhuojun, today: Beijing, Luoyang, Yuhang, today: Hangzhou, four sections, Yongji, Tongji, Hangou, Jiangnan, five rivers, Hai, Yellow, Huai, Yangtze, Qiantang.
china/sui-tang.1984622e323b: The ageing emperor leaves government to favourites. In seven fifty-five the frontier general An Lushan, 安禄山, rebels in the north-east and captures Luoyang and Chang’an; the emperor flees. It takes eight years to end the war. Afterwards, regional generals keep their own armies and the court is never as strong again.
china/sui-tang.47d28747efdc: The kingdom of the ancestors of today’s Tibetans, on the high plateau to the west. A Tang princess married its king in six forty-one.
china/sui-tang.fe790dd6d04c: Aligned with the twenty twenty-two national History Curriculum Standard, compulsory education, ancient China: the prosperous and open Sui-Tang era; textbook: national unified edition, Grade seven Volume two, Unit one, Lessons one to five.
china/sui-tang.6419a0afd22d: Meanwhile, elsewhere: six twenty-two: Muhammad moves from Mecca to Medina — year one of the Islamic calendar. Within thirty years Arab armies have conquered Persia, today: Iran.
china/sui-tang.e65624937487: An eight-year civil war from seven fifty-five to seven sixty-three, started by the general An Lushan. The Tang survived it, but never fully recovered.
china/sui-tang.ce95565417e2: In the year seven fifty, what was the biggest city on Earth? Not Rome and not Constantinople, today: Istanbul: it was Chang’an, today: Xi’an, 长安, capital of Tang China, with about a million people, when Paris and London were small towns. The short Sui, 隋, dynasty reunited China, dug a canal longer than the drive from New York to Miami, and invented exams for government jobs.
china/sui-tang.de04936ae561: The Tang, 唐, which lasted almost three hundred years, built on that to create a golden age open to the world. Explore a one thousand four hundred-year-old bridge and the chessboard city of Chang’an, then drag the year slider to dig the canal yourself.
china/sui-tang.dc0ea199aa56: Suggestions: one, use the water slider and the solid versus open shoulder comparison so students explain the small arches themselves, lighter, less stone, more flood capacity; two, pair the Chang’an, today: Xi’an, model with Bai Juyi’s line comparing the city to a go board; three, after the canal game, have students recite the one, two, three, four, five mnemonic;
china/sui-tang.63fff1bafd75: Drag the slider from five eighty-one to nine oh seven C E. Go slowly through six oh five to six ten and watch the Grand Canal being dug, section by section; then follow the monk Xuanzang, Princess Wencheng and the monk Jianzhen on their journeys. Click any dot or coloured area. Only China’s modern outline is drawn; places in Japan, Korea and India are marked by position alone.
china/sui-tang.42e79c9c1af2: Meanwhile, elsewhere: In eight hundred Charlemagne is crowned emperor in Rome. Viking raiders have begun to attack Europe’s coasts.
china/sui-tang.53b33b7662ef: The bridge is about fifty metres long and about nine metres wide.
china/sui-tang.9025a4d9eeb3: Eight sixty-eight: a Buddhist text, the Diamond Sutra, is printed from carved wooden blocks — the oldest dated printed book in the world, almost six hundred years before Gutenberg. But the dynasty is dying: the huge Huang Chao uprising from eight seventy-five to eight eighty-four wrecks it, and in nine oh seven a general named Zhu Wen ends the Tang.
china/sui-tang.91d3994be2db: Meanwhile, elsewhere: In seven eleven a Muslim army crosses from Africa into Spain. In Mexico, the Maya city of Palenque builds a pyramid tomb for its king Pakal.
china/sui-tang.116de640b6b9: Main arch. One great, flat stone arch over the river. The Zhaozhou Bridge, Anji Bridge, in today’s Zhao County, Hebei, was designed and built under the direction of the Sui craftsman Li Chun. Its single main arch spans more than thirty-seven metres. The arch is a low, flat segment of a circle, so the deck slopes gently and carts can cross easily. It is the oldest surviving open-spandrel stone arch bridge in the world.
china/sui-tang.611d06f248f2: Meanwhile, elsewhere: six twenty-two: Muhammad moves from Mecca to Medina — year one of the Islamic calendar. Within thirty years Arab armies have conquered Persia.
china/sui-tang.db492cc89bb4: Sui tyranny led to uprisings and the Sui fell in six eighteen. That year Li Yuan founded the Tang with its capital at Chang’an. Emperor Taizong’s reign brought the “Reign of Zhenguan”; the early reign of Emperor Xuanzong brought the “Heyday of Kaiyuan”, the height of the Tang.
china/sui-tang.fc08d01d9239: The ageing emperor leaves government to favourites. In seven fifty-five the frontier general An Lushan, 安禄山, rebels in the north-east and captures Luoyang and Chang’an, today: Xi’an; the emperor flees. It takes eight years to end the war. Afterwards, regional generals keep their own armies and the court is never as strong again.
china/sui-tang.bce5e83f14dd: In six ninety Wu Zetian, 武则天, takes the throne herself — the only woman ever to rule China as emperor. She promotes talented officials through the examinations and keeps the country prosperous.
china/sui-tang.c67561201f40: About six twenty-nine the monk Xuanzang, 玄奘, sets out for India to study Buddhism where it began. He is away sixteen years and brings back hundreds of books. In six forty-one Princess Wencheng, 文成公主, travels to Tubo to marry its king, Songtsen Gampo, taking seeds, tools and craftsmen with her.
china/sui-tang.cd9105d9e0b0: From six oh five to six ten Emperor Yang, 隋炀帝, forces millions of people to dig a canal over two thousand kilometers long, or one thousand two hundred fifty miles, centred on Luoyang: north to Zhuojun, today’s Beijing, south to Yuhang, Hangzhou. Grain and soldiers can now move between north and south by boat. Drag slowly!
china/sui-tang.3ea8b2422f4d: Meanwhile, elsewhere: In England, an Anglo-Saxon king is buried in a ship full of treasure at Sutton Hoo, about six twenty-five.
china/sui-tang.6011f1b93d97: After about one thousand four hundred years of floods and earthquakes it still stands.
china/sui-tang.4e28d53374c8: Endless forced labour and three failed wars bring the Sui down; in six eighteen the Tang dynasty begins. Its second emperor, Taizong, 唐太宗, ruled six twenty-six to six forty-nine, cuts taxes, listens to criticism from his ministers and picks officials by merit. His reign, Zhenguan, is remembered as a model of good government.
china/sui-tang.1840d71386b1: In five eighty-one Yang Jian founded the Sui with its capital at Chang’an; he is Emperor Wen of Sui. In five eighty-nine Sui armies conquered the Chen in the south, ending a long period of division and reuniting north and south.
china/sui-tang.0f333a253543: A bridge still standing after one thousand four hundred years, the canal still carrying boats, the world’s oldest dated printed book, and the sound of a Tang-era lute. Click a photo to enlarge it; video and audio play only when you press play.
china/sui-tang.69bdadb8e0c5: Meanwhile, elsewhere: In seven thirty-two the Franks stop a Muslim army in France. Baghdad will be founded in seven sixty-two and soon rival Chang’an. Europe’s future emperor Charlemagne is born in the seven forties.
china/sui-tang.bddecbd58995: Four, stress in the sort game that Princess Wencheng’s marriage is relations between peoples, not foreign relations.
china/sui-tang.4c1360c4c848: Meanwhile, elsewhere: About six ten, in Mecca, Muhammad begins to preach: the beginning of Islam.
china/sui-tang.189ded263a84: Yang Jian founded the Sui in five eighty-one and reunified China in five eighty-nine.
china/sui-tang.292ceb5bf40a: Time map: drag through three hundred twenty-six years
china/sui-tang.2ac986e71560: A time of peace and plenty. The Tang had two famous ones, named after the emperors’ reign titles: Zhenguan, 贞观, the years six twenty-seven to six forty-nine, and Kaiyuan, 开元, the years seven thirteen to seven forty-one.
china/sui-tang.2744c8ebee8b: Government jobs won by passing written tests instead of by being born into the right family. Begun under the Sui, the system lasted about one thousand three hundred years, until nineteen oh five.
china/sui-tang.36f2dc975ea0: To improve north-south transport and strengthen control of the whole country, Emperor Yang of Sui began the Grand Canal in six oh five. Centred on Luoyang, it reached Zhuojun in the north and Yuhang in the south — over two thousand kilometers long.

china/taiwan-hkm.e659caca781b: Sun Moon Lake. Taiwan’s largest natural lake. Sun Moon Lake, 日月潭, lies in the central mountains, about seven hundred fifty meters above sea level, or two thousand four hundred fifty feet. Its northern part is round like the sun and its southern part curved like a crescent moon, hence the name. It is also a reservoir for hydropower, and home to the Thao people, 邵族 in Chinese. Round like the sun, curved like the moon.
