georgia/ga-revolution.fc382fa49a8c: Mission one: drag the years, seventeen sixty-three to eighteen oh seven
georgia/ga-revolution.ab61b848af8f: Britain won in seventeen sixty-three but owed a fortune — new taxes like the Stamp Act followed.
georgia/ga-revolution.d6151ee4901b: British troops captured Savannah on December twenty-ninth, seventeen seventy-eight, and held it until July seventeen eighty-two.
georgia/ga-revolution.b9a64eadf2db: March third: British troops rout a Patriot army at Brier Creek. Britain restores royal government in Georgia — the only rebel colony where that happens.
georgia/ga-revolution.cee6067e6d0f: Augusta. Changed hands again and again. The British occupied Augusta in early seventeen seventy-nine, left, and returned in seventeen eighty. Elijah Clarke attacked it in September seventeen eighty but had to retreat. On June fifth, seventeen eighty-one, Patriots under Pickens, Clarke and Henry Lee forced the British to surrender Augusta. Georgia’s government met here from seventeen eighty-six until the capital moved to Louisville in seventeen ninety-six.
georgia/ga-revolution.42a78ae373bb: The capital moves west again, onto land recently ceded by the Creek. It stays here until eighteen sixty-eight.
georgia/ga-revolution.25ac8685261b: Chartered on January twenty-seventh, seventeen eighty-five — the first state-chartered public university in the US. Baldwin wrote the charter: a new republic needs educated citizens. Classes began in Athens in eighteen oh one.
georgia/ga-revolution.86e6c34b24bd: The University of Georgia was… It was chartered in seventeen eighty-five.
georgia/ga-revolution.5b4fd3c4455b: Midway and Sunbury. Georgia’s most eager Patriots. Saint John’s Parish sent Dr. Lyman Hall to the Continental Congress in seventeen seventy-five, before the rest of Georgia joined. Lyman Hall and Button Gwinnett both had ties to this parish. At Fort Morris in Sunbury, November seventeen seventy-eight, Colonel John McIntosh answered a British demand to surrender: “Come and take it!” Liberty County, created in seventeen seventy-seven, got its name from the parish’s Patriot spirit.
georgia/ga-revolution.225e940b4f2b: Britain wins Florida from Spain; Georgia’s southern border moves to the Saint Marys River. The Proclamation of seventeen sixty-three bans settlement west of the Appalachians.
georgia/ga-revolution.97a8cf02c7d6: Wilkes County militia leader. Led a column at Kettle Creek in seventeen seventy-nine and helped retake Augusta in seventeen eighty-one. Clarke County is named for him.
georgia/ga-revolution.1aa2a2bd0586: Milledgeville. The capital keeps moving west. Laid out as the new capital in eighteen oh three on land recently ceded by the Creek. Named for Governor John Milledge. The legislature first met here in eighteen oh seven; it stayed the capital until eighteen sixty-eight, when Atlanta took over.
georgia/ga-revolution.c064e33cd5c7: the significance of Loyalists and Patriots, including the Battle of Kettle Creek and the Siege of Savannah; D, weaknesses of the Articles of Confederation and how they led to a new federal Constitution. Also touches S S eight H four A, reasons for the University of Georgia and the westward movement of the capitals.
georgia/ga-revolution.3bc2c16448cb: At Fort Morris in Sunbury, November seventeen seventy-eight, Colonel John McIntosh answered a British demand to surrender: “Come and take it!”
georgia/ga-revolution.a7caf1f2c3bc: Elijah Clarke attacked it in September seventeen eighty but had to retreat.
georgia/ga-revolution.f4f06b32e2e2: Louisville. A town built to be the capital. Planned as a new capital closer to the center of the settled land. Named for King Louis the Sixteenth of France, who had helped the Americans win the war. In seventeen ninety-six the papers of the Yazoo land sale were burned here in public.
georgia/ga-revolution.b985402a4fe8: What did the Proclamation of seventeen sixty-three do?
georgia/ga-revolution.3a1f4bbf8f1b: Harvard is older, having been founded in sixteen thirty-six, but it is private; UGA was the first chartered by a state.
georgia/ga-revolution.8cce9fa9ac30: In seventeen ninety-six the papers of the Yazoo land sale were burned here in public.
georgia/ga-revolution.a96a7a3dc40e: A one-house legislature held most of the power; the governor was chosen by the legislature for just one year. It created the first eight counties.
georgia/ga-revolution.d46fc8733d85: Siege of Savannah, October seventeen seventy-nine: British — about one hundred fifty-five casualties. Winner: British.
georgia/ga-revolution.8a9f64ebe9b4: Memory hint: Savannah: taken in seventeen seventy-eight, besieged in seventeen seventy-nine, freed in seventeen eighty-two.
georgia/ga-revolution.d86fbd55ad0c: Liberty County, created in seventeen seventy-seven, got its name from the parish’s Patriot spirit.
georgia/ga-revolution.4e1eedf7477c: Don’t mix up: Kettle Creek was a Patriot win, in February seventeen seventy-nine; the Siege of Savannah was a big French-and-Patriot loss, in October seventeen seventy-nine. “February win, October loss.”
georgia/ga-revolution.27f7433fa68e: Mission two: decode the Declaration of Independence
georgia/ga-revolution.080278695120: A young African American who fought as a Patriot artilleryman and was badly wounded at Kettle Creek. In seventeen eighty-six the legislature formally freed him for his service and later granted him land — very rare at the time.
georgia/ga-revolution.887fc943fa06: Boyd was mortally wounded; casualties were about twenty-one Patriots and one hundred fifteen Loyalists, estimates.
georgia/ga-revolution.b38ae9d1c8ae: From seventeen eighty-one the United States ran under the Articles of Confederation: strong states, a weak national government. Shays’ Rebellion in Massachusetts frightened leaders — it took place from seventeen eighty-six to seventeen eighty-seven. Click each weakness to see how the seventeen eighty-seven Constitution fixed it.
georgia/ga-revolution.1af0df34d99e: Liberty Boys met at Tondee’s Tavern in seventeen seventy-four to seventeen seventy-five to protest British laws.
georgia/ga-revolution.a6ac92b96829: July eleventh: British troops sail out of Savannah. Thousands of Loyalists — and people they enslaved — leave with them. Georgia confiscates leading Loyalists’ property.
georgia/ga-revolution.15e58783e1d7: Newspapers, legal papers, even playing cards needed a tax stamp. Georgia’s Liberty Boys protested — they were also called Sons of Liberty — yet Georgia was the only colony where stamps were actually sold, because Governor James Wright enforced the law. It was repealed in seventeen sixty-six.
georgia/ga-revolution.8717035b3b18: What happened at the Siege of Savannah in October seventeen seventy-nine?
georgia/ga-revolution.719f07ed1cf0: The Declaration of Independence was read aloud here on August tenth, seventeen seventy-six.
georgia/ga-revolution.2378077f463a: In Philadelphia, Abraham Baldwin and William Few sign the new US Constitution for Georgia. Baldwin’s July second vote helps keep the convention from breaking up.

math/angles.f603a0b4da57: Do the same inside a right angle. Now the two parts always add to ninety degrees. Two angles that add to ninety degrees are called complementary.

math/angles.db5517fb7189: One angle is enough! Here one angle is one hundred fifteen degrees. Its vertical angle is also one hundred fifteen degrees. Its neighbours on the line are — one hundred eighty degrees minus one hundred fifteen degrees equals sixty-five degrees — and the bottom crossing copies the top. All eight angles from one.
math/angles.35b315ba8d56: Split a straight angle with a ray. However the ray turns, the two angles always fill the half turn, so they add to one hundred eighty degrees. Two angles that add to one hundred eighty degrees are called supplementary.
math/angles.172d053641b5: Add to one hundred eighty degrees
math/angles.28ce977f3677: Common mix-up: Complementary angles add to ninety degrees, supplementary to one hundred eighty degrees, C comes before S, just as ninety comes before one hundred eighty. And corresponding or alternate interior angles are equal only when the two lines are parallel.
math/angles.23d81540a0db: Ninety degrees plus ninety degrees already uses all one hundred eighty degrees.
math/angles.0cce647d8a7e: Two lines cross and make four angles. Turn one line: the angles change, but opposite angles always match. Why? a plus b equals one hundred eighty degrees and b plus c equals one hundred eighty degrees, so a equals c. Opposite angles like these are vertical angles, and they are always equal.
math/angles.6e3e16aaad31: Drag the three corners. Below, the three angles are “torn off” and placed on a straight line. Whatever the shape, they always fill exactly one hundred eighty degrees.
math/angles.733aa2bb5f79: The “slide the crossing” in step five is the key idea behind corresponding angles: parallel lines point in exactly the same direction. Step eight proves the triangle sum with a parallel line through a vertex, reusing alternate interior angles. Have students tear the corners off a paper triangle to check.
math/angles.89c21083f168: When a skateboarder lands a “three sixty”, how much did they actually turn? An angle measures an amount of turn. Starting from that one idea you will see why vertical angles are equal, why parallel lines cut by a transversal make only two different angles, and why the angles of every triangle add up to one hundred eighty degrees.
math/angles.5d198ba8f742: Supplementary angles add to one hundred eighty degrees: one hundred eighty degrees minus sixty-five degrees equals one hundred fifteen degrees.
math/angles.d5b93c60a577: Three equal angles share one hundred eighty degrees: one hundred eighty degrees divided by three equals sixty degrees.
math/angles.0c9a3998f8df: The right angle uses ninety degrees, so the two acute angles are complementary: ninety degrees minus thirty-five degrees equals fifty-five degrees.
math/angles.9672b83d07a1: x plus two x equals one hundred eighty degrees, so three x equals one hundred eighty degrees and x equals sixty degrees.
math/angles.e453f235ccaa: Now a triangle. Its angles measure about sixty-three degrees, fifty-one degrees and sixty-six degrees. Tear off the three corners and put them side by side: together they make a straight line, one hundred eighty degrees.
math/angles.819018a460c3: No: the third angle would be zero degrees
math/angles.79b9af8bdbcf: Two lines cross. One angle is forty-seven degrees. What is the angle opposite it?

math/angles.0770a712f69f: The third angle is sixty-five degrees, and its exterior angle is one hundred eighty degrees minus sixty-five degrees equals one hundred fifteen degrees equals forty degrees plus seventy-five degrees.
math/angles.50a697148403: Complementary angles add to ninety degrees: ninety degrees minus twenty-eight degrees equals sixty-two degrees.
math/angles.05257fa9b8f5: Same-side interior angles add to one hundred eighty degrees: one hundred eighty degrees minus one hundred ten degrees equals seventy degrees.
math/angles.692c244171f7: Always equal, add to one hundred eighty degrees, or add to ninety degrees? Assume the lines are parallel where it matters.
math/angles.da9464bb3954: Supports Georgia seven dot G S R and eight dot G S R, grade seven: use complementary, supplementary, vertical and adjacent angle facts to write and solve equations; grade eight: triangle angle sum, exterior angles, and angles formed when parallel lines are cut by a transversal. math/angles.b10b37c71f16: Use it: a triangle has angles of forty-seven degrees and sixty-eight degrees. The third angle is — x equals one hundred eighty degrees minus forty-seven degrees minus sixty-eight degrees equals sixty-five degrees.

math/angles.1ace70b6077f: So all eight angles come in just two sizes. Matching corners are corresponding angles; the Z-shaped pair are alternate interior angles; both pairs are equal. Same-side interior angles add to one hundred eighty degrees. Tilt the transversal: it all stays true.

math/area.c55e9e580d66: Use the perpendicular height, not the slanted side: six times four equals twenty-four.
math/area.c65037c561bb: A triangle seems harder. The trick: take a second copy, turn it halfway around and attach it. Two identical triangles make a parallelogram with area b h, so one triangle has half: A equals one half times b h equals one half times five times three equals seven point five.
math/area.b462c12828a2: Now push the top sideways to make a parallelogram. Unit squares no longer fit neatly. The base is still five, and the height, measured straight up from the base, is still three, even though the slanted side got longer.
math/area.b092b5043579: A rectangle has area thirty-six and width four. How long is it?
math/area.8f02397d4568: Cut off the triangle on the left along the height line and slide it to the right. It fits exactly! The parallelogram becomes a five times three rectangle, so its area is also — A equals b h equals fifteen.
math/area.77b9f3587e42: A trapezoid has bases four and eight and height five. What is its area?
math/area.6b3e64f2ea82: Four rows of seven squares: seven times four equals twenty-eight. Twenty-two is the perimeter.
math/area.f180dfa42572: A parallelogram has base six, height four and slanted sides of length five. What is its area?
math/area.ebc1a693fd7b: Four times blank equals thirty-six, so the length is nine.

math/area.de63688b9a55: Worked example: a house-shaped pentagon. Split it into a six times three rectangle and a triangle with base six and height two. Area equals eighteen plus one half times six times two equals eighteen plus six equals twenty-four square units.
math/area.08c97a168bdd: One leg is the base and the other is the height: one half times six times eight equals twenty-four.
math/area.3f325f1033d5: A trapezoid has two parallel bases, b one and b two. Same trick: a turned copy makes a parallelogram whose base is b one plus b two. So the trapezoid is half of it: A equals one half times the quantity b one plus b two, times h, equals one half times the quantity two plus five, times three, equals ten point five.
math/area.e59db2295e79: Every formula came from the same idea: rearrange the shape into one you already know. Rectangles and parallelograms: b h. Triangles: half a parallelogram. Trapezoids: half a parallelogram with base b one plus b two.
math/area.9dbf6ab1ed6e: Supports Georgia six dot G S R, finding the area of triangles, special quadrilaterals and polygons by composing, decomposing and rearranging, and applying this to real problems. The lesson uses one idea throughout: turn the new shape into a known one, parallelogram, rectangle; two triangles or two trapezoids, a parallelogram.
math/area.164509406610: Why does the triangle formula have a one half?

math/area.3e277f5cb496: One half times eight times h equals twenty-four, so four h equals twenty-four and h equals six.
math/area.2917da3945b9: A rectangle is seven units long and four units wide. What is its area?
math/area.e8ee03485ea3: Common mix-up: The height is measured straight up, perpendicular to the base, not along the slanted side! And the triangle and trapezoid formulas both have a one half because each is half of a parallelogram.
math/area.d1765590cc1a: Step six is the key “aha”: same base, same height, same area. Have students predict whether the area changes before playing it. In Explore, slanting changes the perimeter but not the area, a good prompt for discussing the difference between the two.
math/area.584b83bf9fb0: Which gives you more pizza: one twelve-inch square pan, or two six-inch square pans? Area is the number of unit squares that cover a shape. Rectangles are easy to count. For everything else, cut, slide and turn the pieces into a shape you already know. Every area formula comes from a rearrangement like that.
math/area.114b7a0a07cc: One half times ten times six equals thirty: half of the sixty a parallelogram would have.
math/area.57dc991c1c4e: A right triangle has legs six centimeters and eight centimeters. What is its area?
math/area.91586d957797: Now slide the top corner left and right, parallel to the base. The triangle changes shape, even leaning outside its base, but the base and height stay the same, so the area never changes: still seven point five.
math/area.05d1e20bbaad: Area counts how many unit squares it takes to cover a shape. This rectangle has three rows of five squares, so its area is — five times three equals fifteen square units.

math/expressions.79640367fc1f: Let a blue bar stand for x and a small yellow square stand for one. Words turn into pictures, and pictures into expressions: “three more than a number” is x plus three; “triple a number” is three x, which means three times x.

math/expressions.12305199d7d6: Before step five, have students compute three times six mentally, then ask whether it can be split into two easier pieces. math/expressions.4a7e5b0bbb3e: Why can't x plus three be simplified to three x?
math/expressions.e7d75190c4e6: Common mix-up: three times the quantity x plus two is NOT three x plus two! The three multiplies every term inside, so it is three x plus six. And x plus three can't be combined into three x: a bar and a square are not like terms.
math/expressions.f69e6b3c7246: Which expression means "twice a number x, decreased by three"?

math/expressions.869868493dd2: Three friends each buy a movie ticket and a two-dollar drink. Can you write the total before you even know the ticket price? A letter is just a box that holds a number. Draw it as a tile, and combining like terms, the distributive property and factoring all become tile-arranging. You can see exactly why three times the quantity x plus two equals three x plus six.
math/expressions.3c831db3b5b8: Combine the x-bars: three x plus five x equals eight x. The two has a different shape, so it stays.
math/expressions.bae0cbcba2e1: A rectangle is four tall and x plus three wide. Its area is…

math/expressions.0aa2ce90e093: Once we know what is in the box, we can evaluate. If x equals four, every bar is really four squares long. Count: four, eight, twelve, then thirteen, fourteen. So three x plus two equals three times four plus two equals fourteen.
math/expressions.fcbf003102e5: Now an area picture. A rectangle three tall and six wide holds three times six equals eighteen squares. Cut it into two pieces, three times four equals twelve and three times two equals six: together still eighteen. So three times the quantity four plus two equals three times four plus three times two.
math/expressions.8cea90daaab8: Now replace the four with an unknown length x. The blue piece becomes three x-bars, area three x; the yellow piece is still six. So three times the quantity x plus two equals three x plus six, whatever x is.
math/expressions.86c94cfaa11d: Try x equals one: x plus three equals four but three x equals three. A bar and a square can't merge.
math/expressions.51aab55e4e51: Imagine a box holding some marbles. We don’t know how many, and the number could change: three, seven, twelve … So we give the box a name, a letter such as x. That letter is a variable.
math/expressions.da495d09b7b0: The GCF of six and fifteen is three: six x divided by three equals two x and fifteen divided by three equals five.
math/expressions.be84948185e2: Factoring runs it backwards. Take the tiles of four x plus eight and arrange them into a rectangle with identical rows. It is four tall and x plus two wide, so four x plus eight equals four times the quantity x plus two.
math/expressions.6240ebebfab4: Expressions that equal three times the quantity x plus two for every x go left; the rest go right. Tip: try x equals one and x equals two.
math/expressions.a52a77dd0a7f: Use the distributive property: six times forty-seven equals what?
math/expressions.2f4981031c48: Supports Georgia six dot P A R, using variables, writing expressions from words, evaluating, and generating equivalent expressions with properties of operations, including the distributive property and factoring out a common factor. math/expressions.b9114834844c: Worked example: simplify two times the quantity three x plus one, plus four x. Distribute the two: six x plus two plus four x. Combine like terms: ten x plus two. Check with x equals one: both forms give twelve.

math/expressions.55a177ef3454: Like terms are tiles with the same shape. In two x plus three plus x plus one, slide the bars together and the squares together: three x plus four. A bar and a square can never merge, because x and one are different sizes.

math/fractals.4d885d020d7e: Given an equilateral triangle with sides of three centimeters, find the perimeter after two iterations.

math/fractals.5dfcf2ff3939: Halve the side four times to get the quantity one half, all to the fourth power, equals one sixteenth.
math/fractals.f41fde2f6d7b: The smaller frond map is selected with probability eighty-five percent.

math/fraction-division.7fbee82ddb94: Steps five to seven give two explanations of the algorithm: common denominators then divide numerators, and “multiply by the denominator, divide by the numerator”, which together are multiplying by the reciprocal. In Explore, have students predict whether the quotient is more or less than one before checking.
math/fraction-division.45ea50af648d: Four pieces fit and one third is left. One third is half of a two-thirds piece, so four and a half.
math/fraction-division.f2d7200136c3: Division as measurement: how many pieces of size two fit into six? Three.
math/fraction-division.69cfa16b7025: Supports Georgia six dot N R, interpret and compute quotients of fractions with visual models and the standard algorithm. The lesson uses the measurement meaning of division: “How many groups fit?” Whole-number division first, then fraction bars that show why dividing by a proper fraction makes the answer bigger. Step four is the key idea: measure the leftover in pieces.
math/fraction-division.7bbd5faa88e9: Why does this work? Measure everything in the same unit, thirds. Three is nine over three and a piece is two over three. How many twos fit in nine? Nine over three, divided by two over three, equals nine divided by two equals four and a half. Same denominator, so just divide the numerators.
math/fraction-division.b32e3f856922: What is six more than two?
math/fraction-division.1236c617ae19: Quotient greater or less than one?
math/fraction-division.1f503070dbec: You divide a positive number by a fraction between zero and one. The answer is…
math/fraction-division.1f31de6aaf48: What if it does not fit evenly? In three divided by two thirds, four pieces fit and one third is left over. That leftover is half a piece, so the answer is four and a half, not four and a third.
math/fraction-division.099af96a0156: You have two and a half cups of rice; one serving is three quarters cup. How many servings?
math/fraction-division.dfd198933f2b: Which question does six divided by two answer, thinking of "fitting pieces"?
math/fraction-division.b7e1ab0115e0: Common mix-up: Measure the leftover in PIECES, not in wholes. In three divided by two thirds, four pieces fit and one third is left; that one third is half a piece, so the answer is four and a half, not four and a third. And flip only the divisor, the second fraction, never the first one!
math/fraction-division.6e351ca01625: A five-meter ribbon is cut into three-quarter-meter pieces. How many FULL pieces can you make?
math/fraction-division.3bf6089bfbd2: Now four divided by two thirds. First cut every whole into thirds: twelve thirds in all. Each yellow piece is two thirds long, so twelve divided by two equals six pieces fit.
math/fraction-division.c955c7f93ad0: Another way to see it: dividing by two over three is two moves. How many thirds? Multiply by three, so three becomes nine thirds. How many groups of two thirds? Divide by two. Together: times three over two, the reciprocal of two over three.
math/fraction-division.2d3b22653eda: Worked example: you have two and a half cups of rice and one serving is three quarters of a cup. Five over two, divided by three over four, equals five over two, times four over three, equals twenty over six equals three and a third: three full servings and a third of another.
math/fraction-division.94d35496709b: Pieces smaller than one fit more times than whole units do.
math/fraction-division.9b37935f6272: Same question with a fraction: four divided by one half, how many halves fit in four? Every whole holds two halves, so four wholes hold eight. Dividing by one half gives more, not less!
math/fraction-division.2ea9930ce2f5: five sixths equals ten twelfths, and ten twelfths divided by five twelfths equals two.
math/fraction-division.8dff238d5b06: Five divided by three quarters equals twenty over three equals six and two thirds, so six full pieces, with some ribbon left over.
math/fraction-division.e1f51a73ceef: What is six groups of two?
math/fraction-division.81f8fdd6862c: Dividing by four is multiplying by one quarter: two thirds times one quarter equals two twelfths equals one sixth.
math/fraction-division.928fd2f2200f: Keep the first fraction, flip only the divisor: seven eighths times five halves.
math/fraction-division.69a97ed241c3: How many sixes fit in two?
math/fraction-division.4f709bd64696: three quarters equals six eighths, and six eighths divided by one eighth equals six.
math/fraction-division.a46e59f053fc: Start with whole numbers. Six divided by two asks: how many twos fit in six? Lay pieces of length two under a bar of length six. Three fit, so six divided by two equals three.
math/fraction-division.52d6173445ba: four equals twelve thirds, and twelve thirds divided by two thirds equals six.
math/fraction-division.76c9ceb46c39: A cookie recipe needs three quarters of a cup of sugar, but the only scoop you can find is one quarter of a cup. How many scoops? “To divide by a fraction, multiply by its reciprocal” is usually memorized. But division only asks a simple question: how many pieces of this size fit? Watch the pieces being laid down one by one, and the rule will appear on its own.
math/fraction-division.5302cd9cec5a: one half times four over three equals four sixths equals two thirds. Less than one piece fits, so the answer is less than one.
math/fraction-division.ff0d1e7f8d24: five over two times four over three equals twenty over six equals three and one third servings: three full servings and one third of another.
math/fraction-division.e5585bccfc68: How many twos fit in six?
math/fraction-division.83f7b11840c1: There are two halves in every whole, so four wholes hold eight halves.
math/fraction-division.6ea600202035: When the piece is bigger than what you have, not even one piece fits. One half divided by three quarters: the half fills only two of the three quarters in a piece, so the answer is one half times four thirds equals two thirds of a piece.

math/functions.730aa9ece4fd: Now plot each input-output pair from our machine as a point, x, y. They line up! Inputs in between work too: “two point five maps to six” lands on the same line. The graph is a picture of the whole function.
math/functions.a738c6ac385e: Supports Georgia eight dot F G R, a function assigns exactly one output to each input; representing functions with tables, mapping diagrams, graphs and equations; linear versus nonlinear functions; describing a functional relationship from a graph and interpreting rate of change. Step four deliberately contrasts “one input, two outputs” with “two inputs, one output”, the most common misconception.
math/functions.5a26ff909b6e: You press B four on a vending machine and get chips. What if the same button sometimes gave you gum instead? A function is like a dependable machine: put in a number and it always gives back one definite result. We will look at the same function four ways, machine, table, mapping diagram and graph, and then learn to read “how fast things change” straight from a graph.
math/functions.8ec28d995bb5: Same table, y equals four, seven, ten, thirteen for x equals zero to three. Which equation fits?
math/functions.783ee11879ec: Compare y equals x squared. Its outputs zero, one, four, nine jump by plus one, plus three, plus five: the rate of change keeps growing, so the graph bends. That is a nonlinear function. Equal steps in x with equal jumps in y means linear.
math/functions.9092bbecd864: Name it: a function gives each input exactly one output. For y equals two x plus one, every step of one to the right goes up two: the rate of change is two, and the starting value, at x equals zero, is one. A constant rate makes a straight line: a linear function.
math/functions.d1bf389eb90f: A table: x equals zero, one, two, three and y equals four, seven, ten, thirteen. What is the rate of change?
math/functions.a14950c5e0c2: Not every rule is a function. "Give me a number whose square is x" sends four to both two and minus two: one input, two outputs, so it is NOT a function. But two inputs sharing one output, like negative two, all squared equals two squared equals four, is perfectly fine.
math/functions.6e1da518dc86: Common mix-up: Two different inputs sharing the same output is fine, two and minus two both square to four, and it is still a function. What is NOT allowed is one input with two or more different outputs.
math/functions.cf9db2f1e416: Meet a machine. Whatever number you drop in, it doubles it and then adds one. Drop in three… out comes seven.
math/functions.4c0240fece2a: Rate three, starting value four, the output at x equals zero.
math/functions.245662d11415: For the walking graph in step nine, have students tell the story aloud before playing it. The mystery rule in Explore works well in pairs: one feeds numbers, the other guesses.
math/functions.d370dff60d23: Time passes but distance stays the same: rate of change zero.
math/functions.ffb90a4c2b0c: The input two has two outputs, three and five.
math/functions.1374071b3e20: A taxi charges three dollars plus two dollars per mile. As a function, the cost for eight miles is…
math/functions.e7138db7d164: Worked example: a plant is three, five, seven, nine centimeters tall in weeks zero to three. It grows plus two centimeters each week, rate of change two, starting at three centimeters, so h equals two w plus three. In week ten: h equals two times ten plus three equals twenty-three centimeters.
math/functions.0e3b63b40ea0: Squaring makes the rate of change grow: one, three, five, … The graph is a curve.
math/functions.db1f0db0d366: For y equals three x minus two, what is the output when x equals four?
math/functions.7364f4ced4f4: For y equals two x plus five, which input gives the output seventeen?
math/functions.929a5d3cc671: y grows by three each time x grows by one.
math/functions.40e74d813bf2: Graphs tell stories. Here distance from home is a function of time: walking away, rising, stopped to chat, flat, rate zero, running, steeper equals faster, then walking home, falling, negative rate.

math/roots-irrationals.2d089ebea93a: Keep zooming: one point four one, then one point four one four, … Every zoom reveals one more digit, and it never stops: the square root of two equals one point four one four two one three five six and so on. Mean A equals eleven centimeters, mean B equals fifteen centimeters, and both have a mean absolute deviation, MAD, of one point four centimeters. The centers differ by four centimeters, almost three MADs, so the two piles overlap only a little: the fertilizer really seems to help.
math/sampling.694751fc72ce: Here is a jar of three hundred beads, some of them red. The whole jar is the population. What fraction is red? We could count every bead, but for a real population, every voter in a country, every fish in a lake, that is impossible.

Sample proportion: eighteen over fifty equals thirty-six percent. Estimate for the whole school: zero point three six times six hundred equals two hundred sixteen students. It is an estimate, not an exact count.
math/sampling.5a720098e09d: Group A has mean twenty, group B has mean twenty-six, and both MADs are two. What can you say?
math/sampling.8886bddc6a05: Repeat it forty times. Each dot is one random sample of twenty beads, placed at its percentage of red. The dots pile up into a hill: most samples land near the middle, but some are far off.
math/sampling.889b22dee633: Reveal the truth: ninety of the three hundred beads are red, exactly thirty percent. Both piles are centered near thirty percent. That is inference: the proportion in a random sample is a fair estimate of the proportion in the population.
math/sampling.92c27bdcf449: Two random samples from the same jar give thirty percent and forty-five percent red. Why?
math/sampling.56a65c0929ea: Many random samples give a dot plot centred at forty percent. The best estimate of the population percentage is…
math/sampling.2b42ea76b22f: The population is the whole group you want to learn about; the sixty are the sample.
math/sampling.0cdd43ae3799: A random sample of fifty cars has eight red cars. Estimate the number of red cars among two thousand cars.
math/sampling.1921c0984b0a: Twenty-six minus twenty equals six equals three times two. A gap of two MADs or more is usually meaningful.
math/sampling.d490c19f776d: But beware of bias. These red beads were poured in last and the jar was never shaken, so they sit near the top. Grab the twenty beads on top and seventeen are red: eighty-five percent! When not every bead has an equal chance, the sample is biased, and repeating it never fixes that.
math/sampling.75c42517ea2b: The means differ by three MADs: a real difference is likely
math/sampling.69818642aa9a: mean eight, MAD two point four

math/slope.433f6cae441f: Note that Chinese textbooks usually write y equals k x plus b, where k plays the role of m. In Explore, have students describe what happens as m passes from positive through zero to negative; the matching game practises finding slope from two points.
math/slope.68a77865613a: At x equals zero, y equals three times zero minus five equals minus five. That is the y-intercept b.
math/slope.6a88e19923f1: Start at a point on the line and walk to another one: three squares right, the run, then two squares up, the rise. We land back on the line.
math/slope.f55212ebce12: Where does the line start? It crosses the y-axis at the y-intercept b equals one. From there every three steps right add two, so y equals two over three, times x plus one. In general: y equals m x plus b
math/slope.83df4dda4333: If the line falls as you move right, the rise is negative, so the slope is negative. A horizontal line has rise zero, so m equals zero. A vertical line has run zero, and rise over zero is undefined.
math/slope.d0c815ab31b7: What is the slope of y equals minus four x plus seven?
math/slope.f1ad4c294017: A bigger slope makes a steeper line; a slope close to zero makes a flatter one. Watch the triangle stretch as m changes. Its run is two, and its rise is two m.
math/slope.11d111f2b729: Find the equation of the line through the point zero, four, and the point two, zero.
math/slope.7239a1bd26e0: Common mix-up: Slope is rise divided by run, vertical change divided by horizontal change, not the other way round. Subtract the y's and the x's in the same order. And keep these apart: a horizontal line has slope zero, but a vertical line's slope is undefined, you cannot divide by zero.
math/slope.a729bc8e170e: What is the slope of the line through the point two, one, and the point six, nine?
math/slope.2c427d63b07e: The run is zero, and we cannot divide by zero.
math/slope.6268fad8962c: m equals the quantity zero minus four over the quantity two minus zero, equals minus two and the line crosses the y-axis at four.
math/slope.198cb4719113: In y equals m x plus b, the number multiplying x is the slope.
math/slope.c4342967b738: The rate per mile is the slope, two; the starting fee is the intercept, three.
math/slope.8dec8fc7afcb: Supports Georgia seven dot P A R and eight dot F G R, the first on proportional relationships, unit rate, and the second on using similar triangles to explain why slope is the same between any two points; y equals m x plus b; finding slope and intercept from two points or a table. Steps three to four are the heart: ask students to predict whether the big and small triangles have the same rise over run before playing.
math/slope.7f787f74fb5d: That unchanging ratio is the slope, written m: m equals rise over run equals Delta y over Delta x equals y sub two minus y sub one, over x sub two minus x sub one. For our line m equals two over three: each one step right, it rises two over three.
math/slope.c952d836a528: Steepness depends on the size of m, ignoring the sign: the absolute value of minus five — equals five — is the biggest.
math/slope.ac8df8991c93: Drag the sliders. m sets the tilt, run one in green, rise m in orange; b sets where the line crosses the y-axis, the pink dot.
math/slope.5e2ede80ec01: Which is steeper, the wheelchair ramp at your school or a ski run? How do you put a number on “steep”? How steep is a line, exactly? Walk along it in little staircase steps and you will find that “rise divided by run” is the same for every step. That unchanging ratio is the slope, and together with a starting value it gives y equals m x plus b.
math/slope.f4d68686c726: Worked example: find the line through the point one comma three and the point three comma seven. Slope: m equals the quantity seven minus three, over the quantity three minus one, which equals four over two, which equals two. Put one point in: three equals two times one plus b, so b equals one. The line is y equals two x plus one.
math/slope.e342d82ab024: Do it again, and again. From anywhere on the line, three right and two up lands you back on the line. The staircase steps are all identical.
math/slope.9aac74940ed0: Rise — nine minus one equals eight. Run — six minus two equals four, so m equals eight over four equals two.
math/slope.d39787e3ebf3: Go three right and two up from zero, one: you reach three, three.

physics/heat-transfer.9a621cec41b6: Three. Time in the simulations is sped up; temperatures are illustrative.

physics/heat-transfer.f7adb9f28450: Radiation, glowing coil. Heat carried by electromagnetic waves. The red-hot coil gives off infrared radiation in all directions — hold your hand beside it, never on it, and you feel the warmth. Radiation needs no matter. That is how the Sun’s energy crosses one hundred fifty million kilometers of empty space to reach Earth. Dark, dull surfaces absorb radiation well; shiny, light surfaces reflect it.

physics/heat-transfer.9825f097fd48: Thermometer, temperature. Measures how hot or cold. Temperature measures the average kinetic energy of the particles in a substance. Faster particles equals higher temperature. Water boils at one hundred degrees Celsius and freezes at zero degrees Celsius, at sea level. The liquid in the thermometer expands when it warms up, so it rises up the tube.

physics/heat-transfer.e877e4afdd31: Steam, thermal energy. Energy of moving particles. Thermal energy is the total kinetic energy of all the particles in an object. As the water gains thermal energy its molecules move faster. The fastest ones escape from the surface as water vapour. When boiling, the extra energy breaks the water molecules apart from each other instead of raising the temperature, so boiling water stays at one hundred degrees Celsius.

physics/light.82d6f09929d0: Laser, light source. Makes a narrow, straight beam of light. Light is an electromagnetic wave. It needs no air or water to travel, so sunlight can cross empty space to reach us. In one material, light travels in straight lines. We draw these paths as rays with arrows. Light is the fastest thing in the universe: about three hundred thousand kilometers every second in a vacuum.
physics/light.d91b32b93c1c: Try this: in the Reflection scene, have students rotate the mirror and record angle i and angle r, then state the law of reflection themselves. physics/light.98c52a9d9b3c: When light meets matter it can be reflected — meaning bounce — refracted or transmitted — meaning pass through and bend — or absorbed, meaning turned into heat.
physics/light.6c1118cd0c9c: Common mix-up: Radio waves and X-rays are both “light” and travel at the same speed in a vacuum, about three hundred thousand kilometers per second; they are EM waves. Only their wavelength, frequency and energy differ. Radio waves are not sound waves!
physics/light.def788db9284: Normal line. An imaginary line at ninety degrees to the surface. The dashed yellow line is the normal. It is drawn wherever light hits a surface. The angle of incidence, i, and the angle of reflection or refraction, r, are measured from the normal. A ray that travels exactly along the normal does not bend when it enters glass.
physics/light.17afd7602a1b: Light ray. A model of the path light takes. The moving dots show the direction light travels. When light meets matter it can be reflected, bounce, refracted or transmitted, pass through and bend, or absorbed, turned into heat. physics/light.e510675c6232: Glass block. Refraction: light bends when its speed changes. Light slows from about three hundred thousand kilometers per second in air to about two hundred thousand kilometers per second in glass. Entering glass, fast, slow, the ray bends TOWARD the normal. Leaving, slow, fast, it bends AWAY. With parallel sides, the ray comes out parallel to the way it went in, just shifted sideways. If light inside glass hits the surface at a big angle, more than about forty-two degrees, it cannot escape: total internal reflection. Optical fibers use this.
physics/light.c93e7d7f20d7: Common mix-up: A convex lens does not always make things look bigger. When the object is far away, beyond two F, the image is real, upside down and smaller. That is how cameras and your own eyes work.

physics/sound.37b85e5a1e4e: Air molecules, the medium. Pass the vibration along. Sound is a mechanical wave: it needs a medium — a solid, liquid or gas — to travel through. Each molecule just jiggles back and forth around its place and bumps the next one. The molecules do not fly from the speaker to your ear. Sound travels faster in liquids and fastest in solids, because their particles are closer together: air about three hundred forty-three meters per second, water about one thousand four hundred eighty meters per second, steel about five thousand nine hundred sixty meters per second.
physics/sound.afa10631b7c8: An echo is a sound wave reflected back from a surface. The sound travels there AND back, so: distance equals speed times time divided by two. Bats, dolphins and ship sonar all measure distance this way.

physics/specific-heat.d58717832944: Temperature. A measure of how hot or cold something is. At a higher temperature, particles generally move more vigorously. Even particles in a solid keep vibrating. Internal energy, nèinéng. Add the energy from particles’ motion to the potential energy from their interactions to get the object’s internal energy. Internal energy depends on factors such as temperature, mass, and state. Ice has internal energy, too. Heat, rèliàng. Energy transferred because of a temperature difference, measured in joules, joules. The net transfer by heat is from higher to lower temperature. Molecules are always moving randomly. During diffusion, kuòsàn, 扩散, particles move in all directions, with an overall spread from higher to lower concentration. They keep moving after the gases are mixed. Molecules also exert forces on one another. At very close range they repel, and at somewhat greater distances attraction can hold them together.

physics/waves.6e7f3b4d0a0d: When a stadium crowd does “the wave”, the wave races around the stands. But does anyone leave their seat? A wave is a vibration that carries energy from place to place — without carrying the material along with it. Shake a three D rope, push a slinky and make ripples. Change the amplitude, wavelength and frequency and test speed equals frequency times wavelength for yourself.
physics/waves.685cf6d28c9b: The real thing. Ripples spreading out on water after a disturbance. The energy travels outward in rings, but the water itself mostly bobs up and down in place.
physics/waves.959260ce750e: The real thing. A toy spring like this is perfect for longitudinal waves: push one end and a squeezed-together section travels along the coils; that section is a compression.
physics/waves.0d5feec810fd: Bigger amplitude equals more energy. The energy grows with the amplitude squared: double A, four times the energy.
physics/waves.83152d9984c4: A wave has a frequency of four hertz and a wavelength of two meters. What is its speed?
physics/waves.32c4ff092d4e: Amplitude. How big the vibration is. Amplitude is the distance from the rest position to a crest, or to a trough. Bigger amplitude equals more energy. The energy grows with the amplitude squared: double A, four times the energy. For sound, larger amplitude means louder; for light, brighter; for water, taller waves.
physics/waves.a64c20d3298a: The real thing. A seismograph at Weston Observatory, Massachusetts, records earthquake waves. Bigger wiggles mean bigger amplitude and stronger shaking.
physics/waves.234521ec4985: The real thing. A computer simulation of a ripple tank: straight water waves hit a curved barrier and are brought together at one point, the focus.
physics/waves.cab8e196f10d: about three times ten to the eighth meters per second in a vacuum, three hundred thousand kilometers every second
physics/waves.39e38832a03d: Four, in the ripple tank, click bright and calm bands and compare path differences: whole wavelengths, constructive; odd half-wavelengths, destructive. Frequencies in three D are slowed down so they can be seen.
physics/waves.86ac08a33712: Classroom ideas: one, with “Same medium” ticked, have students raise the frequency and predict what happens to the wavelength. It shrinks; speed stays the same. Two, untick it and discuss: in real life, what sets a wave’s speed? The medium. Three, follow the red bead to correct the idea that water flows along with a wave.
physics/waves.f6f0ca8ae150: The real thing. A surfer in Santa Cruz, California. The wave carries energy toward the shore, and the surfer rides that energy.
physics/waves.aa525c2e8fd7: Vibrating source, frequency. Where every wave begins. Every wave starts with a vibration: a hand shaking a rope, a speaker cone, a pebble dropped in a pond. Frequency, f, is the number of complete waves made — or passing a point — each second. Unit: hertz, hertz. One hertz equals one wave per second. Period T equals one divided by f is the time for one complete wave. Wave speed v equals f times lambda.
physics/waves.e879c49bee6e: Set by the medium, for example, sound in air about three hundred forty-three meters per second
physics/waves.b5678866b9f2: Period — T equals one divided by f — is the time for one complete wave. Wave speed v equals f times lambda.
physics/waves.a6237fd85924: Frequency is the number of complete waves made — or passing a point — each second, with f as its symbol. Unit: hertz, H Z. One hertz equals one wave per second.

politics/china-world.634608aa3ce6: One hundred forty-two kilometers in Indonesia, trains at three hundred fifty kilometers per hour, opened October twenty twenty-three.
politics/china-world.13c7366b7e56: Medical teams abroad, Algeria, nineteen sixty-three. Doctors sent abroad for sixty years. China sent its first medical team to Algeria in nineteen sixty-three. Since then teams have worked in more than seventy countries, mostly in Africa, treating about two hundred ninety million patients, figure as of twenty twenty-three. During COVID nineteen China sent medical supplies and vaccines to many countries.
politics/china-world.3da6c6cd60df: China at the United Nations. A permanent member of the Security Council. In nineteen seventy-one the UN General Assembly restored the lawful seat of the People’s Republic of China. China is one of five permanent members of the Security Council and the second-largest payer of the UN budget. Textbook: China is a builder of world peace, a contributor to global development and a defender of international order.
politics/china-world.6cd182c1bdc0: Proposed by China in twenty thirteen, it revives the idea of the ancient Silk Road: building railways, ports and trade links together with other countries.
politics/china-world.a150133a4810: Xi’an. A stop on the “Belt”. Start of the ancient Silk Road, when it was the Han and Tang capital Chang’an. In one hundred thirty-eight B C E the envoy Zhang Qian set out west from here.
politics/china-world.d808457d741c: China-Laos Railway. From “land-locked” to “land-linked”. One thousand thirty-five kilometers from Kunming in China to Vientiane, capital of Laos; opened December twenty twenty-one. Laos has no coast. The railway gives it a fast link to ports and markets. It crosses mountains through one hundred sixty-seven tunnels.
politics/china-world.c685051a0fbf: The Belt and Road. One belt on land, one road at sea. Proposed by China in twenty thirteen, it revives the idea of the ancient Silk Road: building railways, ports and trade links together with other countries. More than one hundred fifty countries have signed cooperation documents. Click the dots, stops, and gold diamonds, China’s contributions. Use the switches and drag the year.
politics/china-world.a623e3e67646: Memory hook: Since nineteen sixty-three, doctors without a break.
politics/china-world.4756af748579: Quanzhou. A port on the “Road”. One of the world’s great ports in the Song and Yuan dynasties, a UNESCO World Heritage site since twenty twenty-one.
politics/china-world.5ccf5828129d: Jakarta-Bandung High-Speed Railway. Southeast Asia’s first high-speed line. One hundred forty-two kilometers in Indonesia, trains at three hundred fifty kilometers per hour, opened October twenty twenty-three. The trip between Jakarta and Bandung fell from over three hours to about forty minutes. Built jointly by Indonesian and Chinese companies using Chinese high-speed rail technology.
politics/china-world.1ce5cf719bec: More than one hundred fifty countries have signed cooperation documents.
politics/china-world.d2c7e75d0175: The trip between Jakarta and Bandung fell from over three hours to about forty minutes.
politics/china-world.1a6d023d082f: Mombasa-Nairobi Railway, Kenya. Kenya’s first new railway in a century. About four hundred eighty kilometers, built by a Chinese company and opened in twenty seventeen. It cut the trip from the port of Mombasa to the capital Nairobi from over ten hours to about five. Bridges and underpasses let giraffes and elephants cross the line in Tsavo National Park.
politics/china-world.93d6cbe0812a: Piraeus, Athens. A port on the “Road”. Greece’s main port. A Chinese shipping company has run its container terminals since two thousand nine and it became one of the Mediterranean’s busiest.
politics/china-world.70429ee632c5: “Compare with the US” cards are factual and say plainly where views differ — a good chance to compare sources. politics/china-world.7d359ae17105: Case one, The sneaker factory. Your uncle’s factory in Fujian makes sneakers for brands in Europe and America. This year a country far away raises its import taxes, and orders fall by a third.
politics/china-world.71786d918989: The Twenty-first-Century Maritime Silk Road, by sea
politics/china-world.8c970b375a65: Mombasa. A port on the “Road”. Kenya’s port. Zheng He’s fleet reached this coast in the fourteen hundreds; today a Chinese-built railway starts here.
politics/china-world.7d2ee002f50e: UN peacekeepers, South Sudan. The “blue helmets”. China first sent military observers to a UN mission in nineteen ninety; since then it has sent more than fifty thousand peacekeepers. Among the five permanent members of the UN Security Council, China sends the most peacekeepers; it is the second-largest payer of peacekeeping costs. In South Sudan, Chinese units protect civilians, build roads and run a hospital.
politics/china-world.6909077f8a74: Samarkand. A stop on the “Belt”. A two thousand seven hundred-year-old trading city in Uzbekistan, famous on the old Silk Road.
politics/china-world.a50a20920cb0: China-Europe freight trains. A “steel camel caravan” across Eurasia. The first train ran from Chongqing to Duisburg in twenty eleven, taking about sixteen days — far quicker than by sea. By twenty twenty-four more than one hundred thousand trains had run, linking over two hundred European cities. They carry electronics and cars west; wine, timber and machinery east.

politics/china-world.48a43568ab00: Almaty. A stop on the “Belt”. Largest city of Kazakhstan — the country where the “Silk Road Economic Belt” was first proposed in twenty thirteen.
politics/china-world.8b19376237a5: Venice. A stop on the “Belt”. Home of Marco Polo, who travelled to China in the twelve hundreds. On the schematic map the land and sea routes meet here.
politics/china-world.86fa22286a65: Guangzhou. A port on the “Road”. A trading port for over two thousand years, and still one of the busiest on Earth.

politics/development.c5028f940a93: Every industrial country has faced this trade-off. The US had deadly smog and a river that caught fire in the nineteen sixties before passing the Clean Air Act and Clean Water Act, in nineteen seventy and nineteen seventy-two, respectively. China met the same problem later and faster, with far more people.
politics/development.48a561c1e43a: Can a country get richer and cleaner and fairer at the same time — or does it have to choose? In about forty years China went from a poor country to the world’s second-largest economy, and paid a price in smoggy air and polluted rivers along the way. Today Chinese ninth-graders study three key words for what comes next: innovation, 创新, sharing, 共享, and green, 绿色.

politics/state-organs.88ecf4558f54: State Council. The State Council, that is, the Central People’s Government, is the executive body of the highest organ of state power and the highest administrative organ. Led by the Premier, 总理, under the “Premier responsibility system”. Runs the country’s administration: the economy, education, science, health, the environment and more. Makes administrative regulations in line with the Constitution and the laws. Local people’s governments are the local administrative organs; all of them are under the State Council’s unified leadership. Governments must act according to law, 依法行政.

At the centre is the National People’s Congress, 全国人民代表大会, NPC: Chinese students learn that the other organs are created by it, answer to it and are supervised by it. politics/state-organs.112e28a2f3ba: National People’s Congress. The National People’s Congress, NPC, is the highest organ of state power. Legislative power: amends the Constitution; makes and amends basic laws. Power to decide: approves national plans and budgets and other major matters. Power to appoint and remove: elects or decides on the top leaders of the other state organs — and can remove them. Power to supervise: watches over the Constitution and the work of the other organs. Its Standing Committee, 常务委员会, is its permanent body and works when the NPC is not in session. Local people’s congresses are the local organs of state power.

politics/state-system.c8e6fe43d7a1: Community-level self-governance. People in villages and city neighbourhoods run their own community affairs. Villagers’ committees, 村民委员会, and urban residents’ committees, 居民委员会, are self-governing organisations of local people. Residents elect the committee members directly. politics/state-system.37dc9712a422: Multi-party cooperation and political consultation. Led by the Communist Party of China, CPC; a basic political system of China. The CPC is the governing party. Eight other parties, “democratic parties”, are participating parties: they take part in state affairs. They work with the CPC as partners — the textbook calls them friendly parties, not opposition parties. Guiding principle: “long-term coexistence, mutual supervision, sincerity with each other, sharing weal and woe”. The Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference, 人民政协, CPPCC, is the main body for this cooperation: it consults, supervises democratically, and takes part in discussing state affairs.

Under the unified leadership of the state, areas where minority ethnic groups live in concentrated communities practise regional autonomy. China has fifty-six ethnic groups; the Constitution says all are equal. Autonomous areas come in three sizes: autonomous regions, prefectures and counties. The five autonomous regions are Inner Mongolia, Xinjiang, Guangxi, Ningxia and Tibet. Their people’s congresses and governments can make rules that fit local ethnic customs and culture. Every autonomous area is an inseparable part of the People’s Republic of China.

ushistory/us-civilrights.eb693f99d7a0: The Albany Movement. Nineteen sixty-one to nineteen sixty-two, Albany, Georgia. Students, churches and the NAACP in Albany, Georgia, protested segregation across the whole city at once — buses, parks, libraries, stores. Hundreds were arrested; Dr. King was jailed there too. The police chief avoided violent scenes, so the nation paid less attention. Albany did not win quick victories, but leaders learned to focus on one target — a lesson they used in Birmingham.
ushistory/us-civilrights.5bcb2ece19b0: The Birmingham Campaign. April to May nineteen sixty-three, Birmingham, Alabama. Birmingham was one of the most segregated cities in America. Protesters held marches and sit-ins, and boycotted downtown stores. Jailed for marching, King wrote the “Letter from Birmingham Jail”, explaining why people could not keep waiting for justice. In May, children and teenagers marched. Police used fire hoses and dogs on them. TV pictures shocked the nation; in June President Kennedy proposed a civil rights bill. In September a bomb at the Sixteenth Street Baptist Church killed four girls.

ushistory/us-civilrights.563b6a8e47e7: Selma to Montgomery. March nineteen sixty-five, Selma, Montgomery, Alabama. In Selma, only a tiny share of Black adults were allowed to register to vote. On the seventh of March, nineteen sixty-five, “Bloody Sunday”, state troopers attacked peaceful marchers, led by John Lewis and Hosea Williams, on the Edmund Pettus Bridge. ushistory/us-civilrights.3e0b8fb7f337: Six point seven percent in nineteen sixty-four, sixty-six point five percent by nineteen sixty-nine.

ushistory/us-civilwar.2e736a14f538: Sherman’s March to the Sea, Savannah. The fifteenth of November to the twenty-first of December, eighteen sixty-four, Georgia. Union campaign. The goal was to break the South’s ability — and will — to keep fighting. Thousands of enslaved people followed the army to freedom. Sherman telegraphed Lincoln, offering Savannah as a “Christmas gift”.
ushistory/us-civilwar.52b67568a4f0: Lee surrenders to Grant on April ninth. Five days later Lincoln is shot at Ford’s Theatre; he dies on April fifteenth. About six hundred twenty thousand to seven hundred fifty thousand soldiers died in the war, two-thirds of them from disease.
ushistory/us-civilwar.44894a151b61: Where did Robert E. Lee surrender to Ulysses S. Grant in April eighteen sixty-five?

ushistory/us-civilwar.5f45d8e399fe: The bloodiest single day in American history: about twenty-three thousand casualties.

ushistory/us-civilwar.a5ba11715858: Sherman captures Atlanta on September second — just in time to lift Northern spirits before the election.
ushistory/us-civilwar.25a938ef304a: Ford’s Theatre, Washington. The fourteenth of April, eighteen sixty-five. President Lincoln assassinated. Five days after Appomattox, actor John Wilkes Booth shot Lincoln at a play. Lincoln died the next morning. Vice President Andrew Johnson became president and led the first years of Reconstruction.
ushistory/us-civilwar.854e6cf77cb5: Fort Sumter. The twelfth to the thirteenth of April, eighteen sixty-one, South Carolina. Confederate victory — the war begins. ushistory/us-civilwar.b67e65eb2c86: The first former Confederate state to be readmitted, after accepting the fourteenth Amendment.

Before leaving, Union troops burned much of the city’s industry and railroads.
ushistory/us-civilwar.21ce54ba3156: Lincoln called for seventy-five thousand volunteers. Four more states then seceded — Virginia, Arkansas, North Carolina, Tennessee.
ushistory/us-civilwar.5cabf5547326: On December twentieth, South Carolina declares it is leaving the Union. Secession means a state claiming the right to quit the United States; secession in Chinese is 脱离联邦.

yuwen/yw-idioms.66878baa8d4d: A couplet, 对联, is a pair of lines that mirror each other: the same number of characters, matching word types and structure, and opposite tones. Tone rule of thumb: Mandarin first and second tones are “level”, 平, third and fourth are “oblique”, 仄. The first line usually ends on 仄, the second on 平. Characters marked 入 were “entering tones” in old Chinese and count as 仄.

yuwen/yw-modern-classics.1ed4af211d4e: 好一个安塞腰鼓. The recurring exclamation acts like a refrain. It allows each new description to rise from the same rhythmic point.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.391432a35380: 整个世界. The phrase enlarges what looks like an ordinary act of carrying. The adults feel the weight of caring for the older and younger generations together.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.5272da740869: 望. This verb directs the eye across a wide landscape. The later historical discussion inherits that expansive scale.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.98c2910beac0: 繁多. The word puts visible variety into the argument. Unity matters here because differences are still visible.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.159f20813662: 勤劳一生. The phrase sums up years of daily work. The essay shows how the mother’s habits shaped the choices her son made as an adult.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.a372ee28322f: Mao Dun wrote this wartime essay in nineteen forty-one. Its description of northern landscapes makes room for a tribute to people who resist hardship.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.26da0eae2315: A short story first published in nineteen twenty-five and later collected in Stories of Family Life. Its first-person narrator looks back on an accusation he wishes he could take back.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.97caadd9c74c: A memoir first printed in Mangyuan in nineteen twenty-six and collected in Dawn Blossoms Plucked at Dusk. The adult writer revisits the places where he grew up in Shaoxing, Zhejiang. A private study of this kind was a traditional school run by a tutor.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.65eeb41dd0da: The American poet first published this poem in The Atlantic in nineteen fifteen. It was later collected in Mountain Interval. The path in the poem is a visible object a reader can also interpret as a life decision.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.f1e373fad6a7: Written in nineteen thirty-eight during the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression. Ai Qing imagines a bird singing in a wounded landscape.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.0480987e0e26: Bian, a poet and translator, uses a compact four-line lyric to shift the point from which ordinary scenes are seen. The poem dates to nineteen thirty-five.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.c332a09ac53a: 淡黑的起伏的连山, 仿佛是踊跃的铁的兽脊似的. The dark, rolling ridges looked like the backs of iron beasts bounding away. The dark ridges look like backs leaping backward because the boat is moving swiftly. The moving image carries the children’s impatience to arrive.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.cf6a6d3f0126: An excerpt from Yang’s memoir of Shenzhou five, China’s first crewed space mission, in two thousand three. He records what he could observe and how he responded to uncertainty.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.7a7dc30081db: 三哼经. A-Chang’s own way of saying the title Shan Hai Jing. Her misremembered title marks how unfamiliar the book is to her. The gap between those few sounds and her successful search makes the gift startling.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.db5af59e3f3d: 依依. The repeated sound makes remembering feel lingering and affectionate. The same mood ties together episodes that otherwise happen at different times and places.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.de42dbf25dc9: First published in New Youth in nineteen nineteen and collected in Call to Arms. A tavern worker remembers a poor man who clings to the status of a scholar in the world of the old examination system.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.3a68d96310e8: National textbook platform: Grade nine, Volume one
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.7a05ee398119: Written during the war in nineteen forty-one. Duanmu writes of northeastern China as a homeland remembered in absence.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.d3d380ad4f51: 愧怍. The last word makes the narrator reexamine her own conduct. It opens a question about dignity and recognition beyond the value of the gift.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.fcf6f495db2e: 年轻舵手. The image joins responsibility to uncertainty. Having the steering role raises the stakes of the storm.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.7535b6c740eb: Lu Xun began studying medicine here in nineteen oh four. The memoir recounts both the support of his anatomy professor and the experiences that preceded his departure.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.c6787351c16c: This canal-country story uses nicknames and lively narration to evoke local storytelling. The revised textbook moves the excerpt from Grade nine, Volume two to Volume one.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.a5b13b747679: 其实地上本没有路; 走的人多了, 也便成了路. The ground has no trail at first. When enough people walk there, a trail takes shape. A trail is made by repeated footsteps. The metaphor makes hope depend on what people do together. The moonlit setting returns as the narrator imagines that future.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.f8da94ee0dda: 一丈青大娘. The nickname recalls a Water Margin heroine and prepares the reader for a vigorous, outspoken character before any description is complete.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.a4a3f68d4087: Grade nine, Volume one, Unit four
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.514cbd529487: Grade nine, Volume one, Unit one
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.d16ad57a8643: Educator Yu Yi recalls how books, teachers and familiar views shaped her as a reader. This is a recent addition to the Grade seven reading unit.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.ae658fda1dfd: Wen spoke in Kunming on July fifteenth, nineteen forty-six, at a memorial meeting for Li Gongpu. Different records preserve slightly different wordings.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.f31dbce5c073: 定然. The repeated word of certainty makes an imagined scene sound vividly present. It gives a wish the force of conviction.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.e5bf4fc3207d: Dai’s short elegy remembers the writer Xiao Hong, who died in Hong Kong in nineteen forty-two. 口占 refers to composing aloud on the spot.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.593475258c28: A short story first published in New Youth in May nineteen twenty-one, later collected in Call to Arms. A return to an ancestral home frames a story about childhood closeness and adult social distance.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.6d2cf2a8b098: Published in Literary Weekly on November twenty-second, nineteen twenty-five. In this memoir a son looks back on a farewell at Pukou, across the Yangtze from central Nanjing. His grandmother has died and his father has lost his position.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.fce243c0dfe8: Frost moved to England with his family in nineteen twelve and returned to the United States in nineteen fifteen, the year The Road Not Taken first appeared.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.6c501a792c78: First published in New Youth in January nineteen eighteen. Shen was teaching at Peking University and taking part in the New Culture movement. The poem uses conversational wording and line breaks typical of early experiments in modern verse.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.0005b253e5b6: 我永无改正我的过失的机会了! After the death, the cry marks a change from certainty about the cat’s guilt to certainty about the narrator’s own wrongdoing.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.07ff05fcdd9d: Published in nineteen twenty-two as 天上的市街 and collected in Starry Sky. Older volumes put it among the readings, while the revised Grade seven volume places it with the Unit six writing materials.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.3b3df96044b2: 手牵着手, 肩并着肩. The repetition gives cooperation a bodily form. As the forest grows more oppressive, the image keeps the “we” together.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.564920143348: Grade seven, Volume one, Unit five
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.e84604e4296b: 瀑布. The metaphor gives a hanging mass of flowers direction and movement. That motion prepares the passage from standing still to walking again.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.d0d401a6ce14: Grade seven, Volume one, Unit four
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.14bf7dbe8a34: 燎原. A light held in one hand broadens into fire spreading across open country. The expanding scale matches the essay’s growing public concern.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.62aaed2833a1: Grade seven, Volume one, Unit six
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.448f13fdc600: Without the ending there are two silhouettes. With it the speaker’s posture becomes a choice. The continuing “着” also keeps the whole scene in the present.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.04683aaf81b5: Grade seven, Volume one, Unit one
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.27778a5c82d7: Grade seven, Volume one, Unit three
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.5d8ef665d71c: 他的性格, 在我的眼里和心里是伟大的. The judgment is earned by small actions. The red corrections and the care shown to a foreign student give the abstract word “great” a concrete meaning.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.19c8636800ea: Grade seven, Volume one, Unit two
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.c32b82d744e2: 柔和之中只有宽厚绝无软弱. The sentence treats different water motions as different expressions of the same strength. The close observation of force and shape supports the judgment.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.3a989801bd9d: 明朗. A word often used for light describes a laugh. It gives the reader a sensory impression of warmth and openness.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.cfa8cb03446a: Mu Dan wrote this poem in nineteen thirty-eight. An opening scene of movement in nature grows into an imagined joining of human feeling and the world.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.cd8dc63ab8ad: 啊! 黄河! Direct address sets off successive sections and gives each a fresh surge of emphasis. The river becomes the figure the speaker can praise face to face.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.5ccd033bc1ae: 自由花. A living flower gives the abstract ideal of freedom a visible shape. The image sends the imagined result past the speaker’s own lifetime.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.bb406e311bd4: Grade eight, Volume two, Unit one
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.a89eea94e9cb: A nineteen twenty-six memoir from Dawn Blossoms Plucked at Dusk. In Sendai, Japan, Lu Xun studied medicine and met anatomy teacher Fujino Genkurō. The narrator recalls how the experience shaped his decision to leave medicine.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.f05f8ba223c0: 静谧. This word gives the autumn scene a mood as well as a sound level. Notice how that mood prepares the inward turn.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.394fb04f16f5: Grade eight, Volume two, Unit five

yuwen/yw-modern-classics.46ad929ef6e9: Grade eight, Volume two, Unit four
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.a3201a9f70d4: National textbook platform: Grade eight, Volume two
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.27c676225f42: Composed in nineteen thirty-six. This modern work uses a traditional ci tune pattern, so it is a bridge to the classical poetry lessons.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.78493b348301: First published in Tagore’s Bengali collection Shishu in nineteen oh three. Tagore published his own English version in The Crescent Moon in nineteen thirteen. A champa is a fragrant tree blossom.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.64c771174fd9: 无耻啊! An exclamation lets anger be heard in the speaker’s voice, while the neighboring questions demand that people judge what happened.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.004300e7e89d: 不必说……也不必说……单是…… The paired openings sweep across the garden. The turn to a single strip of wall zooms into what a child can hear, touch, and taste.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.95cb07f09f0c: 看风景. Repeated words keep the activity familiar while the viewer and the viewed switch places. That switch is the poem’s main event.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.d9f58d3585d1: This Russian lyric was written in eighteen twenty-five and appeared that year in Moscow Telegraph. It takes the form of an intimate address to someone having a difficult time.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.b9b63b4c6877: A memorial poem for Zhou Enlai. It appears in the revised Grade nine, Volume one poetry unit.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.1981decf0a5a: 心中的雨点. An image first seen outdoors comes to stand for worry and pain. The plant’s physical shelter suggests a kind of emotional shelter.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.6cba8cc9b0b2: Selected prose, stories, and poems from all six national textbook volumes, including international readings. Units follow the revised contents, with notes for supplementary readings from earlier editions. Yin Fu’s poem appears in the Grade nine, Volume two revision preview.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.0dbda4c9f77b: Zhu began teaching at Tsinghua in Beijing in nineteen twenty-five, the year the essay appeared. The station in the remembered scene is in Nanjing, across the Yangtze from the city center.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.b10372e4a3cf: 图画美. The phrase sets a test for the design examples. Ask how each example changes what can be seen from a particular viewpoint.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.62171d3a8224: an edible mushroom also written 鸡枞
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.4850fa144d15: Grade nine, Volume two, Unit two
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.bec05984bc4c: “厚障壁”, A thick wall between two people.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.4822fd278a5b: 泛滥. The word often describes water spilling beyond its banks. Applied to feeling, it lets homesickness seem too forceful to contain.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.7bb0e08af07b: A poem from the late nineteen seventies by Shu Ting, associated with the Misty Poets. A chain of objects links hardship, longing, and renewal.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.2d4f568ffa5d: 你在哪里? The recurring question gives a long search a stable rhythm and lets each reply take the reader to a new place.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.d219ea592bba: Grade nine, Volume two, Unit one
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.103756bdafb1: First published in Our Monthly in August nineteen twenty-eight under the name Ren Fu. The poem belongs to the writing of a young poet in Shanghai’s revolutionary literary circles. Listed in the revised Grade nine, Volume two preview.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.8205a1f59bec: The pivot word 却, “yet”, turns a nearby tree into a possible support the speaker does not use. Standing upright can suggest independence in a cold setting.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.dbeb79242617: A Russian prose poem published in the journal Life in April nineteen oh one. It is often read against the social unrest of late imperial Russia. Its central bird flies into a gathering storm.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.0278ad82ce5c: zero over eight matched, zero missed
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.192ed946c412: A Russian satirical story first published in the humor magazine Oskolki in eighteen eighty-four. A market dispute repeatedly tests a police officer’s supposed rules.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.1460707b8f95: 长夜漫漫. A long night gives duration to grief. The quiet tone leaves the reader room to feel the length rather than hear it explained.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.9a5775c6b9e7: 一枚小小的邮票. The object could fit on a fingertip. What matters is how much distance it must carry. Later objects build on that gap between size and feeling.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.1e5dca78be97: A French short story first printed in Le Gaulois on August seventh, eighteen eighty-three. A family living in Le Havre hopes its fortunes will improve once a relative comes home.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.394a984b9e57: 一滴水. The tiny first-person speaker can move through narrow channels. This choice organizes the entire view of the town from its water system outward.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.5b417a7105b4: Xiao Hong knew Lu Xun in Shanghai. She builds his portrait out of encounters and household details. Older textbooks place this excerpt in Grade seven, Volume two, Unit one.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.a67f764cb708: First published in nineteen thirty-four in Xuewen. The poem addresses an unnamed “you” through spring imagery. Proposed biographical identifications remain debated.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.c553fb5c9866: Grade seven, Volume two, Unit one
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.e6b82fa02d25: A short story first published in nineteen seventy-seven. Mountain travelers in southwest China try to find out who maintains a hut that shelters strangers.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.5eae959cff49: 台阶高, 屋主人的地位就相应高. The story makes a social measure literally visible as height. Later details test how much that visible status can change the father’s actual life.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.dda2813453a1: Grade seven, Volume two, Unit two
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.0aacddbc17a2: 大约孔乙己的确死了. “Probably” registers the limits of the bartender’s knowledge. “Certainly” gives the ending the force of a bleak conclusion about Kong’s injuries and isolation.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.e639c6fb0496: First printed in Fiction Monthly in December nineteen twenty-two and collected in Call to Arms. A grown narrator remembers a rural festival performance in a Jiangnan river village. “I” is the storyteller in a short story.
